<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2021-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2021-11 Park et al. v. Korean Central" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2021-11: Park et al. v. Korean Central, M50GA, pp. 797–809" data-search-text="2021-11 Park et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery Teaching elders challenged Korean Central Presbytery’s summary censure of a minister before an indictment was prepared. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s action because discipline preceded particular charges and a specific confession, and because an independent church lacked authority to impose PCA censure. It declared the underlying matter moot because the alleged event was twenty-one years old and the victim would not cooperate, ending the proceeding without remand. The ruling addressed neither the allegations’ merits nor all old charges categorically. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 30-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-3, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-20, BCO 34-6, BCO 34-7, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.3 censure without indictment BCO 32-3 disciplinary procedure sexual misconduct pastor-congregant mootness non-PCA discipline teaching elder discipline BCO 38-1 without process statute of limitations BCO 32-20 cooperating victim">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2021-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga50_2023__2021-11.html">Park et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2021-11">Teaching elders challenged Korean Central Presbytery’s summary censure of a minister before an indictment was prepared. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s action because discipline preceded particular charges and a specific confession, and because an independent church lacked authority to impose PCA censure. It declared the underlying matter moot because the alleged event was twenty-one years old and the victim would not cooperate, ending the proceeding without remand. The ruling addressed neither the allegations’ merits nor all old charges categorically.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2021-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2021-12" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2021-12 Michelson v. Northwest Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2021-12: Michelson v. Northwest Georgia, M49GA, pp. 836–839" data-search-text="2021-12 Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery The Michelsons’ complaint challenged a congregational meeting’s procedure for electing three assistant pastors as associate pastors—allegedly without a pulpit committee, ballots, counted abstentions, or protection for a substantial minority. The SJC dismissed it as not judicially in order: BCO 43-1 requires complaint against an act or decision of a court, but the complaint attacked congregational actions, while the Session’s only act was calling the meeting and was not objected to. The SJC noted other possible redress; the dissent found the Session’s call and recommendation justiciable. complaint Judicially out of order; Dismissed Not reached — BCO 43-1, BCO 43-10, BCO 20-2, BCO 20-4, BCO 20-5, BCO 24-1, BCO 25-5, BCO 13-9.b, BCO 13-9.f, BCO 13-9 complaint judicially out of order congregational meeting complaint against congregation vs. court pastoral call procedure pulpit committee associate pastor election justiciability BCO 43-1 act or decision of a court act of a court standing ballot requirements">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2021-12</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga49_2022__2021-12.html">Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2021-12">The Michelsons’ complaint challenged a congregational meeting’s procedure for electing three assistant pastors as associate pastors—allegedly without a pulpit committee, ballots, counted abstentions, or protection for a substantial minority. The SJC dismissed it as not judicially in order: BCO 43-1 requires complaint against an act or decision of a court, but the complaint attacked congregational actions, while the Session’s only act was calling the meeting and was not objected to. The SJC noted other possible redress; the dissent found the Session’s call and recommendation justiciable.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2021-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2021-13" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2021-13 Dudt v. Northwest Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2021-13: Dudt v. Northwest Georgia, M49GA, pp. 906–929" data-search-text="2021-13 Dudt v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session&#x27;s will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise. appeal Sustained; Not guilty Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) — BCO 29-1, BCO 29-3, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-5, BCO 31-7, BCO 31-8, BCO 31-10, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-16, BCO 32-18, BCO 32-19, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 42-3, BCO 42-4, BCO 42-5, BCO 42-6, BCO 42-8, BCO 27-4, BCO 24-7, BCO 14-7, BCO 15-3, BCO 20-2, BCO 30-1, BCO 39-3 ruling elder discipline email to congregation session authority over elders ordination vows subjection to brethren express vs. implied will of session ninth commandment burden of proof suspension from office notice of appeal bill of attainder Talley Resolution elder dissent BCO 39-3 appellate standard of review">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2021-13</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga49_2022__2021-13.html">Dudt v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Not guilty</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2021-13">A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session&#x27;s will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2021-13" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2021-15</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga50_2023__2021-15.html">Barber et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Other</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2021-15">Barber and others challenged Presbytery&#x27;s actions rescinding Herron&#x27;s contumacy judgment. The SJC answered their complaint by reference to its completed trial decision in 2022-10, which acquitted Herron on all seven charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to ministerial good standing. That decision found the lawsuit&#x27;s sinfulness unproved, undermining the related contumacy charge. The complaint notice supplied no separate issue-by-issue ruling.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2021-15" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2020-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2020-05 Speck v. Missouri" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2020-05: Speck v. Missouri, M49GA, pp. 840–878" data-search-text="2020-05 Speck v. Missouri Presbytery Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s approval of six theological judgments concerning teachings at Revoice 18, its rejection of his procedural point of order, and its refusal to debate gay-couple adoption. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2020-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga49_2022__2020-05.html">Speck v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2020-05">Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s approval of six theological judgments concerning teachings at Revoice 18, its rejection of his procedural point of order, and its refusal to debate gay-couple adoption. The SJC sustained only the first issue, particularly as to Judgments 2, 3, and 5: Presbytery improperly imported BCO 34-5’s ministerial-process standard into court review and then inadequately addressed identified errors affecting church peace and purity. It rejected the procedural and adoption claims and remanded for a focused new hearing under BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f).</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2020-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2020-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2020-06 Gordon v. Southern New England" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2020-06: Gordon v. Southern New England, M49GA, pp. 702–733" data-search-text="2020-06 Gordon v. Southern New England Presbytery A church member appealed Presbytery’s affirmance of his conviction and excommunication for failing to heed Session admonition and membership vows, including prolonged absence from that church. The SJC affirmed and denied the appeal, holding that all four specifications—lack of reasonable indulgence, haste, prejudice, and injustice—were nonspecific and unsupported. It emphasized his admissions that the charges were true, the adequate timeline, and the bar on considering evidence not offered at trial. A dissent disputed his PCA membership, standing, and the Session’s jurisdiction. appeal Denied Not stated legacy 2020-6 BCO 5-9, BCO 5-1, BCO 5-2, BCO 5-5, BCO 13-8, BCO 29-1, BCO 30-3, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 40-5, BCO 42-3, BCO 57-5, BCO 57-5.5, BCO 5-9.g, BCO 5-9.i church transfer between denominations OPC to PCA membership transfer excommunication jurisdiction membership vows failure to attend worship session authority limits">

Pacific Presbytery Pacific Presbytery allowed its Judicial Commission to read a six-page adverse report containing new assertions beyond TE Rankin Wilbourne&#x27;s agreed BCO 38-1 confession, then ruled his sins &quot;base and flagitious&quot; and deposed him. The SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the deposition, holding BCO 38-1 barred the prejudicial report and BCO 34-7 did not apply without a pending trial. It recommended treating the 17-month censure as sufficient definite suspension, restoring ministerial standing without call, and closing the matter; dissolution of his call was not annulled. complaint Sustained; Annulled Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2020-7 BCO 14-7, BCO 15-1, BCO 15-3, BCO 27-5, BCO 30-3, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-5, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-20, BCO 32-19, BCO 34-7, BCO 36-4, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 40-4 BCO 38-1 case without process deposition confession of guilt investigative commission procedure base and flagitious accused right to counsel BCO 31-2 investigation">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2020-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga49_2022__2020-09.html">Wilbourne v. Pacific Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2020-07">Pacific Presbytery allowed its Judicial Commission to read a six-page adverse report containing new assertions beyond TE Rankin Wilbourne&#x27;s agreed BCO 38-1 confession, then ruled his sins &quot;base and flagitious&quot; and deposed him. The SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the deposition, holding BCO 38-1 barred the prejudicial report and BCO 34-7 did not apply without a pending trial. It recommended treating the 17-month censure as sufficient definite suspension, restoring ministerial standing without call, and closing the matter; dissolution of his call was not annulled.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2020-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Pacific Presbytery The SJC sustained the complaint of TEs Gendall, Hightower, and Lien against Pacific Presbytery&#x27;s handling of a BCO 38-1 confession by TE Rankin Wilbourne. Presbytery had denied the complaint. The SJC held that reading a prejudicial six-page judicial-commission report before the agreed statement of facts violated BCO 38-1 and tainted the censure. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2020-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2020-09 Ozbalt and Barr v. Pacific" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2020-09: Ozbalt and Barr v. Pacific, M49GA, pp. 687–702" data-search-text="2020-09 Sean Ozbalt and Erin Barr v. Pacific Presbytery Pacific Crossroads Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s handling of a minister’s BCO 38-1 confession, particularly its hearing an adverse investigative report outside the agreed statement before imposing deposition. The SJC sustained Case 2020-09 by reference to its consolidated decision and annulled the deposition: BCO 38-1 permits censure to rest only on the mutually approved statement, not additional adverse material. It recommended treating the elapsed 17 months as definite suspension and closing the matter. The minister returned to good standing without call; dissolution of his call remained intact. complaint Sustained; Annulled Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2020-9 BCO 14-7, BCO 15-1, BCO 15-3, BCO 27-5, BCO 30-3, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-5, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-19, BCO 32-20, BCO 34-7, BCO 36-4, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 40-4 Judicial commission procedures Constitutional procedure violations Deposition and censure BCO 38-1 confession procedure">

<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2020-09">Pacific Crossroads Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s handling of a minister’s BCO 38-1 confession, particularly its hearing an adverse investigative report outside the agreed statement before imposing deposition. The SJC sustained Case 2020-09 by reference to its consolidated decision and annulled the deposition: BCO 38-1 permits censure to rest only on the mutually approved statement, not additional adverse material. It recommended treating the elapsed 17 months as definite suspension and closing the matter. The minister returned to good standing without call; dissolution of his call remained intact.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2020-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Savannah River, M49GA, p. 742" data-search-text="2020-10 Eagle v. Savannah River Presbytery A complaint was filed with the SJC before Savannah River Presbytery completed its hearing on it. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order as prematurely filed and did not reach the merits. It reset the complainant&#x27;s time to elevate the complaint so that timing begins on the later of notification of the SJC action or Presbytery&#x27;s ruling. The SJC adopted the decision by roll call. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached — BCO 38-3, BCO 43-3 administratively out of order premature filing complaint timing">

<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2020-10">A complaint was filed with the SJC before Savannah River Presbytery completed its hearing on it. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2020-12" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2020-12 Speck v. Missouri" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2020-12: Speck v. Missouri, M49GA, pp. 744–857" data-search-text="2020-12 Speck v. Missouri Presbytery Ryan Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its refusal to commence process against Greg Johnson on four allegations concerning same-sex attraction as sin, identity in Christ, sanctification, and fitness for office. The SJC denied the complaint in full. It found no clear procedural error and held that Johnson’s explanations and clarifications made Presbytery’s non-indictment judgments reasonable. No trial was ordered. The ruling neither adjudged Johnson guilty nor endorsed every statement or broader constitutional position concerning same-sex attraction. complaint Denied Not stated — BCO 11-3, BCO 11-4, BCO 13-9, BCO 31-2, BCO 40-5, BCO 41-1, BCO 43-10, BCO 15-3, BCO 34-1, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 31-3, BCO 31-9, BCO 35-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 43-6, BCO 14-7, BCO 38-3 Revoice conference homosexuality and identity same-sex attraction gay identity theological investigation strong presumption of guilt BCO 31-2 investigation Missouri Presbytery Memorial Presbyterian Church Greg Johnson sexual ethics Westminster Standards conformity Revoice Conference homosexuality identity in Christ sanctification above reproach qualification for eldership ordination standards sexual orientation concupiscence original sin Westminster Confession of Faith indictment complaint against non-indictment judgment of charity AIC Report on Human Sexuality">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2020-12</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga49_2022__2020-12.html">Speck v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2020-12">Ryan Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its refusal to commence process against Greg Johnson on four allegations concerning same-sex attraction as sin, identity in Christ, sanctification, and fitness for office. The SJC denied the complaint in full. It found no clear procedural error and held that Johnson’s explanations and clarifications made Presbytery’s non-indictment judgments reasonable. No trial was ordered. The ruling neither adjudged Johnson guilty nor endorsed every statement or broader constitutional position concerning same-sex attraction.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2020-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2020-13" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2020-13 Benyola v. Central Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2020-13: Benyola v. Central Florida, M48GA, p. 817" data-search-text="2020-13 Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery The SJC dismissed Peter Benyola&#x27;s complaint against Central Florida Presbytery as administratively out of order because he lacked standing to complain of the Presbytery&#x27;s action. Benyola was neither a teaching elder member of that Presbytery nor a ruling elder commissioner representing a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting when the Presbytery considered and denied the complaint. Citing prior SJC standing decisions, the Commission held the defect could not be cured and dismissed unanimously, 22-0-0, without reaching the merits. complaint Administratively out of order; Dismissed Not reached — None listed administratively out of order standing presbytery commissioner">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2020-13</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2020-13.html">Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2020-13">The SJC dismissed Peter Benyola&#x27;s complaint against Central Florida Presbytery as administratively out of order because he lacked standing to complain of the Presbytery&#x27;s action. Benyola was neither a teaching elder member of that Presbytery nor a ruling elder commissioner representing a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting when the Presbytery considered and denied the complaint. Citing prior SJC standing decisions, the Commission held the defect could not be cured and dismissed unanimously, 22-0-0, without reaching the merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2020-13" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

</div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-01 Dodson et al. v. Ohio" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-01: Dodson et al. v. Ohio, M48GA, pp. 649–667" data-search-text="2019-01 Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot. complaint Partially sustained; Moot Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2019-1 BCO 11-4, BCO 13-9, BCO 27-5, BCO 27-5.d, BCO 29-1, BCO 29-3, BCO 30-1, BCO 30-2, BCO 30-3, BCO 30-4, BCO 31-7, BCO 32-6, BCO 32-13, BCO 33-2, BCO 34-5, BCO 36-5, BCO 36-6, BCO 37-2, BCO 37-3, BCO 37-4, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 42-3, BCO 42-8, BCO 42-9, BCO 43-10, BCO 46-1, BCO 40-5, BCO 16-1 heresy Trinity partialism excommunication contumacy censures indefinite suspension order of censures BCO 27-5 BCO 30-4 personal offenses vs. general offenses lay member discipline evidence of contumacy">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-01.html">Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Moot</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-01">Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-02 Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-02: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia, M48GA, pp. 667–692" data-search-text="2019-02 Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2019-2 BCO 13-6, BCO 21-4, BCO 21-4.e, BCO 21-4.f, BCO 31-2, BCO 35-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 40-3, BCO 40-4, BCO 40-5, BCO 34-5, BCO 56-4, BCO 27-5.b, BCO 12-5, BCO 56-4.h, BCO 27-4 ministerial exam transfer from another denomination stated differences WCF 1.1 continuationism cessationism prophecy tongues spiritual gifts RAO 16-3.e.5 BCO 21-4 fundamentals of the system of doctrine">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-02.html">Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-02">The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-03 Crouse v. Northwest Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-03: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia, M48GA, pp. 692–700" data-search-text="2019-03 Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination &#x27;vetting&#x27; removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1&#x27;s sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session&#x27;s sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision. complaint Sustained Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2019-3 BCO 24-1, BCO 24-6, BCO 39-3, BCO 14-7, BCO 3-2, BCO 31-2, BCO 32-2, BCO 29-1, BCO 29-3, BCO 31-7, BCO 32-3, BCO 31-5, BCO 32-16, BCO 32-19, BCO 31-8, BCO 27-4, BCO 32-18, BCO 42-3, BCO 42-6, BCO 30-1, BCO 36-5, BCO 42-5, BCO 35-13, BCO 42-4, BCO 42-8, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 20-2 officer nomination process ruling elder election session prescreening nominees mandatory sequence BCO 24-1 divorce and church office session discretion">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-03.html">Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-03">A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination &#x27;vetting&#x27; removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1&#x27;s sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session&#x27;s sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-04 Williams v. Chesapeake" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-04: Williams v. Chesapeake, M48GA, pp. 756–761" data-search-text="2019-04 Williams v. Chesapeake Presbytery An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 2019-4 BCO 31-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 38-1, BCO 15-3, BCO 21-5, BCO 29-4 case of process vs case without process guilty plea BCO 38-1 confession indictment due process BCO 32 vs BCO 38-1 conflation teaching elder discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-04.html">Williams v. Chesapeake Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-04">An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-05 Goggan v. Missouri" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-05: Goggan v. Missouri, M48GA, pp. 762–765" data-search-text="2019-05 Goggan v. Missouri Presbytery An excommunicated member appealed the Missouri Presbytery judicial commission&#x27;s guilty verdict and excommunication, alleging specifications of error. The SJC denied the appeal and did not sustain any specification, holding only that the appellant failed to demonstrate sufficient reason to sustain the alleged errors; the excommunication thus remained in effect. The record noted Presbytery dismissed the commission without the BCO 15-3 vote to approve its report, but the adopted reasoning gave no further explanation and did not address that fact. appeal Denied Not stated legacy 2019-5 BCO 15-3, BCO 27-5, BCO 27-5.c church discipline excommunication member discipline judicial commission appeal BCO 15-3 approval of commission judgment">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-05</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-05.html">Goggan v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-05">An excommunicated member appealed the Missouri Presbytery judicial commission&#x27;s guilty verdict and excommunication, alleging specifications of error. The SJC denied the appeal and did not sustain any specification, holding only that the appellant failed to demonstrate sufficient reason to sustain the alleged errors; the excommunication thus remained in effect. The record noted Presbytery dismissed the commission without the BCO 15-3 vote to approve its report, but the adopted reasoning gave no further explanation and did not address that fact.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-06 Presbyterian Church in America v. of the Mississippi Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-06: Presbyterian Church in America v. of the Mississippi Valley, M48GA, pp. 701–719" data-search-text="2019-06 Presbyterian Church in America v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley In a BCO 40-5 matter, the SJC held that a presbytery erred in upholding a session&#x27;s erasure of a member who pled not guilty to failing to submit and pursued divorce. The session wrongly equated declining divorce counsel with refusing submission, failed to assess membership duties in another branch, failed to notify her of erasure, and proceeded without process after dropping charges. The SJC sustained the challenge, directed the session to note the notice failure and remove her under BCO 38-3(a), but ordered no express reversal. bco_40_5_matter Sustained BCO 40-5 — important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceeding; Independent review (constitutional interpretation) legacy 2019-6 BCO 38-4, BCO 38-3, BCO 40-5, BCO 57-5, BCO 31-2, BCO 57-5.5, BCO 38-3.a BCO 40-5 report erasure from membership roll BCO 38-4 case without process divorce and church discipline not guilty plea membership vows notification of erasure grossly unconstitutional proceeding session discipline">

Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-06">In a BCO 40-5 matter, the SJC held that a presbytery erred in upholding a session&#x27;s erasure of a member who pled not guilty to failing to submit and pursued divorce. The session wrongly equated declining divorce counsel with refusing submission, failed to assess membership duties in another branch, failed to notify her of erasure, and proceeded without process after dropping charges. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-07 Fozard v. North Texas" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-07: Fozard v. North Texas, M48GA, pp. 719–729" data-search-text="2019-07 Fozard v. North Texas Presbytery At issue was whether North Texas Presbytery wrongly denied a complaint challenging Fort Worth Presbyterian Church’s “Special Case Felons” integration policy as contrary to Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the complainant did not show the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution and that BCO 39-3.3 required deference absent clear error, leaving the lower-court actions in effect. The decision, adopted 20-1, expressly did not endorse the Respondents’ Preliminary Principles arguments; a concurrence disclaimed approval of the policy, and one member dissented. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2019-7 BCO 11-2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 57-5, BCO 11-3, BCO 11-4, BCO 42-9, BCO 43-10, BCO 30-1, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 39-3 special case felons sex offenders in church session policy corporate worship attendance terms of communion Preliminary Principles 1 and 2 rights of conscience deference to lower court criminal justice ministry church membership restrictions">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-07.html">Fozard v. North Texas Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-07">At issue was whether North Texas Presbytery wrongly denied a complaint challenging Fort Worth Presbyterian Church’s “Special Case Felons” integration policy as contrary to Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the complainant did not show the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution and that BCO 39-3.3 required deference absent clear error, leaving the lower-court actions in effect. The decision, adopted 20-1, expressly did not endorse the Respondents’ Preliminary Principles arguments; a concurrence disclaimed approval of the policy, and one member dissented.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-08 Ganzel v. Central Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-08: Ganzel v. Central Florida, M48GA, pp. 729–751" data-search-text="2019-08 Ganzel v. Central Florida Presbytery A minister appealed a judgment finding him guilty on most charges and imposing six months’ suspension. The SJC held BCO 32-20 barred Specifications 1, 2, and 4 because Presbytery lacked extraordinary justification for prosecuting old allegations, but did not bar ongoing Specification 3. It separately found the entire process constitutionally flawed and prejudicial. The SJC reversed the whole censure, declined Presbytery’s requested harsher sentence, and concluded the matter. A concurrence disputed the majority’s BCO 32-20 interpretation while agreeing with the result. appeal Sustained Not stated legacy 2019-8 BCO 32-20, BCO 31-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-5, BCO 32-7, BCO 32-8, BCO 32-2, BCO 15-3, BCO 15-1, BCO 36-3, BCO 36-4, BCO 34-6, BCO 42-3, BCO 42-9, BCO 43-2, BCO 40-3, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 30-3 statute of limitations BCO 32-20 scandal abuse of spiritual authority pastoral leadership disciplinary process double jeopardy judicial commission indictment specificity record-keeping definite suspension case without process reconciliation">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-08</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-08.html">Ganzel v. Central Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-08">A minister appealed a judgment finding him guilty on most charges and imposing six months’ suspension. The SJC held BCO 32-20 barred Specifications 1, 2, and 4 because Presbytery lacked extraordinary justification for prosecuting old allegations, but did not bar ongoing Specification 3. It separately found the entire process constitutionally flawed and prejudicial. The SJC reversed the whole censure, declined Presbytery’s requested harsher sentence, and concluded the matter. A concurrence disputed the majority’s BCO 32-20 interpretation while agreeing with the result.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-09 Mueller v. South Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-09: Mueller v. South Florida, M48GA, pp. 766–771" data-search-text="2019-09 Mueller v. South Florida Presbytery On complaint by RE William F. Mueller, the SJC reviewed whether the Redlands Community Church Session erred on January 14, 2019 by allegedly reaffirming its practice of fencing the Lord&#x27;s Table contrary to BCO 58-4. The SJC denied the complaint: the only relevant motion failed for lack of a second, so the Session took no action and did not reaffirm anything. It noted the case could have been ruled out of order earlier and that Mueller could pursue relief under BCO 40-5; a concurrence stressed BCO 58-4 remains binding and criticized Presbytery&#x27;s handling. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 2019-9 BCO 58-4, BCO 43-6, BCO 43-8, BCO 43-9, BCO 40-5 fencing the Lord&#x27;s Table Lord&#x27;s Supper BCO 58-4 communicants in good standing complaint standing session action">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-09.html">Mueller v. South Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-09">On complaint by RE William F. Mueller, the SJC reviewed whether the Redlands Community Church Session erred on January 14, 2019 by allegedly reaffirming its practice of fencing the Lord&#x27;s Table contrary to BCO 58-4. The SJC denied the complaint: the only relevant motion failed for lack of a second, so the Session took no action and did not reaffirm anything. It noted the case could have been ruled out of order earlier and that Mueller could pursue relief under BCO 40-5; a concurrence stressed BCO 58-4 remains binding and criticized Presbytery&#x27;s handling.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-10 Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-10: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona, M48GA, pp. 771–787" data-search-text="2019-10 Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. But the provision does not expressly require a meeting or detailed discussion. The underlying matter remained unresolved: Presbytery could proceed with or without process, or dismiss it. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 38-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 30-1, BCO 30-3, BCO 34-9, BCO 35-1, BCO 42-2, BCO 31-7, BCO 32-3, BCO 31-10, BCO 42-6, BCO 15-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 43-10, BCO 34-10, BCO 42-9, BCO 32-19 case without process BCO 38-1 confession statement of facts approval deposition from office investigative committee report self-incrimination teaching elder discipline confession procedures">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-11 Crouse v. Northwest Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-11: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia, M48GA, pp. 787–796" data-search-text="2019-11 Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery A complaint challenging a session&#x27;s refusal to advance an ordained deacon&#x27;s nomination for re-election to the diaconate was denied by the SJC. Northwest Georgia Presbytery had adopted its judicial commission&#x27;s judgment that the session did not err; applying BCO 39-3(3)&#x27;s deference to discretionary judgments, the SJC found no clear error, held formal charges were unnecessary and re-election was not guaranteed, and refused to attribute one elder&#x27;s questionable retaliation rationale to the session. The majority encouraged prompt communication of reasons. A dissent would apply BCO 39-3.4 and sustain. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 24-1, BCO 24-7, BCO 29-1, BCO 29-2, BCO 32-18, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 9-3 deacon re-election eligibility for office session discretion de facto deposition retaliation for complaint standard of review BCO 39-3 deference right to file complaint officer nomination candidate eligibility">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2019-13" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2019-13 Gendy v. Central Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2019-13: Gendy v. Central Florida, M48GA, pp. 796–800" data-search-text="2019-13 Gendy v. Central Florida Presbytery A member removed from the rolls under BCO 38-4 challenged Presbytery&#x27;s ruling that she lacked standing to complain because she was no longer a member. The SJC sustained the complaint: standing under BCO 43-1 cannot be defeated by the very removal challenged. Removal under BCO 38-4 is pastoral discipline, a disciplinary case, not a merely administrative act. The SJC remanded to Presbytery to consider the complaint and take the action it should have taken—remand to the Session. The merits of the removal were not decided. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 38-3, BCO 38-3.a, BCO 38-4, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-3, BCO 27-1.a, BCO 27-4, BCO 2-2, BCO 57-5 standing to complain membership removal pastoral discipline without process BCO 38-4 right to withdraw membership church discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2019-13</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2019-13.html">Gendy v. Central Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-13">A member removed from the rolls under BCO 38-4 challenged Presbytery&#x27;s ruling that she lacked standing to complain because she was no longer a member. The SJC sustained the complaint: standing under BCO 43-1 cannot be defeated by the very removal challenged. Removal under BCO 38-4 is pastoral discipline, a disciplinary case, not a merely administrative act. The SJC remanded to Presbytery to consider the complaint and take the action it should have taken—remand to the Session. The merits of the removal were not decided.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-13" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2019-14">The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it. The complainants had not documented that they first presented the complaint to Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery under BCO 43-2, and the SJC held that the Presbytery—not the SJC—was the proper court for the charges and specifications in the March 2, 2020 letter. The dismissal was recorded 19-0-0; no merits were reached.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2019-14" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2018-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2018-01 Mapes v. Metro NY" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2018-01: Mapes v. Metro NY, M48GA, pp. 638–649" data-search-text="2018-01 Glen Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery A ruling elder appealed convictions and censures arising from his brief refusal to leave a closed Temporary Session meeting. The SJC affirmed only his conviction for failing to submit to church government, because he knowingly attended and his apology acknowledged fault; it reversed findings of dereliction, sedition, rioting, and the balance for lack of supporting evidence. It rejected his first four appeal specifications, but held suspension and deposition excessive, substituted Admonition, and restored both sacraments and office, although he belonged to no particular Session. appeal Partially sustained; Moot; Reversed Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2018-1 BCO 40-5, BCO 31-2 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2018-01</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga48_2021__2018-01.html">Glen Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Moot; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2018-01">A ruling elder appealed convictions and censures arising from his brief refusal to leave a closed Temporary Session meeting. The SJC affirmed only his conviction for failing to submit to church government, because he knowingly attended and his apology acknowledged fault; it reversed findings of dereliction, sedition, rioting, and the balance for lack of supporting evidence. It rejected his first four appeal specifications, but held suspension and deposition excessive, substituted Admonition, and restored both sacraments and office, although he belonged to no particular Session.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2018-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2018-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2018-02 Lewis v. of the Mississippi Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2018-02: Lewis v. of the Mississippi Valley, M47GA, pp. 562–575" data-search-text="2018-02 Anna Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session&#x27;s alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews. bco_40_5_matter Out of order (type not stated) Not reached legacy 2018-2 BCO 40-5, BCO 38-4, BCO 15-4, BCO 40-1, BCO 40-2, BCO 40-4, BCO 40-6, BCO 13-9.f, BCO 34-1 BCO 40-5 report General Assembly referral SJC jurisdiction church membership erasure notice separate opinions">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2018-02</code> <span>· BCO 40-5 matter</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga47_2019__2018-02.html">Anna Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Out of order (type not stated)</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2018-02">After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session&#x27;s alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2018-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Metropolitan New York Presbytery A complaint sought a congregational meeting to vote on leaving the PCA after the temporary session denied the request in November 2017. The SJC dismissed the complaint as moot and not judicially in order. Both parties agreed at the panel hearing that the presbytery had voted in October 2018 to dismiss the congregation pending consent under BCO 13-9(f), and consent was given at a December 2018 called meeting. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2018-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga47_2019__2018-04.html">Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2018-04">A complaint sought a congregational meeting to vote on leaving the PCA after the temporary session denied the request in November 2017. The SJC dismissed the complaint as moot and not judicially in order. Both parties agreed at the panel hearing that the presbytery had voted in October 2018 to dismiss the congregation pending consent under BCO 13-9(f), and consent was given at a December 2018 called meeting. No merits ruling was made. Three commissioners dissented; one was disqualified.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2018-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2018-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2018-05 McKay v. Central Indiana" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2018-05: McKay v. Central Indiana, M47GA, pp. 576–577" data-search-text="2018-05 McKay v. Central Indiana Presbytery The SJC held that TE David McKay&#x27;s complaint against Central Indiana Presbytery was administratively out of order. The decisive defect was procedural: the e-mail transmitted to the lower court clerk did not satisfy BCO 43-3 because the complainant&#x27;s correspondence was insufficient to constitute proper notice. The SJC therefore reached no merits issue. All 24 participating commissioners concurred, with no dissent. The ruling enforces BCO 43-3&#x27;s notice requirement before a complaint can proceed. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2018-5 BCO 43-3, BCO 13-9 complaint administrative out of order notice requirement BCO 43-3 e-mail notice">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2018-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga47_2019__2018-05.html">McKay v. Central Indiana Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2018-05">The SJC held that TE David McKay&#x27;s complaint against Central Indiana Presbytery was administratively out of order. The decisive defect was procedural: the e-mail transmitted to the lower court clerk did not satisfy BCO 43-3 because the complainant&#x27;s correspondence was insufficient to constitute proper notice. The SJC therefore reached no merits issue. All 24 participating commissioners concurred, with no dissent. The ruling enforces BCO 43-3&#x27;s notice requirement before a complaint can proceed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2018-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2018-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2018-06 Edwards v. North Texas" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2018-06: Edwards v. North Texas, M47GA, pp. 577–578" data-search-text="2018-06 Edwards v. North Texas Presbytery The SJC held that Jared Edwards&#x27;s complaint against North Texas Presbytery was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, because the case had never been filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 &amp; 43-2). No merits were reached. The ruling drew 23 concurrences and no dissent; TE Fowler was disqualified as a member of the presbytery party (OMSJC 2.10(d)(3)(iii)). The decision illustrates the SJC&#x27;s threshold filing requirement: a complaint that bypassed the lower court cannot proceed. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2018-6 BCO 42-4, BCO 43-2 complaint administrative out of order BCO 43-2 BCO 42-4 filing requirements adjudicated below">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2018-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga47_2019__2018-06.html">Edwards v. North Texas Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2018-06">The SJC held that Jared Edwards&#x27;s complaint against North Texas Presbytery was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, because the case had never been filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 &amp; 43-2). No merits were reached. The ruling drew 23 concurrences and no dissent; TE Fowler was disqualified as a member of the presbytery party (OMSJC 2.10(d)(3)(iii)). The decision illustrates the SJC&#x27;s threshold filing requirement: a complaint that bypassed the lower court cannot proceed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2018-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2017-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2017-01 Dailey v. Heritage" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2017-01: Dailey v. Heritage, M46GA, pp. 571–581" data-search-text="2017-01 Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery Heritage Presbytery treated a member&#x27;s September 2016 filing against her session as a BCO 43-3 complaint and began adjudicating it. The SJC sustained RE Scott Dailey&#x27;s complaint against that action. BCO 43-3 allows higher-court review only if the lower court denies a complaint or fails to consider it by its next stated meeting. The session timely ruled the filing did not meet BCO 43-1 and did consider it, so neither condition applied. Presbytery&#x27;s post-November 12, 2016 adjudicative actions were annulled; possible underlying disciplinary matters were left to BCO 31-2 and 40-5. complaint Sustained; Annulled Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2017-1 BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-3, BCO 43-5, BCO 43-6, BCO 43-7, BCO 43-9, BCO 43-10, BCO 31-2, BCO 40-5, BCO 40-1, BCO 25-2, BCO 15-1, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 39-3.3 BCO 43-3 complaint procedure administratively out of order fails to consider higher court jurisdiction double jeopardy church discipline worship team dismissal New Covenant Presbyterian Church Heritage Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2017-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga46_2018__2017-01.html">Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2017-01">Heritage Presbytery treated a member&#x27;s September 2016 filing against her session as a BCO 43-3 complaint and began adjudicating it. The SJC sustained RE Scott Dailey&#x27;s complaint against that action. BCO 43-3 allows higher-court review only if the lower court denies a complaint or fails to consider it by its next stated meeting. The session timely ruled the filing did not meet BCO 43-1 and did consider it, so neither condition applied. Presbytery&#x27;s post-November 12, 2016 adjudicative actions were annulled; possible underlying disciplinary matters were left to BCO 31-2 and 40-5.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2017-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2017-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2017-02 Postles v. Heritage" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2017-02: Postles v. Heritage, M46GA, pp. 582–586" data-search-text="2017-02 Postles v. Heritage Presbytery The SJC denied a complaint challenging Heritage Presbytery’s November 12, 2016 action charging a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and appointing a prosecutor to investigate and, if necessary, indict. The complaint alleged the investigating committee lacked authority for judicial process, no written report existed, and the procedure and wording violated BCO 31-2. The Commission held a committee recommendation is not judicial action, no special instruction was required, the BCO 31-2 steps were followed, and the wording did not violate the accused’s rights. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 2017-2 BCO 15-1, BCO 15-3, BCO 31-2 ad interim committee committee recommendation vs. action judicial process initiation BCO 31-2 BCO 15-1 BCO 15-3 ordination vow violation appointment of prosecutor New Covenant Presbyterian Church Heritage Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2017-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga46_2018__2017-02.html">Postles v. Heritage Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2017-02">The SJC denied a complaint challenging Heritage Presbytery’s November 12, 2016 action charging a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and appointing a prosecutor to investigate and, if necessary, indict. The complaint alleged the investigating committee lacked authority for judicial process, no written report existed, and the procedure and wording violated BCO 31-2. The Commission held a committee recommendation is not judicial action, no special instruction was required, the BCO 31-2 steps were followed, and the wording did not violate the accused’s rights.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2017-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2017-06</code> <span>· Judicial reference</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga46_2018__2017-06_2017-07.html">Request for Reference from Blue Ridge Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2017-06">Blue Ridge Presbytery asked the SJC to hear and decide a complaint by reference. The SJC denied the request because the record demonstrated neither presbytery-wide disqualification nor serious division, constitutional questions, or new, delicate, or difficult issues warranting reference. Presbytery therefore had to hear and decide the complaint itself. The ruling concerned only the proper court for adjudication and did not decide the complaint’s merits; companion case 2017-07 was answered by reference to this decision.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2017-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

It noted that those responses and the requested minutes were forwarded to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records. The entry does not disclose the underlying citation grounds or evaluate the presbytery&#x27;s records on the merits; it confirms citation compliance and sends the materials on for ordinary records review.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2017-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-01 Aven v. Ohio Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-01: Aven v. Ohio Valley, M45GA, pp. 495–509" data-search-text="2016-01 Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC&#x27;s prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to &#x27;hear further&#x27; from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey&#x27;s nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits. complaint Denied; Remanded Not stated legacy 2016-1 BCO 21-4.e, BCO 21-4.f, BCO 21-5.2, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 40-2, BCO 40-2.1, BCO 14-6.a, BCO 14-6.g, BCO 14-6.i, BCO 14-6.k, BCO 14-7, BCO 13-6, BCO 31-2, BCO 34-5, BCO 39-3, BCO 14-6, BCO 43-3, BCO 42-4 paedocommunion Larger Catechism 177 Lord&#x27;s Supper covenant children stated differences fundamentals of the system of doctrine compliance with SJC remand standard of review clear error infant faith 1 Corinthians 11:27-29">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-01.html">Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-01">An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC&#x27;s prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to &#x27;hear further&#x27; from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey&#x27;s nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-02 Robertstad v. North Texas" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-02: Robertstad v. North Texas, M45GA, pp. 509–514" data-search-text="2016-02 Robertstad v. North Texas Presbytery The SJC found TE Arnold Robertstad&#x27;s complaint against North Texas Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order under BCO 43-3. Robertstad initially filed by e-mail—not an allowed filing—and his hard-copy filing arrived after the thirty-day deadline. The SJC reasoned that BCO 42-4/43-3 notification language concerns a lower court notifying parties, not party e-filing, and OMSJC 18.10.b bars e-mail filing. The merits were not reached; a concurrence urged later clarification by amendment, and no further proceedings are indicated. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2016-2 BCO 43-3, BCO 42-4, BCO 43-2 filing requirements e-mail filing thirty-day deadline administratively out of order BCO 43-3 notification of decision">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-02.html">Robertstad v. North Texas Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-02">The SJC found TE Arnold Robertstad&#x27;s complaint against North Texas Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order under BCO 43-3. Robertstad initially filed by e-mail—not an allowed filing—and his hard-copy filing arrived after the thirty-day deadline. The SJC reasoned that BCO 42-4/43-3 notification language concerns a lower court notifying parties, not party e-filing, and OMSJC 18.10.b bars e-mail filing. The merits were not reached; a concurrence urged later clarification by amendment, and no further proceedings are indicated.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-05 Troxell v. of the Southwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-05: Troxell v. of the Southwest, M45GA, pp. 514–523" data-search-text="2016-05 Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest A complaint challenged Presbytery’s institution of two charges against a teaching elder and related pretrial actions. The SJC annulled the household-management charge because process began fifteen months after the alleged offense and the record showed no recently flagrant, newly evident, or continuing offense under BCO 32-20. It also held that declaring the elder not in good standing removed rights without process, but left his properly imposed suspension effective. It rejected objections to discussion, questioning, and the timely submission charge, which could proceed without any determination of guilt. complaint Partially sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 2016-5 BCO 32-20, BCO 35-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 13-13, BCO 14-2, BCO 19-1, BCO 24-7, BCO 43-1, BCO 31-10, BCO 31-10.17, BCO 32-14 statute of limitations BCO 32-20 one-year rule recently become flagrant divorce remarriage ecclesiastical divorce suspension from official functions good standing complaint during judicial process managing household">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-05.html">Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-05">A complaint challenged Presbytery’s institution of two charges against a teaching elder and related pretrial actions. The SJC annulled the household-management charge because process began fifteen months after the alleged offense and the record showed no recently flagrant, newly evident, or continuing offense under BCO 32-20. It also held that declaring the elder not in good standing removed rights without process, but left his properly imposed suspension effective. It rejected objections to discussion, questioning, and the timely submission charge, which could proceed without any determination of guilt.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-07 Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-07: Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville, M45GA, pp. 523–524" data-search-text="2016-07 Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville Presbytery Avery and Lewelling complained that Nashville Presbytery wrongly denied their complaint against Shepherding Committee actions: initiating an investigation of TE Jim Bachmann and forwarding the report to the Committee on Judicial Business. The SJC dismissed. The November 10, 2015 challenge was untimely under BCO 43-2&#x27;s 60-day filing rule; the February 9, 2016 challenge was not a proper complaint because it targeted committee activities, not a court&#x27;s act or decision. All specifications were judicially out of order and could not be put in order. complaint Judicially out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 2016-7 BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2 complaint standing committee actions vs court actions timeliness of complaint BCO 43 complaint procedure shepherding committee">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-07.html">Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-07">Avery and Lewelling complained that Nashville Presbytery wrongly denied their complaint against Shepherding Committee actions: initiating an investigation of TE Jim Bachmann and forwarding the report to the Committee on Judicial Business. The SJC dismissed. The November 10, 2015 challenge was untimely under BCO 43-2&#x27;s 60-day filing rule; the February 9, 2016 challenge was not a proper complaint because it targeted committee activities, not a court&#x27;s act or decision. All specifications were judicially out of order and could not be put in order.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
