<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-08 Doty v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-08: Doty v. Nashville, M45GA, pp. 524–531" data-search-text="2016-08 Doty v. Nashville Presbytery A complainant challenged Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s handling of allegations against a teaching elder. The SJC held the matter judicially out of order and dismissed it, finding the original filing with the church session was not a BCO 43-1 complaint because the session lacked jurisdiction over the teaching elder. Presbytery properly treated the allegations as BCO 31-2/34-1 reports, and the complainant, not a Nashville member, lacked standing to complain about that new action. A nine-member dissent argued the filing of charges conferred standing under prior SJC cases. complaint Judicially out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 2016-8 BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 31-2, BCO 34-1, BCO 32-2, BCO 29-1, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-9, BCO 34-2, BCO 34-4, BCO 31-9, BCO 15-3, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-8, BCO 32-18, BCO 33-2, BCO 35-3, BCO 35-5, BCO 38-3, BCO 31-3, BCO 31-4 complaint standing charges vs reports non-member standing to complain BCO 43-1 standing filing charges with wrong court reports under BCO 31-2 investigation and declination to indict">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-08.html">Doty v. Nashville Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-08">A complainant challenged Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s handling of allegations against a teaching elder. The SJC held the matter judicially out of order and dismissed it, finding the original filing with the church session was not a BCO 43-1 complaint because the session lacked jurisdiction over the teaching elder. Presbytery properly treated the allegations as BCO 31-2/34-1 reports, and the complainant, not a Nashville member, lacked standing to complain about that new action. A nine-member dissent argued the filing of charges conferred standing under prior SJC cases.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-09 Fordice v. Pacific Northwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-09: Fordice v. Pacific Northwest, M45GA, pp. 531–542" data-search-text="2016-09 Fordice v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery A church member challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaint after it resolved accusations against a minister through a BCO 38-1 confession rather than trial. The SJC held that using confession without process was not itself error, but the statement and confession failed to correlate with and address the specific allegations. It sustained the complaint, annulled the denial, and remanded for Presbytery to amend the documents, institute process, reactivate the investigative committee, or otherwise respond directly and specifically to the unresolved allegations. complaint Sustained; Remanded Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2016-9 BCO 31-2, BCO 34-1, BCO 38-1, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 31-8, BCO 34-2, BCO 34-5, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 43-1, BCO 29-1, BCO 31-9, BCO 15-3, BCO 31-3 BCO 38-1 confession without process strong presumption of guilt full statement of facts BCO 31-2 investigation complaint against denial of process standing to complain ungodly pattern of behavior remand to presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-09.html">Fordice v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-09">A church member challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaint after it resolved accusations against a minister through a BCO 38-1 confession rather than trial. The SJC held that using confession without process was not itself error, but the statement and confession failed to correlate with and address the specific allegations. It sustained the complaint, annulled the denial, and remanded for Presbytery to amend the documents, institute process, reactivate the investigative committee, or otherwise respond directly and specifically to the unresolved allegations.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-11 Frazier v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-11: Frazier v. Nashville, M46GA, pp. 500–523" data-search-text="2016-11 Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial. complaint Denied Not stated — BCO 31-2, BCO 34-1, BCO 34-5, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-5, BCO 43-6, BCO 43-8, BCO 43-9, BCO 29-1, BCO 31-9, BCO 15-3, BCO 15-5.b, BCO 18-4, BCO 18-7, BCO 19-2, BCO 19-6, BCO 19-13, BCO 20-1, BCO 21-4.a, BCO 21-4.d, BCO 42-6, BCO 30-1, BCO 36-5, BCO 36-7, BCO 15-5, BCO 13-2 same-sex attraction homosexuality BCO 31-2 investigation strong presumption of guilt due diligence great discretion committee on judicial business recusal appearance of impropriety indictment complaint denied standards of review BCO 39-3.3 deference">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga46_2018__2016-11.html">Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-11">The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-12" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-12 Harwell et al. v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-12: Harwell et al. v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-12">Complainants sought review of Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s August 9, 2016 actions but filed directly with the SJC instead of first with Presbytery. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order and unable to be put in order: the initial filing was not a complaint against an act or decision (BCO 43-1) but suggested charges or an investigation request (BCO 31-2); BCO 43-2 required prior filing with Presbytery, and the sixty-day period had run. The complaint was dismissed without a merits ruling.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-14" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-14 Wills v. Metro Atlanta" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-14: Wills v. The SJC said no and denied the complaint. On the constitutional issue, it held that BCO 13-9.f grants dissolution power and BCO 40-6 does not impose formal process for it. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-14</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2016-14.html">Wills v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-14">Did a presbytery violate the BCO or clearly err by dissolving a congregation without its consent? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. On the constitutional issue, it held that BCO 13-9.f grants dissolution power and BCO 40-6 does not impose formal process for it. On the discretionary issue, it found no clear error in the record. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-15" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-15 Bachmann v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-15: Bachmann v. Nashville, M46GA, pp. 526–536" data-search-text="2016-15 Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery TE James Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s decision to replace his judicial commission&#x27;s recommended admonition with indefinite suspension. The SJC sustained the appeal: Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the verdict and amending the censure, which it had to approve or disapprove as a whole without debate. Bachmann&#x27;s earlier procedural challenges were not sustained; his unconditional post-trial confession waived them. The SJC rendered the commission&#x27;s judgment and admonition as its own decision, remanded to Presbytery, and restored Bachmann to good standing, subject to possible pastoral oversight items 2–4. appeal Sustained Not stated — BCO 15-3, BCO 30-3, BCO 36-2, BCO 36-3, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 42-6, BCO 42-9, BCO 31-10 appeal judicial commission BCO 15-3 presbytery amendment of commission judgment censure admonition indefinite suspension confession after trial plea agreement commission procedure repentance">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-15</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga46_2018__2016-15.html">Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-15">TE James Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery&#x27;s decision to replace his judicial commission&#x27;s recommended admonition with indefinite suspension. The SJC sustained the appeal: Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the verdict and amending the censure, which it had to approve or disapprove as a whole without debate. Bachmann&#x27;s earlier procedural challenges were not sustained; his unconditional post-trial confession waived them. The SJC rendered the commission&#x27;s judgment and admonition as its own decision, remanded to Presbytery, and restored Bachmann to good standing, subject to possible pastoral oversight items 2–4.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-15" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-16" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-16 Sartorius v. Siouxlands" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-16: Sartorius v. Siouxlands, M46GA, pp. 535–566" data-search-text="2016-16 Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery Did a presbytery fail in its duty to condemn erroneous opinions by acquitting a minister on theological-error charges? The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the acquittal undisturbed. A complaint against a not-guilty verdict cannot provoke a retrial at the superior court; under BCO 43 the superior court may only annul or remand, not reverse, and the complainant bore the burden to show error from the record. The record contained the defendant&#x27;s testimony, including recantations or clarifications, Defense Exhibit 1, and witness testimony sufficient to refrain from contradicting the trial court. The SJC expressly did not decide the defendant&#x27;s actual views. A separate concurrence elaborated deference standards but did not change the judgment. complaint Denied Not stated — BCO 13-9.f, BCO 15-3, BCO 31-2, BCO 35-1, BCO 35-5, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-5, BCO 43-7, BCO 43-9, BCO 43-10, BCO 42-6 Federal Vision theology New Perspective on Paul covenant of works baptism and saving benefits perseverance of the saints assurance acquittal complaint standards of review BCO 39-3 deference clear error factual finding double jeopardy condemning erroneous opinions BCO 13-9.f retrial Westminster Standards heresy charges judicial commission procedure">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-16">Did a presbytery fail in its duty to condemn erroneous opinions by acquitting a minister on theological-error charges? A complaint against a not-guilty verdict cannot provoke a retrial at the superior court; under BCO 43 the superior court may only annul or remand, not reverse, and the complainant bore the burden to show error from the record. The record contained the defendant&#x27;s testimony, including recantations or clarifications, Defense Exhibit 1, and witness testimony sufficient to refrain from contradicting the trial court. The SJC expressly did not decide the defendant&#x27;s actual views. A separate concurrence elaborated deference standards but did not change the judgment.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2016-17" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2016-17 Webster and Fowler v. Heritage" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2016-17: Webster and Fowler v. Heritage, M46GA, pp. 566–570" data-search-text="2016-17 Webster &amp; Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery Did Heritage Presbytery err by cautioning a session and requesting that it postpone a candidate&#x27;s election or ordination while a complaint about his qualifications was pending? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. The motion was advice, not an act for or requirement imposed on the session; the session could disregard it, and BCO 43-2 does not bar presbyters from discussing matters related to a complaint not yet before them. The SJC left undecided whether such discussions would disqualify presbyters, since the Ullrey complaint never reached presbytery. complaint Denied Not stated — BCO 21-4, BCO 21-4.f, BCO 21-5, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2 infant baptism ruling elder qualifications subscription to Westminster Standards presbytery advice to session jurisdiction of presbytery officer examination fundamental of system of doctrine BCO 21-4 complaint presbytery authority officer qualification infant baptism subscription fundamentals of the system of doctrine New Covenant Presbyterian Church">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2016-17</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga46_2018__2016-17.html">Webster &amp; Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2016-17">Did Heritage Presbytery err by cautioning a session and requesting that it postpone a candidate&#x27;s election or ordination while a complaint about his qualifications was pending? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. The motion was advice, not an act for or requirement imposed on the session; the session could disregard it, and BCO 43-2 does not bar presbyters from discussing matters related to a complaint not yet before them. The SJC left undecided whether such discussions would disqualify presbyters, since the Ullrey complaint never reached presbytery.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2016-17" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Philadelphia, M44GA, p. 512" data-search-text="2015-01 Sanfacon v. Philadelphia Presbytery The SJC held that a ruling elder’s complaint was administratively out of order and could not be put in order because the original complaint was filed 78 days after the challenged Session action—18 days beyond BCO 43-2’s 60-day window. A second complaint was merely an extension of the untimely first. Even though Session and Presbytery recognized the untimeliness but addressed it anyway, the SJC voided all lower-court actions on the complaints. A cited 2001 case was similar. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2015-1 BCO 43-2 administratively out of order timeliness of complaint 60-day filing window inactive ruling elder">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-01.html">Sanfacon v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-01">The SJC held that a ruling elder’s complaint was administratively out of order and could not be put in order because the original complaint was filed 78 days after the challenged Session action—18 days beyond BCO 43-2’s 60-day window. A second complaint was merely an extension of the untimely first. Even though Session and Presbytery recognized the untimeliness but addressed it anyway, the SJC voided all lower-court actions on the complaints. A cited 2001 case was similar.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-02 Gearhart v. Chicago Metro" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-02: Gearhart v. Chicago Metro, M44GA, p. 513" data-search-text="2015-02 Gearhart v. Chicago Metro Presbytery An unsigned complaint challenging a January 21 presbytery action was sent to the PCA Clerk by someone without standing. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1.a and dismissed it: the minister with standing failed to notify the Clerk within BCO 43-3’s 30-day window, and his later e-mail was not an unqualified ratification. Because the complaint could not be put in order, the SJC reached no merits. The decision illustrates strict filing and ratification requirements. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2015-2 BCO 43-3 administratively out of order timeliness of complaint 30-day notification window standing to file">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-02.html">Gearhart v. Chicago Metro Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-02">An unsigned complaint challenging a January 21 presbytery action was sent to the PCA Clerk by someone without standing. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1.a and dismissed it: the minister with standing failed to notify the Clerk within BCO 43-3’s 30-day window, and his later e-mail was not an unqualified ratification. Because the complaint could not be put in order, the SJC reached no merits. The decision illustrates strict filing and ratification requirements.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-04.html">Thompson v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-04">Thompson used a BCO 43 complaint to challenge his Session indictment during an ongoing disciplinary case, according to the separate concurrence. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order. It held that a defendant must raise such objections during process in the court of original jurisdiction under BCO 32-14 and, if still dissatisfied, pursue them on appeal under BCO 42-3. The ruling did not decide the indictment objection’s merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-05 Thompson v. South Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-05: Thompson v. South Florida, M44GA, p. 518" data-search-text="2015-05 Application of Thompson v. South Florida A BCO 40-5 application to cite Granada Presbyterian Church for alleged grossly unconstitutional proceedings and discipline delinquencies was found administratively out of order and dismissed as prematurely filed. The SJC held that, even assuming a credible report, BCO 40-5 first required citing the offending court before South Florida Presbytery, the court of appellate jurisdiction. Because Presbytery had docketed the matter for its August 11, 2015 meeting and had not yet ruled, the SJC could not act. No merits ruling on the discipline allegations was made. bco_40_5_matter Dismissed; No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2015-5 BCO 40-5 BCO 40-5 application prematurely filed administratively out of order grossly unconstitutional proceedings church discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-05</code> <span>· BCO 40-5 matter</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-05.html">Application of Thompson v. South Florida</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed; No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-05">A BCO 40-5 application to cite Granada Presbyterian Church for alleged grossly unconstitutional proceedings and discipline delinquencies was found administratively out of order and dismissed as prematurely filed. The SJC held that, even assuming a credible report, BCO 40-5 first required citing the offending court before South Florida Presbytery, the court of appellate jurisdiction. Because Presbytery had docketed the matter for its August 11, 2015 meeting and had not yet ruled, the SJC could not act. No merits ruling on the discipline allegations was made.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-07 Thompson v. South Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-07: Thompson v. South Florida, M44GA, pp. 521–523" data-search-text="2015-07 Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery The SJC dismissed John B. Thompson&#x27;s complaint against South Florida Presbytery as administratively out of order and prematurely filed. Because BCO 43-2 did not require the presbytery to consider the complaint until its next stated meeting, and that meeting had not yet occurred, the SJC held the case could not be put in order under the BCO or OMSJC. The unanimous officers&#x27; recommendation also called Thompson&#x27;s BCO 40-5 application premature. No merits were reached. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2015-7 BCO 43-2, BCO 40-5, BCO 31-2 administratively out of order prematurely filed next stated meeting requirement">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-07.html">Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-07">The SJC dismissed John B. Thompson&#x27;s complaint against South Florida Presbytery as administratively out of order and prematurely filed. Because BCO 43-2 did not require the presbytery to consider the complaint until its next stated meeting, and that meeting had not yet occurred, the SJC held the case could not be put in order under the BCO or OMSJC. The unanimous officers&#x27; recommendation also called Thompson&#x27;s BCO 40-5 application premature. No merits were reached.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-08 Hardie v. Metro Atlanta" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-08: Hardie v. Metro Atlanta, M44GA, pp. 522–536" data-search-text="2015-08 Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery TE John Hardie appealed his Metro Atlanta Presbytery conviction on three charges of breaking ordination vows and indefinite suspension, alleging seventeen procedural and evidentiary errors. Applying BCO 39-2/3 clear-error deference, the SJC denied every specification and upheld the judgment and censure. It found no clear error in the BCO 31-2 investigation, indictment/prosecutor process, commission membership, evidence rulings, scheduling, alleged prejudice, or censure. It assessed transcription costs equally while encouraging MAP to absorb them, and cautioned that an absent commissioner&#x27;s vote might support a future challenge. appeal Denied Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2015-8 BCO 31-2, BCO 31-8, BCO 31-10, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-17, BCO 35-7, BCO 39-2, BCO 39-3, BCO 42-6, BCO 30-1 appeal denied indefinite suspension ordination vows judicial commission procedure indictment BCO 31-2 investigation BCO 31-10 suspension without censure hearsay evidence witness qualification BCO 31-8 malignant spirit BCO 39-2 standard of review clear error standard">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-08</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-08.html">Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-08">TE John Hardie appealed his Metro Atlanta Presbytery conviction on three charges of breaking ordination vows and indefinite suspension, alleging seventeen procedural and evidentiary errors. Applying BCO 39-2/3 clear-error deference, the SJC denied every specification and upheld the judgment and censure. It found no clear error in the BCO 31-2 investigation, indictment/prosecutor process, commission membership, evidence rulings, scheduling, alleged prejudice, or censure. It assessed transcription costs equally while encouraging MAP to absorb them, and cautioned that an absent commissioner&#x27;s vote might support a future challenge.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-09 Bumgarner v. of the Mississippi Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-09: Bumgarner v. of the Mississippi Valley, M44GA, pp. 536–540" data-search-text="2015-09 Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley A claimant sought BCO 40-5 review of Presbytery’s handling of his earlier judicial case, alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings and delinquency in failing to investigate his 2012 deposition. The SJC found the application administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 40-3 excludes judicial-case proceedings from review and control when notice of appeal or complaint has been given, and he had withdrawn his 2012 complaint acknowledging it could not be resubmitted. It dismissed under OMSJC 9.2(d). The concurrence added that BCO 40 cannot refile a withdrawn complaint or reverse a censure. bco_40_5_matter Dismissed; No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2015-9 BCO 40-3, BCO 40-5, BCO 30-1, BCO 35-7, BCO 38-1 BCO 40-5 application administratively out of order withdrawn complaint cannot be resubmitted judicial case proceedings deposition ruling elder review and control judicial proceedings withdrawn complaint refiling">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-09</code> <span>· BCO 40-5 matter</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-09.html">Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed; No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-09">A claimant sought BCO 40-5 review of Presbytery’s handling of his earlier judicial case, alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings and delinquency in failing to investigate his 2012 deposition. The SJC found the application administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 40-3 excludes judicial-case proceedings from review and control when notice of appeal or complaint has been given, and he had withdrawn his 2012 complaint acknowledging it could not be resubmitted. It dismissed under OMSJC 9.2(d). The concurrence added that BCO 40 cannot refile a withdrawn complaint or reverse a censure.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-10 Thompson v. South Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-10: Thompson v. South Florida, M44GA, p. 539" data-search-text="2015-10 Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery The SJC dismissed a BCO 40-5 application because the matter concerned proceedings in a judicial case in which a complaint had been filed. Under BCO 40-3, such proceedings may not be handled by review and control once notice of appeal or complaint is given to the lower court. The SJC therefore found the case administratively out of order and not capable of being put in order under OMSJC 9.1.a., and dismissed it under OMSJC 9.2(d). bco_40_5_matter Administratively out of order; Dismissed Not reached — BCO 40-3, BCO 40-5 BCO 40-5 application administratively out of order review and control judicial proceedings complaint pending">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-10</code> <span>· BCO 40-5 matter</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-10.html">Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-10">The SJC dismissed a BCO 40-5 application because the matter concerned proceedings in a judicial case in which a complaint had been filed. Under BCO 40-3, such proceedings may not be handled by review and control once notice of appeal or complaint is given to the lower court. The SJC therefore found the case administratively out of order and not capable of being put in order under OMSJC 9.1.a., and dismissed it under OMSJC 9.2(d).</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-11 Thompson v. South Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-11: Thompson v. South Florida, M44GA, pp. 539–554" data-search-text="2015-11 Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery After a Session excommunicated a member without trial for contumacy, the SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, and later Session and Presbytery actions. No mutually agreed BCO 38-1 confession existed, and declining a confession meeting was not immediately censurable objective contumacy under BCO 32-6; subjective contumacy required confession or trial. The SJC did not find the indictment unconstitutional, decide trial guilt, or consider the unpleaded trespass warning. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated — BCO 29-1, BCO 30-1, BCO 32-6, BCO 32-6.b, BCO 36-6, BCO 38-1, BCO 38-3.a, BCO 42-2, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-3, BCO 43-5, BCO 43-7, BCO 43-8, BCO 43-9, BCO 12-1, BCO 12-5.a, BCO 43-1, BCO 40-5, BCO 46-8, BCO 34-2, BCO 31-2, BCO 32-2, BCO 13-9.b, BCO 40-1 contumacy BCO 32-6 excommunication case without process BCO 38-1 pre-trial censure due process refusal to cooperate citation to appear appellate procedure decorum procedural error">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-11.html">Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-11">After a Session excommunicated a member without trial for contumacy, the SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, and later Session and Presbytery actions. No mutually agreed BCO 38-1 confession existed, and declining a confession meeting was not immediately censurable objective contumacy under BCO 32-6; subjective contumacy required confession or trial. He reverted to membership under pending indictment. The SJC did not find the indictment unconstitutional, decide trial guilt, or consider the unpleaded trespass warning.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-12" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-12 Wills v. Metro Atlanta" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-12: Wills v. Metro Atlanta, M44GA, pp. 554–555" data-search-text="2015-12 Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery After Metro Atlanta Presbytery dissolved Grace North Atlanta, a complaint challenging that action was declared administratively out of order for lacking a signature. Wills then complained to the SJC. The SJC held the SJC complaint was not properly before it and was administratively out of order: under BCO 43-2, a complaint must first go to the court whose act is challenged, and Presbytery had not yet addressed that ruling. Wills could file with Presbytery within 30 days. No merits ruling on the dissolution. complaint Dismissed Not reached — BCO 43-2, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 39-3.3 administratively out of order complaint procedure BCO 43-2 first complaint to lower court dissolution of congregation affiliate church">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-12</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2015-12.html">Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-12">After Metro Atlanta Presbytery dissolved Grace North Atlanta, a complaint challenging that action was declared administratively out of order for lacking a signature. Wills then complained to the SJC. The SJC held the SJC complaint was not properly before it and was administratively out of order: under BCO 43-2, a complaint must first go to the court whose act is challenged, and Presbytery had not yet addressed that ruling. Wills could file with Presbytery within 30 days. No merits ruling on the dissolution.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2015-13" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2015-13 Barnes v. Heartland" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2015-13: Barnes v. Heartland, M45GA, pp. 478–495" data-search-text="2015-13 Barnes v. Heartland Presbytery Heartland Presbytery granted a transferring OPC teaching elder an exception to WCF 19, judging his stated differences &#x27;more than semantic but not out of accord with any fundamental.&#x27; The SJC sustained a complaint not against the merits of that judgment but against the sufficiency of the record supporting it. It held Presbytery clearly erred by failing to develop a sufficient record: the presbyters as a whole did not receive OPCUS&#x27;s adverse actions, its teaching restriction, or the elder&#x27;s longer paper. Remanded for those materials and release documentation to be included in the minutes. A concurrence addressed deference; four dissenters found no clear error. complaint Sustained; Remanded Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 21-4.e, BCO 21-4.f, BCO 21-5.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 40-2, BCO 40-2.2.3, BCO 40-4, BCO 14-6.a, BCO 14-6.g, BCO 13-6, BCO 31-2, BCO 40-2.3, BCO 39-3 stated differences WCF 19 law of God republication two kingdoms transfer of credentials examination of candidates fundamentals of the system of doctrine record of the case clear error standard of review OPC transfer Klinean theology">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2015-13</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga45_2017__2015-13.html">Barnes v. Heartland Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2015-13">Heartland Presbytery granted a transferring OPC teaching elder an exception to WCF 19, judging his stated differences &#x27;more than semantic but not out of accord with any fundamental.&#x27; The SJC sustained a complaint not against the merits of that judgment but against the sufficiency of the record supporting it. It held Presbytery clearly erred by failing to develop a sufficient record: the presbyters as a whole did not receive OPCUS&#x27;s adverse actions, its teaching restriction, or the elder&#x27;s longer paper. Remanded for those materials and release documentation to be included in the minutes. A concurrence addressed deference; four dissenters found no clear error.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2015-13" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<section class="judicial-year" data-judicial-year="2014"><h2>2014</h2>
<div class="judicial-year__records">
<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2014-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2014-01 Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2014-01: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley, M44GA, pp. 499–513" data-search-text="2014-01 Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred by judging TE Charles Hickey&#x27;s difference with Larger Catechism 177—over restricting the Lord&#x27;s Supper to those able to examine themselves—as more than semantic but neither hostile to the system nor vital to religion. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint. Because the Record did not sufficiently address Hickey&#x27;s particular expression and rationale, the Commission remanded to Presbytery for further hearing and a fuller record. It reserved the merits, including whether this formulation of paedocommunion is allowable. complaint Partially sustained Not stated legacy 2014-1 BCO 21-5.2, BCO 21-4.e, BCO 21-4.f, BCO 21-5.3, BCO 43-10, BCO 21-4, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-3 paedocommunion Westminster Larger Catechism 177 Lord&#x27;s Supper admission confessional exceptions fundamentals of the system of doctrine covenant children infant faith remand for insufficient record">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2014-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga44_2016__2014-01.html">Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2014-01">Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred by judging TE Charles Hickey&#x27;s difference with Larger Catechism 177—over restricting the Lord&#x27;s Supper to those able to examine themselves—as more than semantic but neither hostile to the system nor vital to religion. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint. Because the Record did not sufficiently address Hickey&#x27;s particular expression and rationale, the Commission remanded to Presbytery for further hearing and a fuller record. It reserved the merits, including whether this formulation of paedocommunion is allowable.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2014-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<section class="judicial-year" data-judicial-year="2013"><h2>2013</h2>
<div class="judicial-year__records">
<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-01 Dunn and Pesnell v. Philadelphia Metro West" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-01: Dunn and Pesnell v. Philadelphia Metro West, M42GA, pp. 554–560" data-search-text="2013-01 Dunn and Pesnell v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery The complaint challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery’s November 17, 2012 vote adopting its Complaint Commission’s recommendation to institute process and try TE David Swavely. The SJC did not sustain it. Although the record showed possible procedural irregularities—including unauthorized circulation of an earlier complaint—the SJC found no reversible error: presbyteries receive deference on factual records and broad latitude to judge the sufficiency of investigations. The recommendation to proceed to trial stands, subject to later parliamentary action. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2013-01.html">Dunn and Pesnell v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-01">The complaint challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery’s November 17, 2012 vote adopting its Complaint Commission’s recommendation to institute process and try TE David Swavely. The SJC did not sustain it. Although the record showed possible procedural irregularities—including unauthorized circulation of an earlier complaint—the SJC found no reversible error: presbyteries receive deference on factual records and broad latitude to judge the sufficiency of investigations. The recommendation to proceed to trial stands, subject to later parliamentary action. The SJC did not decide Swavely’s guilt.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-03 Marshall v. Pacific" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-03: Marshall v. Pacific, M43GA, pp. 548–554" data-search-text="2013-03 Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery Marshall complained that Pacific Presbytery wrongly refused to dismiss a judicial case despite alleged procedural irregularities in the indictment and process. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order: objections arising in a judicial case were to be preserved for appeal under BCO 32-14 and 42-3, and Marshall’s pending appeal independently barred a complaint under BCO 43-1. It granted no complaint relief. Separate opinions disputed the first rationale but agreed that the pending appeal barred the complaint. complaint Judicially out of order Not reached legacy 2013-3 BCO 32-14, BCO 42-3, BCO 43-1 complaint vs. appeal interlocutory appeal judicial case in progress complaint while appeal pending procedural regularity indictment objections">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga43_2015__2013-03.html">Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-03">Marshall complained that Pacific Presbytery wrongly refused to dismiss a judicial case despite alleged procedural irregularities in the indictment and process. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order: objections arising in a judicial case were to be preserved for appeal under BCO 32-14 and 42-3, and Marshall’s pending appeal independently barred a complaint under BCO 43-1. It granted no complaint relief. Separate opinions disputed the first rationale but agreed that the pending appeal barred the complaint.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-04 the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-04: the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina, M42GA, pp. 560–569" data-search-text="2013-04 the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery Hope Community Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s requirement that a multi-site congregation eventually particularize its second worship site. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the requirement, and struck it from the Presbytery Manual because BCO 12-5e specifically entrusts the time and place of worship to the Session, which Presbytery’s general church-enlargement authority could not supersede. The narrow ruling did not resolve broader concerns about multi-site churches or eliminate Presbytery’s review of a second site’s location under BCO 13-9(g). complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 2013-4 BCO 5-2, BCO 5-3.b, BCO 12-5.e, BCO 13-9.g, BCO 8-2.b, BCO 12-5, BCO 13-9, BCO 43-6, BCO 40-4 multi-site church particularization session authority over time and place of worship presbytery manual church planting policy mission church presbytery limits on session authority BCO vs. presbytery rules">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2013-04.html">the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-04">Hope Community Church’s Session challenged Presbytery’s requirement that a multi-site congregation eventually particularize its second worship site. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the requirement, and struck it from the Presbytery Manual because BCO 12-5e specifically entrusts the time and place of worship to the Session, which Presbytery’s general church-enlargement authority could not supersede. The narrow ruling did not resolve broader concerns about multi-site churches or eliminate Presbytery’s review of a second site’s location under BCO 13-9(g).</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-06 Gonzales v. Great Lakes" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-06: Gonzales v. Great Lakes, M43GA, pp. 555–567" data-search-text="2013-06 Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his claim that Presbytery failed to make required findings that he habitually neglected official functions and that any neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, and required no further action. The other four specifications were moot. Presbytery remained free to pursue proper Chapter 31 process or a procedurally compliant BCO 34-10 divestiture. appeal Sustained Not stated legacy 2013-6 BCO 13-2, BCO 34-10, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 46-8, BCO 42-3, BCO 21-1, BCO 34-8 divestiture without censure minister without call BCO 34-10 process lack of acceptance to the Church habitual failure to perform official functions strong presumption of guilt required procedural steps appellate deference">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-06</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga43_2015__2013-06.html">Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-06">A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his claim that Presbytery failed to make required findings that he habitually neglected official functions and that any neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, and required no further action. The other four specifications were moot. Presbytery remained free to pursue proper Chapter 31 process or a procedurally compliant BCO 34-10 divestiture.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-07 Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. of Southwest Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-07: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. of Southwest Florida, M42GA, pp. 566–573" data-search-text="2013-07 Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida The SJC sustained the Session&#x27;s complaint against Presbytery. Presbytery had ruled a member&#x27;s original complaint administratively out of order as untimely but then remanded the matter to the Session; the SJC held that once out of order, no complaint remained to remand. It also held Presbytery could not direct or instruct the Session to initiate formal process without BCO 40-5&#x27;s required citation step, so those directions were null and void. The member remained under the Session&#x27;s jurisdiction; the civil trespass order was not ecclesiastical discipline and did not alter membership. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2013-7 BCO 40-4, BCO 40-5, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-3, BCO 43-8, BCO 43-9, BCO 43-10, BCO 11-4, BCO 31-1, BCO 40-6, BCO 43-6 complaint procedure timeliness of complaint civil trespass order church member rights presbytery jurisdiction review and control BCO 40-5 process directing session to initiate process membership standing original jurisdiction member discipline session jurisdiction presbytery authority over session due process excommunication without charges BCO 40-4 remand">

<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-07">The SJC sustained the Session&#x27;s complaint against Presbytery. Presbytery had ruled a member&#x27;s original complaint administratively out of order as untimely but then remanded the matter to the Session; the SJC held that once out of order, no complaint remained to remand. The member remained under the Session&#x27;s jurisdiction; the civil trespass order was not ecclesiastical discipline and did not alter membership.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-08 Jackson v. Northwest Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-08: Jackson v. Northwest Georgia, M43GA, pp. 568–571" data-search-text="2013-08 Jackson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery Jackson challenged Northwest Georgia Presbytery’s failure to act on his BCO 40-5 letter alleging delinquency by Midway’s Session. The SJC found his complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because he was not a commissioner at Presbytery’s January 2013 meeting; originating a BCO 40-5 report did not confer standing. Separately, the SJC accepted jurisdiction over Presbytery’s failure to respond and remitted the matter for constitutional disposition, without deciding whether the Session committed the alleged delinquencies. complaint Administratively out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 2013-8 BCO 40-4, BCO 40-5, BCO 43-1, BCO 24-1 standing to file complaint BCO 40-5 credible report important delinquency commissioner standing session minutes ruling elder nomination">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga43_2015__2013-08.html">Jackson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-08">Jackson challenged Northwest Georgia Presbytery’s failure to act on his BCO 40-5 letter alleging delinquency by Midway’s Session. The SJC found his complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because he was not a commissioner at Presbytery’s January 2013 meeting; originating a BCO 40-5 report did not confer standing. Separately, the SJC accepted jurisdiction over Presbytery’s failure to respond and remitted the matter for constitutional disposition, without deciding whether the Session committed the alleged delinquencies.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-10 Latimer v. Chicago Metro" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-10: Latimer v. Chicago Metro, M43GA, pp. 572–585" data-search-text="2013-10 Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery A presbytery deposed a minister for violating his seventh vow by pursuing an unbiblical divorce after he filed a civil petition. The SJC sustained the appeal in part: the presbytery clearly erred in finding sin in the filing, because the record did not conclusively show intent to divorce rather than protect his children, and the wife&#x27;s counter-filing undermined the failure-to-withdraw inference. The SJC rejected prejudice, irregularity, and venue claims, voided the trial judgment, and noted that his expired prior suspension left him a presbytery member without call. Divorce precedents are fact-specific. appeal Sustained Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 34-7, BCO 31-2, BCO 35-11, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 35-7, BCO 42-7 unbiblical divorce deposition from office ordination vows divorce filing intent definite suspension indefinite suspension adultery child custody sinful intent">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-10</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga43_2015__2013-10.html">Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-10">A presbytery deposed a minister for violating his seventh vow by pursuing an unbiblical divorce after he filed a civil petition. The SJC sustained the appeal in part: the presbytery clearly erred in finding sin in the filing, because the record did not conclusively show intent to divorce rather than protect his children, and the wife&#x27;s counter-filing undermined the failure-to-withdraw inference. The SJC rejected prejudice, irregularity, and venue claims, voided the trial judgment, and noted that his expired prior suspension left him a presbytery member without call. Divorce precedents are fact-specific.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-11 Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. of Southwest Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-11: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. of Southwest Florida, M42GA, pp. 573–584" data-search-text="2013-11 Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida A Session appealed Presbytery’s judgment finding it guilty and suspending it for refusing instructions to institute process against a member. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed the judgment in whole, and dismissed the charges. Once Presbytery denied the member’s complaint, that matter should have ended; moreover, Presbytery did not follow BCO 40-4’s required first step before invoking BCO 40-5 review and control. The delay, prejudice, and missing-witness specifications were moot. The decision did not fault Presbytery’s underlying concern. appeal Sustained Not stated — BCO 40-4, BCO 40-5, BCO 42-6, BCO 15-3, BCO 34-1 appeal civil trespass order church member rights presbytery jurisdiction review and control BCO 40-5 process trial by presbytery judicial commission suspension of session irregularities in proceedings double jeopardy prejudice of judge refusal of reasonable indulgence">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2013-12" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2013-12 Marshall v. Pacific" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2013-12: Marshall v. Pacific, M43GA, pp. 585–586" data-search-text="2013-12 Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery, which failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case, causing irremediable injury. The SJC did not reach the merits; it suspended the lower judgment indefinitely, dismissed the appeal under BCO 42-7, rebuked Pacific Presbytery, and urged greater care in preserving, transcribing, and transmitting testimony. Dismissal therefore did not leave the challenged judgment enforceable. A separate concurrence suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter and questioned imprudent prosecutions. appeal Dismissed Not reached — BCO 42-7, BCO 35-7, BCO 32-14, BCO 43-1, BCO 32-12, BCO 32-2, BCO 42-3 record of the case incomplete record suspended judgment rebuke of lower court trial transcript court reporter">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2013-12</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga43_2015__2013-12.html">Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2013-12">G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery, which failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case, causing irremediable injury. The SJC did not reach the merits; it suspended the lower judgment indefinitely, dismissed the appeal under BCO 42-7, rebuked Pacific Presbytery, and urged greater care in preserving, transcribing, and transmitting testimony. Dismissal therefore did not leave the challenged judgment enforceable. A separate concurrence suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter and questioned imprudent prosecutions.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2013-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-01 Sherfey v. James River" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-01: Sherfey v. James River, M41GA, pp. 570–575" data-search-text="2012-01 Sherfey v. James River Presbytery The SJC dismissed a complaint against James River Presbytery without reaching the merits, holding it judicially out of order because the action complained against was not in the Record of the Case (BCO 43-1; OMSJC 10.6). The adopted ruling gives no further rationale and carried 13 concurring, 5 dissenting, 1 abstaining, 1 disqualified, and 4 absent. A dissent argued the record did contain an adjudicable Session action and that the cited OMSJC provision did not list the ground used; a separate written objection challenged a panel member&#x27;s participation. complaint Judicially out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 2012-1 BCO 42-3, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2 judicially out of order complainable action session authority pastoral call congregation approval impartiality">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2012-01.html">Sherfey v. James River Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-01">The SJC dismissed a complaint against James River Presbytery without reaching the merits, holding it judicially out of order because the action complained against was not in the Record of the Case (BCO 43-1; OMSJC 10.6). The adopted ruling gives no further rationale and carried 13 concurring, 5 dissenting, 1 abstaining, 1 disqualified, and 4 absent. A dissent argued the record did contain an adjudicable Session action and that the cited OMSJC provision did not list the ground used; a separate written objection challenged a panel member&#x27;s participation.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-02 Keating v. Warrior" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-02: Keating v. Warrior, M41GA, pp. 575–581" data-search-text="2012-02 Keating v. Warrior Presbytery Keating challenged Warrior Presbytery’s decision to divest him of ordination without censure while he was absent. The SJC sustained his appeal, reversed and voided the divestiture, and remanded because BCO 34-10’s required opportunity to be heard in his defense was not provided; this also amounted to hurrying before all testimony was taken. It rejected the reasonable-indulgence claim because Presbytery did not know of his postponement request. Keating remained a minister in good standing, but Presbytery could reconsider divestiture after reasonably soliciting a defense. appeal Sustained Not stated legacy 2012-2 BCO 13-2, BCO 32-6, BCO 34-10, BCO 42-3 divestiture without censure notification heard in own defense hurrying to decision ministerial call">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-02</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2012-02.html">Keating v. Warrior Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-02">Keating challenged Warrior Presbytery’s decision to divest him of ordination without censure while he was absent. The SJC sustained his appeal, reversed and voided the divestiture, and remanded because BCO 34-10’s required opportunity to be heard in his defense was not provided; this also amounted to hurrying before all testimony was taken. It rejected the reasonable-indulgence claim because Presbytery did not know of his postponement request. Keating remained a minister in good standing, but Presbytery could reconsider divestiture after reasonably soliciting a defense.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-03 Tarter v. Evangel" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-03: Tarter v. Evangel, M42GA, pp. 539–544" data-search-text="2012-03 Charles Tarter v. Evangel Presbytery A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another. appeal Sustained; Vacated; Remanded Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2012-3 BCO 8-7, BCO 15-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-10, BCO 32-5, BCO 32-8, BCO 32-13, BCO 34-5, BCO 35-5, BCO 35-7, BCO 39-3, BCO 42-3, BCO 34-10 submission to presbytery authority committee jurisdiction independent mission board due process hearsay evidence deposition Teaching Elder discipline indictment adequacy remand">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-03</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2012-03.html">Charles Tarter v. Evangel Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Vacated; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-03">A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-04 Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-04: Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West, M41GA, pp. 582–583" data-search-text="2012-04 Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery The SJC held TE Dwight Dunn&#x27;s complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1 and directed Presbytery to remedy the deficiencies by its next Stated Meeting before further action under OMSJC 9.2. The original complaint had been transmitted to the Faith Church Commission by the Stated Clerk, not committed by Presbytery motion as BCO 15-3 requires, and after the Commission denied it, the Commission did not seek Presbytery approval of its judgment. Because Presbytery had not acted, the SJC complaint was premature; no merits were reached. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2012-4 BCO 15-3, BCO 31-5, BCO 32-20, BCO 29-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-9, BCO 43-8, BCO 15-2, BCO 32-19, BCO 31-2 administratively out of order commission presbytery referral Faith Church Commission procedural deficiency">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2012-04.html">Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-04">The SJC held TE Dwight Dunn&#x27;s complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1 and directed Presbytery to remedy the deficiencies by its next Stated Meeting before further action under OMSJC 9.2. The original complaint had been transmitted to the Faith Church Commission by the Stated Clerk, not committed by Presbytery motion as BCO 15-3 requires, and after the Commission denied it, the Commission did not seek Presbytery approval of its judgment. Because Presbytery had not acted, the SJC complaint was premature; no merits were reached.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-05 Hedman v. Pacific Northwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-05: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest, M41GA, pp. 583–617" data-search-text="2012-05 Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery The SJC denied RE Gerald Hedman&#x27;s complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, which had adopted five not-guilty judgments on charges that TE Peter Leithart&#x27;s baptism, covenant, imputation, justification, and union-with-Christ views contradicted the Westminster Standards. Bound to the record and clear-error review, the SJC found no procedural violation and insufficient evidence that Presbytery clearly erred. It left the verdicts undisturbed, declined to endorse Leithart&#x27;s views generally, and urged continued clarification of his non-standard terminology. A separate dissent would have found error and ordered a new trial or reference. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2012-5 BCO 34-1, BCO 39-2.4, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 42-5, BCO 43-10, BCO 31-2, BCO 13-9, BCO 39-4, BCO 39-3, BCO 29-1, BCO 21-5.3, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-1, BCO 40-1, BCO 10-4, BCO 32-17 Federal Vision Westminster Standards Peter Leithart baptism covenant of works imputation justification union with Christ not guilty standard of review deference to lower court standing complaint vs. appeal Federal Vision theology sacraments">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2012-05.html">Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-05">The SJC denied RE Gerald Hedman&#x27;s complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, which had adopted five not-guilty judgments on charges that TE Peter Leithart&#x27;s baptism, covenant, imputation, justification, and union-with-Christ views contradicted the Westminster Standards. Bound to the record and clear-error review, the SJC found no procedural violation and insufficient evidence that Presbytery clearly erred. It left the verdicts undisturbed, declined to endorse Leithart&#x27;s views generally, and urged continued clarification of his non-standard terminology. A separate dissent would have found error and ordered a new trial or reference.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
