<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-07 Mitchell v. The of the Ascension" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-07: Mitchell v. The of the Ascension, M42GA, pp. 544–555" data-search-text="2012-07 William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension A ruling elder appealed judgments concerning an alleged broken promise to take a sabbatical and deficient performance as Session clerk. Because the pivotal email was absent from the record, the SJC vacated the sabbatical-related judgment and remanded for Presbytery only to consider whether a new trial was warranted. It reversed and dismissed the clerk-duty specification because the four-month delay in submitting minutes was attributable to the Session and did not justify a trial. Only the first specification remained potentially triable. appeal Partially sustained; Vacated Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment); Independent review (constitutional interpretation) legacy 2012-7 BCO 24-7, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 40-1, BCO 40-4, BCO 32-5 Ruling Elder discipline sabbatical from session submission to session clerk of session duties promise-keeping session minutes deference to lower court suspension from office ninth commandment fifth commandment">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-07</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2012-07.html">William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Vacated</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-07">A ruling elder appealed judgments concerning an alleged broken promise to take a sabbatical and deficient performance as Session clerk. Because the pivotal email was absent from the record, the SJC vacated the sabbatical-related judgment and remanded for Presbytery only to consider whether a new trial was warranted. It reversed and dismissed the clerk-duty specification because the four-month delay in submitting minutes was attributable to the Session and did not justify a trial. Only the first specification remained potentially triable.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2012-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2012-08 Sartorius et al. v. Siouxlands" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2012-08: Sartorius et al. v. Siouxlands, M43GA, pp. 528–548" data-search-text="2012-08 Art Sartorius et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. The SJC ordered a new trial on the same indictment under specified evidentiary procedures. Because this was a complaint rather than an appeal, it did not reverse the acquittals into findings of guilt or decide the doctrinal merits. complaint Partially sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2012-8 BCO 31-2 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga43_2015__2012-08.html">Art Sartorius et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-08">Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. The SJC ordered a new trial on the same indictment under specified evidentiary procedures. Because this was a complaint rather than an appeal, it did not reverse the acquittals into findings of guilt or decide the doctrinal merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2012-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

</div>

The SJC reached no merits issue. The vote was 15 concurring, 2 dissenting, 1 disqualified, 1 not qualified, 1 recused, and 4 absent; no dissent rationale is stated. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2012-9 None listed administratively out of order standing to file complaint transfer of membership OPC reception loss of PCA membership">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2012-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2012-09.html">Bennett v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2012-09">The SJC held TE M. Jay Bennett’s complaint against Missouri Presbytery administratively out of order for lack of standing. Korean Central, M40GA, pp. 550–551" data-search-text="2011-01 Choi v. Korean Central Presbytery A complaint challenged the nonacceptance of charges filed with Korean Central Presbytery. The record was unclear whether Presbytery or only its clerk had refused them, and did not show that Presbytery had denied a complaint concerning that refusal. The SJC therefore held the complaint administratively out of order as premature under BCO 43-2, without reaching the merits. complaint Administratively out of order Not reached legacy 2011-1 BCO 43-2 administratively out of order premature filing charges not accepted by presbytery">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-02 Gonzales v. Great Lakes" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-02: Gonzales v. Great Lakes, M40GA, pp. 551–556" data-search-text="2011-02 Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery The SJC denied a minister&#x27;s complaint challenging Presbytery&#x27;s out-of-order dismissal of his request for a BCO 31-2 investigation of another minister. Although the SJC agreed Presbytery wrongly said it had already decided all issues—the earlier complaint (SJC 2010-28) was distinct—it upheld the refusal to investigate. The accused minister had delivered an authorized committee report as chairman; absent evidence he exceeded that authorization, his statements were the committee&#x27;s, not personal, and BCO 31-2 did not require investigation. complaint Out of order (type not stated) Not reached legacy 2011-2 BCO 31-2, BCO 43-4 complaint out of order by lower court committee member immunity ninth commandment BCO 31-2 investigation committee report personal vs. committee action">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2011-02.html">Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Out of order (type not stated)</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-02">The SJC denied a minister&#x27;s complaint challenging Presbytery&#x27;s out-of-order dismissal of his request for a BCO 31-2 investigation of another minister. Although the SJC agreed Presbytery wrongly said it had already decided all issues—the earlier complaint (SJC 2010-28) was distinct—it upheld the refusal to investigate. The accused minister had delivered an authorized committee report as chairman; absent evidence he exceeded that authorization, his statements were the committee&#x27;s, not personal, and BCO 31-2 did not require investigation.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-03 Sagan et al. v. Covenant" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-03: Sagan et al. v. Covenant, M40GA, pp. 554–560" data-search-text="2011-03 Sagan et al. v. Covenant Presbytery Complainants challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt and adoption of recommendations from its MNA Committee, alleging that the committee exceeded its assignment to investigate campus-minister salaries. The SJC denied both consolidated complaints. It held that examining Presbytery’s relationship with MJCCW naturally extended the salary inquiry, fell within the committee’s oversight responsibility, and proposed discussion rather than structural change. Presbytery had also ruled the matters properly before it and rejected an appeal. The SJC could not independently verify assertions about the committee’s traditional oversight. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 2011-3 BCO 14-1.7, BCO 15-1, BCO 43-4 committee authority scope of committee mandate MNA committee campus ministry MJCCW RUM Reformed University Ministry overture">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2011-03_2011-04.html">Sagan et al. v. Covenant Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-03">Complainants challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt and adoption of recommendations from its MNA Committee, alleging that the committee exceeded its assignment to investigate campus-minister salaries. The SJC denied both consolidated complaints. It held that examining Presbytery’s relationship with MJCCW naturally extended the salary inquiry, fell within the committee’s oversight responsibility, and proposed discussion rather than structural change. Presbytery had also ruled the matters properly before it and rejected an appeal. The SJC could not independently verify assertions about the committee’s traditional oversight.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-04 Gunn et al. v. Covenant" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-04: Gunn et al. v. Covenant, M40GA, pp. 554–560" data-search-text="2011-04 Gunn et al. v. Covenant Presbytery Ministers challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt of and action on its MNA Committee report concerning the Mississippi Joint Committee on Campus Work, contending that the committee exceeded its assigned authority. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the study naturally extended the salary inquiry, the committee had oversight of MJCCW, the recommendations sought discussion rather than structural change, and Presbytery had ruled the matters properly before it. The record could not establish claimed traditional limits on oversight, and no corrective relief issued. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 2011-4 BCO 14-1.7, BCO 15-1, BCO 43-4 committee authority scope of committee mandate MNA committee campus ministry MJCCW RUM Reformed University Ministry overture">

<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-04">Ministers challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt of and action on its MNA Committee report concerning the Mississippi Joint Committee on Campus Work, contending that the committee exceeded its assigned authority. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the study naturally extended the salary inquiry, the committee had oversight of MJCCW, the recommendations sought discussion rather than structural change, and Presbytery had ruled the matters properly before it. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2011-05.html">Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-05">The SJC held Young Bae Kim&#x27;s complaint against Korean Capital Presbytery administratively out of order because it was not filed with the Stated Clerk within 30 days after the presbytery&#x27;s October 4, 2010 meeting, as BCO 43 requires. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-06 Sawyers et al. v. Missouri" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-06: Sawyers et al. v. Missouri, M41GA, pp. 552–564" data-search-text="2011-06 Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery Elders complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation by finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held Federal Vision views contrary to the Westminster Standards. The SJC answered yes: MOP erred under BCO 34-5, and the ordinary remedy was compliance with BCO 31-2. But because MOP had already tried Meyers on April 13–14, 2012, the SJC held further action moot, ordering no additional relief. Adopted by the SJC as a whole, with one dissent. complaint Sustained; Moot Not stated legacy 2011-6 BCO 31-2, BCO 29-1, BCO 29-2, BCO 34-5, BCO 27-4, BCO 30-4, BCO 38-1, BCO 34-4, BCO 27-3.c, BCO 27-3, BCO 34-4.b, BCO 32-6, BCO 33-2 Federal Vision Westminster Standards presumption of guilt investigation Jeffrey Meyers mootness">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2011-06.html">Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Moot</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-06">Elders complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation by finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held Federal Vision views contrary to the Westminster Standards. The SJC answered yes: MOP erred under BCO 34-5, and the ordinary remedy was compliance with BCO 31-2. But because MOP had already tried Meyers on April 13–14, 2012, the SJC held further action moot, ordering no additional relief. Adopted by the SJC as a whole, with one dissent.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-08 Sherfey v. James River" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-08: Sherfey v. James River, M40GA, pp. 562–581" data-search-text="2011-08 Sherfey v. James River Presbytery Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery. complaint Judicially out of order Not reached legacy 2011-8 BCO 43-2, BCO 43-3, BCO 43-6, BCO 43-8, BCO 43-9, BCO 39-3.1, BCO 36-1, BCO 36-7, BCO 38-1, BCO 37-8, BCO 34-8, BCO 37-3, BCO 37-5, BCO 37-4, BCO 43-4, BCO 17-2, BCO 21-7, BCO 30-5, BCO 46-8, BCO 37-9, BCO 42-3, BCO 34-10, BCO 32-6, BCO 31-2, BCO 32-6.a, BCO 33-2 judicially out of order complaint procedure de novo review commission scope timeliness of filing BCO 43-3 BCO 43-2">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2011-08.html">Sherfey v. James River Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-08">Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-09 Jennings v. North Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-09: Jennings v. North Florida, M40GA, pp. 565–580" data-search-text="2011-09 Jennings v. North Florida Presbytery North Florida Presbytery restored a minister deposed for adultery by a 19–17 vote. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery had not proceeded with the required caution and that a bare majority could not demonstrate BCO 34-8’s required strongly favorable general sentiment. It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process. complaint Sustained; Annulled; Remanded Not stated legacy 2011-9 BCO 34-8, BCO 37-5, BCO 37-8, BCO 37-3, BCO 37-4, BCO 37-9.a, BCO 30-5, BCO 46-8, BCO 17-2, BCO 21-7, BCO 36-7, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 42-1 restoration from deposition deposed minister general sentiment of the Church super-majority probationary period sexual sin BCO 34-8 BCO 37-8 restoration to office deposition">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2011-09.html">Jennings v. North Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-09">North Florida Presbytery restored a minister deposed for adultery by a 19–17 vote. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery had not proceeded with the required caution and that a bare majority could not demonstrate BCO 34-8’s required strongly favorable general sentiment. It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-10 Testa v. South Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-10: Testa v. South Florida, M40GA, p. 580" data-search-text="2011-10 Testa v. South Florida Presbytery The SJC held Frank Testa&#x27;s complaint against South Florida Presbytery administratively out of order because the presbytery had not yet acted on the underlying matter, so no merits decision was reached. The case thus turns on prematurity rather than the complaint&#x27;s substance; the sparse record does not describe the underlying dispute. The adopted vote was 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, and 4 absent. RE Donohoe was not qualified because he could not certify that he had read the necessary portions of the Record (OMSJC 2.3.b). complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached — None listed administratively out of order premature complaint complaint not yet acted on by presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-10</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2011-10.html">Testa v. South Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-10">The SJC held Frank Testa&#x27;s complaint against South Florida Presbytery administratively out of order because the presbytery had not yet acted on the underlying matter, so no merits decision was reached. The case thus turns on prematurity rather than the complaint&#x27;s substance; the sparse record does not describe the underlying dispute. The adopted vote was 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, and 4 absent. RE Donohoe was not qualified because he could not certify that he had read the necessary portions of the Record (OMSJC 2.3.b).</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Philadelphia Metro West, M42GA, pp. 500–527" data-search-text="2011-11 Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery Hahn challenged Presbytery’s ruling that CTKPC Session lawfully excluded him from that congregation’s worship until a psychiatric evaluation addressed safety concerns. The SJC denied the complaint. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it found no clear error in the lower courts’ credibility and discretionary judgments, given Session’s familiarity with the people and events. It characterized the restriction as informal pastoral safety guidance, not judicial discipline: it did not bar sacraments, worship elsewhere, or transfer, and attendance could resume upon medical assurance. The conditional local restriction therefore remained undisturbed. complaint Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 39-3 pastoral guidance worship attendance session authority complaint clear error">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2011-11_2011-12_2011-15_2011-16.html">Steven Hahn v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-11">Hahn challenged Presbytery’s ruling that CTKPC Session lawfully excluded him from that congregation’s worship until a psychiatric evaluation addressed safety concerns. The SJC denied the complaint. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it found no clear error in the lower courts’ credibility and discretionary judgments, given Session’s familiarity with the people and events. It characterized the restriction as informal pastoral safety guidance, not judicial discipline: it did not bar sacraments, worship elsewhere, or transfer, and attendance could resume upon medical assurance. The conditional local restriction therefore remained undisturbed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Philadelphia Metro West, M42GA, p. 508" data-search-text="2011-12 Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery Hahn appealed Presbytery’s guilty judgment and indefinite suspension from the sacraments, alleging trial irregularities, denial of a requested amendment, haste, and prejudice. The SJC denied the appeal on all three charges: false and unsubstantiated accusations, disobedience and disrespect toward church authorities, and a bitter and malignant spirit. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it deferred to Presbytery’s familiarity with the parties, witnesses, and extensive trial record and found no clear error, even though contrary evidence may have existed. The judgment and censure therefore remained undisturbed. appeal Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 39-3 appeal discipline indefinite suspension trial clear error">

<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-12">Hahn appealed Presbytery’s guilty judgment and indefinite suspension from the sacraments, alleging trial irregularities, denial of a requested amendment, haste, and prejudice. The SJC denied the appeal on all three charges: false and unsubstantiated accusations, disobedience and disrespect toward church authorities, and a bitter and malignant spirit. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it deferred to Presbytery’s familiarity with the parties, witnesses, and extensive trial record and found no clear error, even though contrary evidence may have existed. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-13: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church, M40GA, pp. 580–587" data-search-text="2011-13 Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church An individual appealed directly to the SJC, alleging her church effectively excommunicated her without process, failed the Matthew 18 process, and spiritually abused her by social isolation. The SJC dismissed as premature, without reaching the merits, because there was no record of a judicial decision by the church or of an appeal to Evangel Presbytery, the next higher court; it stated she could proceed only by providing such evidence. The severity of excommunication did not excuse that prerequisite. The SJC asked Presbytery to obtain the session&#x27;s written response to her letter. appeal Dismissed Not reached — BCO 42-1, BCO 42-2, BCO 30-4, BCO 36-6, BCO 15-5, BCO 45-1, BCO 39-2 premature appeal excommunication without process appeal to next higher court spiritual abuse OMSJC 2.10">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-15" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-15 Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-15: Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West, M42GA, pp. 500–528" data-search-text="2011-15 Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery Hahn challenged Presbytery’s refusal to institute process against three church members he had accused. The SJC denied his complaint because Presbytery found that BCO 31-8 applied to Hahn’s conduct and that the evidence did not create a strong presumption of guilt. Deferring to Presbytery absent clear error, the SJC left its refusal to appoint a prosecutor and commence process undisturbed. A concurrence agreed with the result but disputed the majority’s suggestion that filing charges generally requires process. complaint Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 31-2, BCO 31-8, BCO 39-3 institution of process charges discretion pastoral discipline clear error">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-15</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2011-11_2011-12_2011-15_2011-16.html">Steven Hahn v. <div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-15">Hahn challenged Presbytery’s refusal to institute process against three church members he had accused. Philadelphia Metro West, M42GA, pp. 500–528" data-search-text="2011-16 Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery Hahn challenged Presbytery’s refusal to appoint a prosecutor and institute process against Lisa Ridenour, RE Glen Ridenour, and TE Eric Huber. The SJC denied the complaint because Presbytery found BCO 31-8 applicable to Hahn’s accusations and found insufficient evidence of a strong presumption of guilt; the record showed no clear error. A separate concurrence agreed with the result but cautioned against implying that filing charges generally compels process, emphasizing a church court’s broader discretion to investigate and decline prosecution. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 31-8 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-16</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga42_2014__2011-11_2011-12_2011-15_2011-16.html">Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-16">Hahn challenged Presbytery’s refusal to appoint a prosecutor and institute process against Lisa Ridenour, RE Glen Ridenour, and TE Eric Huber. The SJC denied the complaint because Presbytery found BCO 31-8 applicable to Hahn’s accusations and found insufficient evidence of a strong presumption of guilt; the record showed no clear error. A separate concurrence agreed with the result but cautioned against implying that filing charges generally compels process, emphasizing a church court’s broader discretion to investigate and decline prosecution.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2011-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-17">Ministers challenged Jeremy Smith&#x27;s excommunication, but not his deposition. It sustained the complaint solely because Presbytery wrongly treated Smith&#x27;s absence as a refusal to appear: a committee email was not a citation by Presbytery. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2011-18" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2011-18 Ruff v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2011-18: Ruff v. Nashville, M41GA, pp. 566–570" data-search-text="2011-18 Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery Ruff challenged Nashville Presbytery’s investigation and its resolution of allegations against a minister through confession and admonition without formal process. The SJC sustained the complaint only on the confession and administration of censure: the investigation was adequate and BCO 38-1 was available, but the abstract confession did not acknowledge particular sins against particular people. Presbytery had to amend it, sponsor another reconciliation meeting, document satisfaction with the proceedings, or pursue the matter further, potentially through indictment. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 31-2, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3.3 investigation case without process confession admonition adequacy of confession repentance reconciliation">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2011-18</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga41_2013__2011-18.html">Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery</a></h3></header>

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2011-18">Ruff challenged Nashville Presbytery’s investigation and its resolution of allegations against a minister through confession and admonition without formal process. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-01 McNeil v. Chesapeake" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-01: McNeil v. Chesapeake, M40GA, pp. 522–523" data-search-text="2010-01 McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery Michael McNeil’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery was dismissed without a merits ruling after McNeil failed to appear at the SJC hearing. The panel called his name outside the hearing room and the Stated Clerk’s office; he was absent and had filed no brief. The notice had warned under BCO 42-11 that an appellant’s failure to appear would be treated as abandonment. The SJC declared the case abandoned and dismissed it. This illustrates dismissal for nonappearance, not adjudication of the underlying complaint. complaint Dismissed Not reached legacy 2010-1 BCO 42-11 abandonment of appeal failure to appear dismissed">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2010-01.html">McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-01">Michael McNeil’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery was dismissed without a merits ruling after McNeil failed to appear at the SJC hearing. The panel called his name outside the hearing room and the Stated Clerk’s office; he was absent and had filed no brief. The notice had warned under BCO 42-11 that an appellant’s failure to appear would be treated as abandonment. The SJC declared the case abandoned and dismissed it. This illustrates dismissal for nonappearance, not adjudication of the underlying complaint.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-03 McNeil v. Chesapeake" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-03: McNeil v. Chesapeake, M39GA, pp. 575–577" data-search-text="2010-03 McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery An appellant under suspension from the sacraments challenged the presbytery&#x27;s judicial commission process and censure. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order—not decided on the merits—because he had not submitted to a regular trial, as BCO 42-2 requires. Treated as a complaint, it was also out of order: it had not first been presented to the presbytery, and the 30-day period had expired. The SJC further barred complaints about later court actions while he remained under censure, except as to the highest censure. The censure stood. appeal Judicially out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 2010-3 BCO 15-3, BCO 30-4, BCO 32-4, BCO 32-6, BCO 33-3, BCO 36-3, BCO 37-3, BCO 39-3, BCO 42-2, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2 appeal judicially out of order contumacy standing to complain suspension from sacraments communing member in good standing failure to enter plea judicial commission authority">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-03</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-03.html">McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-03">An appellant under suspension from the sacraments challenged the presbytery&#x27;s judicial commission process and censure. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order—not decided on the merits—because he had not submitted to a regular trial, as BCO 42-2 requires. Treated as a complaint, it was also out of order: it had not first been presented to the presbytery, and the 30-day period had expired. The SJC further barred complaints about later court actions while he remained under censure, except as to the highest censure. The censure stood.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-04 Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-04: Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands, M39GA, pp. 578–593" data-search-text="2010-04 Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery A complaint challenged Siouxlands Presbytery&#x27;s investigation of allegations that TE Joshua Moon held heterodox Federal Vision views and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC held that Presbytery had investigated diligently under BCO 31-2 and, deferring under BCO 39-3 to its credibility judgment, found no clear error. It declined to decide whether the overture should have been treated as charges because that issue was not raised below, while leaving future charges possible. A concurrence favored charges; the dissent would have found error and remanded. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2010-4 BCO 13-9.f, BCO 15-3, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-7, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-18, BCO 34-1, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 40-4 Federal Vision theology strong presumption of guilt BCO 31-2 investigation BCO 32-2 charges deference to lower court clear error standard subscription to standards heterodoxy fundamentals of the system of doctrine Westminster Standards baptism and covenant New Perspective on Paul Norman Shepherd paedo-communion">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-04.html">Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-04">A complaint challenged Siouxlands Presbytery&#x27;s investigation of allegations that TE Joshua Moon held heterodox Federal Vision views and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC held that Presbytery had investigated diligently under BCO 31-2 and, deferring under BCO 39-3 to its credibility judgment, found no clear error. It declined to decide whether the overture should have been treated as charges because that issue was not raised below, while leaving future charges possible. A concurrence favored charges; the dissent would have found error and remanded.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-16" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-16 Lyons v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-16: Lyons v. Western Carolina, M39GA, pp. 594–601" data-search-text="2010-16 Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery Kirk Lyons filed BCO 32-2 charges against TE Craig Bulkeley with Western Carolina Presbytery. WCP dismissed the charges, then ruled Lyons&#x27;s complaint administratively out of order for lack of standing. The SJC answered that the dismissal was not erroneous—Presbytery had discretion under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20, and the record showed no clear error—but that WCP erred on standing because Lyons&#x27;s filing brought him under its jurisdiction. Because that error was not prejudicial, the SJC denied the complaint. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 15-3, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-20, BCO 34-2, BCO 38-4, BCO 39-3, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2 standing to bring complaint BCO 32-2 charges BCO 31-8 disqualified accusers BCO 34-2 scandalous charges on slight grounds BCO 32-20 one-year limitation communing member in good standing erasure from church roll dismissal of charges judicial commission authority malignant spirit toward accused">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-16</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2010-16.html">Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-16">Kirk Lyons filed BCO 32-2 charges against TE Craig Bulkeley with Western Carolina Presbytery. WCP dismissed the charges, then ruled Lyons&#x27;s complaint administratively out of order for lack of standing. The SJC answered that the dismissal was not erroneous—Presbytery had discretion under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20, and the record showed no clear error—but that WCP erred on standing because Lyons&#x27;s filing brought him under its jurisdiction. Because that error was not prejudicial, the SJC denied the complaint.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Gulfstream The SJC considered whether Gulfstream Presbytery had adequately answered a BCO 40-5 citation seeking a more acceptable response to exceptions of substance in its records. Korean Northwest, M39GA, pp. 601–602" data-search-text="2010-20 PCA v. Korean Northwest Cited under BCO 40-5 for exceptions of substance and failure to submit minutes, Korean Northwest Presbytery provided an acceptable response and submitted its minutes. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-26" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-26 Lee v. Korean Eastern" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-26: Lee v. Korean Eastern, M40GA, pp. 530–538" data-search-text="2010-26 Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery Korean Eastern Presbytery dismissed TE Eliot Lee&#x27;s charges against two teaching elders without trial, and the SJC sustained Lee&#x27;s complaint that this was unconstitutional. Although a presbytery may dismiss charges under BCO 29-1, 32-20, 34-2, or 31-8, it bears the burden of documenting that basis; KEP did not. The SJC refused Lee&#x27;s request that it enter the guilt verdicts the presbytery should have reached—that power exists on appeal, not complaint. It remanded for KEP to begin process under BCO 32. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 29-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-3, BCO 31-4, BCO 31-8, BCO 31-9, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-20, BCO 34-2, BCO 40-2, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-10, BCO 13-9, BCO 46-6 charges vs. complaint dismissal of charges without trial BCO 31-2 investigation civil lawsuit against church member presbytery discipline bad report vs. specific charges remand">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-26</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2010-26.html">Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-26">Korean Eastern Presbytery dismissed TE Eliot Lee&#x27;s charges against two teaching elders without trial, and the SJC sustained Lee&#x27;s complaint that this was unconstitutional. Although a presbytery may dismiss charges under BCO 29-1, 32-20, 34-2, or 31-8, it bears the burden of documenting that basis; KEP did not. The SJC refused Lee&#x27;s request that it enter the guilt verdicts the presbytery should have reached—that power exists on appeal, not complaint. It remanded for KEP to begin process under BCO 32.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-26" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-27" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-27 Ruff v. Nashville" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-27: Ruff v. Nashville, M40GA, pp. 538–542" data-search-text="2010-27 Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery The SJC dismissed Matt Ruff&#x27;s complaint against Nashville Presbytery as judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.a. Ruff challenged Presbytery&#x27;s failure to investigate a teaching elder, but BCO 43 requires a complaint against an act or decision; lack of action qualifies only when a court meeting has occurred and the court failed to act. Presbytery&#x27;s nearest antecedent meeting was August 18, 2010, and Ruff filed October 27, 2010, beyond BCO 43-2&#x27;s thirty-day limit. Because the defect could not be cured, the case was dismissed without reaching the merits; a separate objection disputed that ruling. complaint Dismissed Not reached — BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 39-3.1 judicially out of order timeliness of complaint complaint against inaction thirty-day filing period lack of action by presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-27</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2010-27.html">Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-27">The SJC dismissed Matt Ruff&#x27;s complaint against Nashville Presbytery as judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.a. Ruff challenged Presbytery&#x27;s failure to investigate a teaching elder, but BCO 43 requires a complaint against an act or decision; lack of action qualifies only when a court meeting has occurred and the court failed to act. Presbytery&#x27;s nearest antecedent meeting was August 18, 2010, and Ruff filed October 27, 2010, beyond BCO 43-2&#x27;s thirty-day limit. Because the defect could not be cured, the case was dismissed without reaching the merits; a separate objection disputed that ruling.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-27" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2010-28" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2010-28 Gonzales v. Great Lakes" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2010-28: Gonzales v. Great Lakes, M40GA, pp. 542–553" data-search-text="2010-28 Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery Gonzales challenged Great Lakes Presbytery’s approval of recommendations following a BCO 31-2 investigation that found no basis for charges. The SJC sustained the complaint only as to recommendation five—which threatened adverse consequences for his recommendation or transfer if he rejected pastoral advice—and annulled its approval. Presbytery could offer pastoral oversight and counsel, including the other recommendations, but without judicial process that counsel could not expressly or implicitly diminish his good standing. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 13-9.a, BCO 20-9, BCO 20-10, BCO 31-2, BCO 34-3, BCO 36-1, BCO 3-3, BCO 43-10, BCO 46-6, BCO 13-9, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 43-2 BCO 31-2 investigation pastoral oversight good standing judicial commission demit ministry presbytery authority fitness for ministry">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2010-28</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga40_2012__2010-28.html">Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2010-28">Gonzales challenged Great Lakes Presbytery’s approval of recommendations following a BCO 31-2 investigation that found no basis for charges. The SJC sustained the complaint only as to recommendation five—which threatened adverse consequences for his recommendation or transfer if he rejected pastoral advice—and annulled its approval. Presbytery could offer pastoral oversight and counsel, including the other recommendations, but without judicial process that counsel could not expressly or implicitly diminish his good standing.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2010-28" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-02 Smith v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-02: Smith v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 182–197" data-search-text="2009-02 Morton Smith v. Western Carolina Smith challenged Presbytery’s reversal of a finding that an elder’s race-and-IQ views did not create a strong presumption of guilt and its immediate judgment against those views. The SJC upheld the reversal as a discretionary determination, without addressing its merits, but annulled the declaration against the views because a strong-presumption finding required judicial process. On remand, Presbytery was to commence process against the elder or rescind that finding and drop the matter. The ruling did not restrict Presbytery’s ability to adopt general position statements outside an investigation. complaint Partially sustained; Annulled; Remanded Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2009-2 BCO 13-9.f, BCO 31-2, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 15-1, BCO 15-3, BCO 27-5, BCO 21-5.7, BCO 24-10, BCO 32-3, BCO 24-7 Judicial procedure Presumption of guilt Racial views Due process Christian liberty Erroneous opinions Western Carolina Presbytery RE Neil Payne">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-02.html">Morton Smith v. Western Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Annulled; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-02">Smith challenged Presbytery’s reversal of a finding that an elder’s race-and-IQ views did not create a strong presumption of guilt and its immediate judgment against those views. The SJC upheld the reversal as a discretionary determination, without addressing its merits, but annulled the declaration against the views because a strong-presumption finding required judicial process. On remand, Presbytery was to commence process against the elder or rescind that finding and drop the matter. The ruling did not restrict Presbytery’s ability to adopt general position statements outside an investigation.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-03 Leissing v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-03: Leissing v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 156–181" data-search-text="2009-03 Leissing v. Western Carolina Leissing challenged Presbytery&#x27;s November 7 action dissolving the calls of REs Linton and Pellom. By reference to Case 2008-15, the SJC sustained the complaint: the Session had canceled the August 7 congregational meeting, so it generated no valid dissolution request and Presbytery erred in appointing the Sealy Commission. The Commission proceedings, the complaint against its decision, and Presbytery&#x27;s resulting dissolution action were voided; absent subsequent congregational action, the elders&#x27; calls remained undissolved. complaint Partially sustained Not stated legacy 2009-3 BCO 13-9, BCO 24-7, BCO 31-2 presbytery jurisdiction elder dissolution congregational meeting validity original jurisdiction sealy commission">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html">Leissing v. Western Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-03">Leissing challenged Presbytery&#x27;s November 7 action dissolving the calls of REs Linton and Pellom. By reference to Case 2008-15, the SJC sustained the complaint: the Session had canceled the August 7 congregational meeting, so it generated no valid dissolution request and Presbytery erred in appointing the Sealy Commission. The Commission proceedings, the complaint against its decision, and Presbytery&#x27;s resulting dissolution action were voided; absent subsequent congregational action, the elders&#x27; calls remained undissolved.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-05 Payne v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-05: Payne v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 197–198" data-search-text="2009-05 Payne v. Western Carolina Presbytery Four complainants challenged Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt, citing delayed action and failure to interview accusers. The SJC denied the complaints: BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but grants great discretion and prescribes neither interviews nor a timetable, and the record showed no clear constitutional error overcoming deference to Presbytery. Lyons and Woodward also lacked standing because they were not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. No renewed investigation or process was ordered. complaint Not sustained; Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2009-5 BCO 31-2, BCO 39-3, BCO 43-1, BCO 11-4 BCO 31-2 investigation strong presumption of guilt standing due process presbytery discretion">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html">Payne v. Western Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained; Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-05">Four complainants challenged Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt, citing delayed action and failure to interview accusers. The SJC denied the complaints: BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but grants great discretion and prescribes neither interviews nor a timetable, and the record showed no clear constitutional error overcoming deference to Presbytery. Lyons and Woodward also lacked standing because they were not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. No renewed investigation or process was ordered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-06 Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-06: Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest, M38GA, pp. 212–216" data-search-text="2009-06 Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery Pacific Northwest Presbytery adopted a report finding TE Peter Leithart&#x27;s views not out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine. The SJC sustained a complaint, holding PNW erred because, without formal judicial process, it lacked authority to declare either that the views were out of accord or that they were not. The record still suggested a strong presumption of guilt. The SJC refused complainants&#x27; affirmative declaration and remanded with directions for pastoral counsel under BCO 31-7 and possible BCO 31-2 compliance. complaint Sustained; Reversed; Remanded Not stated legacy 2009-6 BCO 29-1, BCO 29-2, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-7, BCO 34-5, BCO 34-6, BCO 39-3 Federal Vision doctrinal standards strong presumption of guilt BCO 31-2 pastoral counsel">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-06.html">Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-06">Pacific Northwest Presbytery adopted a report finding TE Peter Leithart&#x27;s views not out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine. The SJC sustained a complaint, holding PNW erred because, without formal judicial process, it lacked authority to declare either that the views were out of accord or that they were not. The record still suggested a strong presumption of guilt. The SJC refused complainants&#x27; affirmative declaration and remanded with directions for pastoral counsel under BCO 31-7 and possible BCO 31-2 compliance.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-07 Urish v. Rocky Mountain" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-07: Urish v. Rocky Mountain, M38GA, pp. 235–242" data-search-text="2009-07 Urish v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery The SJC denied James Urish and others&#x27; complaint against Rocky Mountain Presbytery for sustaining Dan Breed&#x27;s ordination exam. Breed had said women could teach Scripture to mixed adults in settings like Sunday school under session oversight, but not preach, hold elder office, or teach outside session authority. Because the Westminster Standards and BCO did not expressly resolve that view, the SJC found no clear error under BCO 39 and affirmed Presbytery&#x27;s denial. A concurrence criticized Breed&#x27;s exegesis of 1 Tim. 2:12 but stressed the SJC was not endorsing it. complaint Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2009-7 BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 21-5.3, BCO 4-4, BCO 53-2, BCO 21-4.c.1.b, BCO 21-4.c.2 women teaching in church theological examination ordination standards women&#x27;s roles in church ministry 1 Timothy 2:12 exegesis church authority and governance">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-07.html">Urish v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-07">The SJC denied James Urish and others&#x27; complaint against Rocky Mountain Presbytery for sustaining Dan Breed&#x27;s ordination exam. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-08 Linton v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-08: Linton v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 197–207" data-search-text="2009-08 Linton v. Western Carolina Presbytery An elder challenged Presbytery’s failure to interview accusers, alleged investigative delay, and resulting finding of no strong presumption of a pastor’s guilt. The SJC denied the complaint. BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes no timeline or interview procedure, giving courts substantial discretion before formal process begins. The ordinary stated-meeting sequence used here disclosed no clear constitutional error. The SJC therefore deferred to Presbytery’s superior proximity to the facts and upheld its finding. complaint Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2009-8 BCO 31-2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 43-1, BCO 11-4 Church discipline 31-2 investigation Presbytery procedures Due process Standing of complainants Judicial discretion">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html">Linton v. Western Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-08">An elder challenged Presbytery’s failure to interview accusers, alleged investigative delay, and resulting finding of no strong presumption of a pastor’s guilt. The SJC denied the complaint. BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes no timeline or interview procedure, giving courts substantial discretion before formal process begins. The ordinary stated-meeting sequence used here disclosed no clear constitutional error. The SJC therefore deferred to Presbytery’s superior proximity to the facts and upheld its finding.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-09 Lyons v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-09: Lyons v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 197–207" data-search-text="2009-09 Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery Lyons challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a teaching elder, alleging failure to interview accusers, undue delay, and an erroneous finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC denied the complaint and additionally held that Lyons lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. The consolidated opinion explained that BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes neither interviews nor a timeline; finding no constitutional or clear factual error, it deferred to Presbytery’s judgment. complaint Partially sustained; Denied Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 2009-9 BCO 31-2, BCO 38-1, BCO 40-2, BCO 24-10, BCO 27-5, BCO 34-2, BCO 21-5.7 Presbytery judicial procedure Due process in investigation BCO 31-2 investigation Denial of hearing to accusers Presbytery finding of guilt">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html">Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-09">Lyons challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a teaching elder, alleging failure to interview accusers, undue delay, and an erroneous finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC denied the complaint and additionally held that Lyons lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. The consolidated opinion explained that BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes neither interviews nor a timeline; finding no constitutional or clear factual error, it deferred to Presbytery’s judgment.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-10 Woodward v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-10: Woodward v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 197–207" data-search-text="2009-10 Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery Robert Woodward challenged Presbytery’s acceptance of a finding that accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley did not raise a strong presumption of guilt, alleging investigators never heard his evidence. The SJC denied the complaint, specifically holding that Woodward lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. It also held that BCO 31-2 prescribes no interview requirement or fixed timeline and found no clear constitutional error warranting departure from ordinary deference to Presbytery. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) — BCO 31-2, BCO 38-1, BCO 27-5, BCO 40-2, BCO 13-9, BCO 15-1, BCO 15-2, BCO 24-7, BCO 24-10 Judicial Investigation Procedural Due Process Church Discipline Presbytery Authority Race and Church Life">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-10</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-05_2009-08_2009-09_2009-10.html">Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-10">Robert Woodward challenged Presbytery’s acceptance of a finding that accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley did not raise a strong presumption of guilt, alleging investigators never heard his evidence. The SJC denied the complaint, specifically holding that Woodward lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. It also held that BCO 31-2 prescribes no interview requirement or fixed timeline and found no clear constitutional error warranting departure from ordinary deference to Presbytery.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-11 Edison et al. v. Southwest Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-11: Edison et al. v. Southwest Florida, M38GA, pp. 129–131" data-search-text="2009-11 Larry Edison et al. v. Southwest Florida Presbytery Ministers complained that Southwest Florida Presbytery improperly reexamined Bryan Gregory and reversed his examination, membership, and call after previously receiving him. The SJC upheld Presbytery’s authority to hear and sustain the earlier complaint but sustained the present complaint on the remedial actions. Sustaining a complaint did not itself undo prior acts; once Presbytery had treated Gregory as a member, his membership rights could be removed only through disciplinary due process. The SJC annulled the reexamination and March 24 actions and directed Presbytery to consider appropriate remedies. Gregory’s theology was not before it. complaint Partially sustained Not stated — BCO 33-1, BCO 13-6 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2009-11.html">Larry Edison et al. v. Southwest Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-11">Ministers complained that Southwest Florida Presbytery improperly reexamined Bryan Gregory and reversed his examination, membership, and call after previously receiving him. The SJC upheld Presbytery’s authority to hear and sustain the earlier complaint but sustained the present complaint on the remedial actions. Sustaining a complaint did not itself undo prior acts; once Presbytery had treated Gregory as a member, his membership rights could be removed only through disciplinary due process. The SJC annulled the reexamination and March 24 actions and directed Presbytery to consider appropriate remedies. Gregory’s theology was not before it.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-12">Presbytery refused to hear Armes’s complaint against his excommunication, initially reasoning that excommunication deprived him of standing and later ruling the complaint untimely. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-21" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-21 Armes v. Southwest Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-21: Armes v. Southwest Florida, M39GA, pp. 530–535" data-search-text="2009-21 Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery Armes challenged Presbytery&#x27;s refusal to hear his second complaint about Session&#x27;s trespass notice and threat of arrest, which Presbytery treated as duplicating his pending excommunication complaint. The SJC sustained the complaint because the trespass action occurred later and was distinct, although the matters could be heard together. It remanded for Presbytery or a commission to hear the complaint under BCO 43-8. The SJC did not decide whether Session could issue such a notice; review remained subject to timely filing and standing. complaint Partially sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 38-1, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-4, BCO 43-8, BCO 30-4 excommunication standing to complain trespass notice complaint procedure remand same substance">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-21</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-12_2009-21.html">Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-21">Armes challenged Presbytery&#x27;s refusal to hear his second complaint about Session&#x27;s trespass notice and threat of arrest, which Presbytery treated as duplicating his pending excommunication complaint. The SJC sustained the complaint because the trespass action occurred later and was distinct, although the matters could be heard together. It remanded for Presbytery or a commission to hear the complaint under BCO 43-8. The SJC did not decide whether Session could issue such a notice; review remained subject to timely filing and standing.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-21" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-22" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-22 McNeil v. Chesapeake" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-22: McNeil v. Chesapeake, M39GA, pp. 535–540" data-search-text="2009-22 McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery The SJC denied a censured husband&#x27;s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery&#x27;s approval of a judicial commission report, which had upheld his session&#x27;s refusal to receive his charges against his wife after she filed for civil divorce. Applying BCO 39-3.2–3.3, the SJC deferred to the lower courts&#x27; factual and discretionary findings absent clear error. It found no clear procedural error, upheld the conclusion that the wife did not sin by seeking civil protection, and invoked BCO 31-8&#x27;s caution about accusations from one under censure. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) — BCO 31-8, BCO 39-3.2, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 13-9, BCO 32-20, BCO 39-3, BCO 32-2, BCO 43-1, BCO 32-3, BCO 31-2, BCO 34-2 church discipline marital conflict charges against spouse great deference appellate review civil courts">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-23" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-23 Koerkenmeier v. Illiana" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-23: Koerkenmeier v. Illiana, M39GA, pp. 538–544" data-search-text="2009-23 Koerkenmeier v. Illiana Presbytery Illiana Presbytery appointed a commission with broad power &#x27;to deal with matters&#x27; at Center Grove Presbyterian Church after a pastor requested inquiry into alleged evils. The SJC sustained the complaint but held the error harmless: the broad charge could take original jurisdiction from the session contrary to BCO 11-3 &amp; 4 and 33-1, while a limited investigative committee under BCO 13-9(f) and 31-2 would have been proper. Because the commission never exercised that power and the session endorsed its findings, no remedy, including invalidation of the adopted report, was ordered. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 11-3, BCO 11-4, BCO 13-9, BCO 13-9.f, BCO 31-2, BCO 33-1 presbyterial oversight commission powers congregational jurisdiction original jurisdiction BCO 13-9f harmless error">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-23</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-23.html">Koerkenmeier v. Illiana Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-23">Illiana Presbytery appointed a commission with broad power &#x27;to deal with matters&#x27; at Center Grove Presbyterian Church after a pastor requested inquiry into alleged evils. The SJC sustained the complaint but held the error harmless: the broad charge could take original jurisdiction from the session contrary to BCO 11-3 &amp; 4 and 33-1, while a limited investigative committee under BCO 13-9(f) and 31-2 would have been proper. Because the commission never exercised that power and the session endorsed its findings, no remedy, including invalidation of the adopted report, was ordered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-23" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
<div class="judicial-case__topics" aria-label="Topic tags"><span class="judicial-case__topics-label">Topics</span><span class="judicial-pill">presbyterial oversight</span><span class="judicial-pill">commission powers</span><span class="judicial-pill">congregational jurisdiction</span><span class="judicial-case__topics-extra" id="judicial-topics-2009-23" hidden><span class="judicial-pill">original jurisdiction</span><span class="judicial-pill">BCO 13-9f</span><span class="judicial-pill">harmless error</span></span><button type="button" class="judicial-topics__toggle" aria-controls="judicial-topics-2009-23" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Show 3 more topics" data-topic-count="3">+3 topics</button></div>
