<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-24" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-24 Phelps v. Pacific" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-24: Phelps v. Pacific, M39GA, pp. 543–548" data-search-text="2009-24 Phelps v. Pacific Presbytery Phelps complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by finding no constitutional irregularities in the New Life Burbank Session&#x27;s ordination of Lee Irons as a ruling elder, despite PP&#x27;s earlier refusal to receive Irons as a teaching-elder candidate. The SJC denied the complaint. Under BCO 39-3.3, the Court owed great deference to the lower court&#x27;s discretionary fitness judgment; the single office of elder does not require identical eligibility processes, and the NLB Session had jurisdiction after Irons renounced OPC jurisdiction. PP&#x27;s action stood; the SJC declined to decide the NAPARC issue. complaint Denied Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 8-9, BCO 18-3, BCO 21-4, BCO 21-5, BCO 24-1, BCO 24-6, BCO 39-3.3 ruling elder ordination teaching elder ordination OPC discipline one office two forms renunciation of jurisdiction NAPARC presbytery discretion">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-24</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-24.html">Phelps v. Pacific Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-24">Phelps complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by finding no constitutional irregularities in the New Life Burbank Session&#x27;s ordination of Lee Irons as a ruling elder, despite PP&#x27;s earlier refusal to receive Irons as a teaching-elder candidate. The SJC denied the complaint. Under BCO 39-3.3, the Court owed great deference to the lower court&#x27;s discretionary fitness judgment; the single office of elder does not require identical eligibility processes, and the NLB Session had jurisdiction after Irons renounced OPC jurisdiction. PP&#x27;s action stood; the SJC declined to decide the NAPARC issue.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-24" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
<div class="judicial-case__topics" aria-label="Topic tags"><span class="judicial-case__topics-label">Topics</span><span class="judicial-pill">ruling elder ordination</span><span class="judicial-pill">teaching elder ordination</span><span class="judicial-pill">OPC discipline</span><span class="judicial-case__topics-extra" id="judicial-topics-2009-24" hidden><span class="judicial-pill">one office two forms</span><span class="judicial-pill">renunciation of jurisdiction</span><span class="judicial-pill">NAPARC</span><span class="judicial-pill">presbytery discretion</span></span><button type="button" class="judicial-topics__toggle" aria-controls="judicial-topics-2009-24" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Show 4 more topics" data-topic-count="4">+4 topics</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2009-25" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2009-25 Brown v. Northern California" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2009-25: Brown v. Northern California, M39GA, pp. 548–567" data-search-text="2009-25 Brown v. Northern California Presbytery Brown challenged Presbytery’s abstract approval of six views concerning diaconal practice. The SJC sustained the consolidated complaints and annulled Presbytery’s action because a church court cannot issue a binding decree apart from properly exercising jurisdiction over specific persons. Constitutional conformity must instead be determined through authorized examination or judicial processes. The judgment deliberately left unresolved whether any of the six views themselves were faithful to the Constitution; the detailed view-by-view analysis appeared only in a concurring opinion. complaint Sustained; Annulled Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 9-7, BCO 11-4, BCO 12-5, BCO 13-9, BCO 14-6, BCO 14-7, BCO 16-2, BCO 21-5, BCO 24-6, BCO 31-1, BCO 40-1, BCO 40-2.3, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 43-10, BCO 9-1, BCO 9-2, BCO 9-3, BCO 9-4, BCO 31-2, BCO 32-2, BCO 32-3, BCO 35-7, BCO 5-8.3, BCO 17-1 diaconate deaconess women in church office in thesi statement abstract decree presbyterial jurisdiction BCO 9-7 appointed deaconess elected deaconess equal partners nobody ordained GUMP standard Kniseley standard">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-25</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga39_2011__2009-25_2009-26.html">Brown v. Northern California Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2009-25">Brown challenged Presbytery’s abstract approval of six views concerning diaconal practice. The SJC sustained the consolidated complaints and annulled Presbytery’s action because a church court cannot issue a binding decree apart from properly exercising jurisdiction over specific persons. Constitutional conformity must instead be determined through authorized examination or judicial processes. The judgment deliberately left unresolved whether any of the six views themselves were faithful to the Constitution; the detailed view-by-view analysis appeared only in a concurring opinion.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2009-25" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2009-27</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__stub_2009-27.html">Cutler v. Platte Valley</a></h3></header>

<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-01 Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-01: Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia, M37GA, pp. 176–193" data-search-text="2008-01 Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia Presbytery Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices, applied a three-part inquiry, and deferred to Presbytery on the candidate’s credible vow. Because complainants identified no violated doctrinal standard, no error was shown. The ruling reaffirmed that the BCO bars ordaining women as deacons. complaint Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2008-1 BCO 7-2, BCO 9-3, BCO 21-4, BCO 39-3 ordination licensure women deacons stated difference confessional subscription">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-01_2008-10.html">Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-01">Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices, applied a three-part inquiry, and deferred to Presbytery on the candidate’s credible vow. Because complainants identified no violated doctrinal standard, no error was shown. The ruling reaffirmed that the BCO bars ordaining women as deacons.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-09 Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church v. Evangel" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-09: Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church v. Evangel, M37GA, pp. 193–200" data-search-text="2008-09 Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church v. Evangel Presbytery Red Mountain Session challenged Presbytery’s ruling that it had inadequately addressed a member’s demand to declare his wife’s divorce unbiblical, and Presbytery’s resulting declaration and Matthew 18 instruction. The SJC sustained all four issues and reversed Presbytery. It held Session’s context-sensitive ruling disclosed no clear error, use of BCO 31-2 was reasonable, Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by allowing its commission to revise a report after floor discussion, and Presbytery judged the wife without due process. The SJC expressly did not decide whether biblical divorce grounds existed. complaint Sustained; Reversed Not stated legacy 2008-9 BCO 31-2, BCO 15-3 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-09.html">Session of Red Mountain Presbyterian Church v. Evangel Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-09">Red Mountain Session challenged Presbytery’s ruling that it had inadequately addressed a member’s demand to declare his wife’s divorce unbiblical, and Presbytery’s resulting declaration and Matthew 18 instruction. The SJC sustained all four issues and reversed Presbytery. It held Session’s context-sensitive ruling disclosed no clear error, use of BCO 31-2 was reasonable, Presbytery violated BCO 15-3 by allowing its commission to revise a report after floor discussion, and Presbytery judged the wife without due process. The SJC expressly did not decide whether biblical divorce grounds existed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
<div class="judicial-case__topics" aria-label="Topic tags"><span class="judicial-case__topics-label">Topics</span><span class="judicial-muted">None listed</span></div>
</div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-10 Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-10: Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia, M37GA, pp. 176–193" data-search-text="2008-10 Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery The complaint challenged Presbytery’s approval of a candidate who believed women could hold the diaconal office but promised to follow the BCO, which permits only men to be ordained as deacons. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed approval of his ordination examination. It held that a BCO difference is evaluated through compliance, doctrinal, and ordination-vow inquiries; the record supported compliance and a credible vow, while complainants had not identified violated doctrinal standards. Absent contrary evidence, Presbytery’s judgment received deference. complaint Denied; Affirmed Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 7-2, BCO 9-3, BCO 21-4, BCO 39-3 ordination licensure women deacons stated difference confessional subscription">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-10</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2008-01_2008-10.html">Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-10">The complaint challenged Presbytery’s approval of a candidate who believed women could hold the diaconal office but promised to follow the BCO, which permits only men to be ordained as deacons. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed approval of his ordination examination. It held that a BCO difference is evaluated through compliance, doctrinal, and ordination-vow inquiries; the record supported compliance and a credible vow, while complainants had not identified violated doctrinal standards. Absent contrary evidence, Presbytery’s judgment received deference.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
<div class="judicial-case__topics" aria-label="Topic tags"><span class="judicial-case__topics-label">Topics</span><span class="judicial-pill">ordination</span><span class="judicial-pill">licensure</span><span class="judicial-pill">women deacons</span><span class="judicial-case__topics-extra" id="judicial-topics-2008-10" hidden><span class="judicial-pill">stated difference</span><span class="judicial-pill">confessional subscription</span></span><button type="button" class="judicial-topics__toggle" aria-controls="judicial-topics-2008-10" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Show 2 more topics" data-topic-count="2">+2 topics</button></div>
</div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-11 Broadwater et al. v. Chesapeake" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-11: Broadwater et al. v. Chesapeake, M38GA, pp. 130–133" data-search-text="2008-11 Broadwater et al. v. Chesapeake Presbytery Presbytery empowered a commission both to assume original jurisdiction over matters involving church members and to receive a Session&#x27;s reference concerning a membership transfer. The SJC vacated the original-jurisdiction mandate because Presbytery had neither found that the Session refused to act nor required the commission to make that finding before proceeding. The authority to receive the reference remained intact; requests from other Sessions alone did not satisfy BCO 33-1. complaint Partially sustained; Vacated Not stated — BCO 33-1 original jurisdiction presbytery commission session authority church discipline BCO 33-1 original jurisdiction conditions">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-11.html">Broadwater et al. v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Vacated</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-11">Presbytery empowered a commission both to assume original jurisdiction over matters involving church members and to receive a Session&#x27;s reference concerning a membership transfer. The SJC vacated the original-jurisdiction mandate because Presbytery had neither found that the Session refused to act nor required the commission to make that finding before proceeding. The authority to receive the reference remained intact; requests from other Sessions alone did not satisfy BCO 33-1.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-14" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-14 White v. Siouxlands" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-14: White v. Siouxlands, M38GA, pp. 135–150" data-search-text="2008-14 White v. Siouxlands Presbytery A minister complained that his presbytery wrongly refused to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister’s Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 31-2, BCO 31-5, BCO 31-7, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-2, BCO 35-1, BCO 35-3, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 40-4, BCO 40-5, BCO 8-2 BCO 31-2 investigation Federal Vision theology Covenant of Works presbytery oversight duty hearsay judicial investigation Westminster Standards appellate deference BCO 39-3 great discretion New Perspective on Paul">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-14</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-14.html">White v. Siouxlands Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-14">A minister complained that his presbytery wrongly refused to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister’s Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-14" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-15" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-15 Smith v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-15: Smith v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 177–180" data-search-text="2008-15 Morton Smith v. Western Carolina The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session majority had validly canceled the meeting. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls therefore remained undissolved and Neville was uncalled, absent later congregational action. The SJC also upheld Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation as unwise and its refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation. complaint Partially sustained Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 38-1, BCO 36-5, BCO 37-3, BCO 27-5, BCO 24-7, BCO 40-2, BCO 13-9, BCO 15-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 40-5 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-15</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html">Morton Smith v. Western Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-15">The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session majority had validly canceled the meeting. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls therefore remained undissolved and Neville was uncalled, absent later congregational action. The SJC also upheld Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation as unwise and its refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-15" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-16" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-16 Hutchinson and Bulkeley v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-16: Hutchinson and Bulkeley v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 189–190" data-search-text="2008-16 Hutchinson &amp; Bulkeley v. Western Carolina Ministers challenged Presbytery’s handling of RE Payne’s confession as a BCO 38-1 case without process, asking the SJC to declare it incomplete and require prosecution of additional alleged sins. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a complaint cannot bypass the BCO 33-1 and 34-1 procedures by seeking relief akin to original jurisdiction. Further allegations could be filed as formal charges with Payne’s Session, which could investigate, prosecute, or reference the matter to a higher court. complaint Denied; Affirmed Not stated — BCO 31-2, BCO 33-1, BCO 34-1, BCO 38-1, BCO 39-3 case without process confession indefinite suspension institution of process discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-16</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html">Hutchinson &amp; Bulkeley v. Western Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-16">Ministers challenged Presbytery’s handling of RE Payne’s confession as a BCO 38-1 case without process, asking the SJC to declare it incomplete and require prosecution of additional alleged sins. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a complaint cannot bypass the BCO 33-1 and 34-1 procedures by seeking relief akin to original jurisdiction. Further allegations could be filed as formal charges with Payne’s Session, which could investigate, prosecute, or reference the matter to a higher court.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-17" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-17 Hutchinson and Bulkeley v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-17: Hutchinson and Bulkeley v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 156–181" data-search-text="2008-17 Hutchinson &amp; Bulkeley v. Western Carolina Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s decision to suspend RE Neill Payne indefinitely from office but not from the Sacraments. The SJC did not sustain the complaint: BCO 30-3 expressly permits suspension from office without sacramental suspension, and no provision requires both censures together. Because the appropriate censure involved discretion and judgment, the SJC deferred absent clear error. Authority to remove or increase Payne’s censure had returned to his Session. complaint Partially sustained Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) — BCO 58-4, BCO 58-2, BCO 30-3, BCO 37-3, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 38-1, BCO 36-5 ecclesiastical discipline sacrament suspension ruling elder conduct censure appropriateness deference to presbytery discretionary judgment">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-17</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html">Hutchinson &amp; Bulkeley v. Western Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-17">Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s decision to suspend RE Neill Payne indefinitely from office but not from the Sacraments. The SJC did not sustain the complaint: BCO 30-3 expressly permits suspension from office without sacramental suspension, and no provision requires both censures together. Because the appropriate censure involved discretion and judgment, the SJC deferred absent clear error. Authority to remove or increase Payne’s censure had returned to his Session.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-17" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2008-18" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2008-18 Hutchinson and Bulkeley v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2008-18: Hutchinson and Bulkeley v. Western Carolina, M38GA, pp. 156–181" data-search-text="2008-18 Hutchinson &amp; Bulkeley v. Western Carolina Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s refusal to condemn RE Neill Payne’s views in a circulated “Africa e-mail.” The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a presbytery may not condemn a church officer’s allegedly erroneous opinions without due process and that four sentences, an approving newspaper reference, and the Commission’s summary did not present Payne’s views fully enough for responsible adjudication. The SJC rejected race or intelligence as the primary determinant of a nation’s fate, while allowing the e-mail to be used as evidence in formal charges. complaint Partially sustained Not stated — BCO 38-1, BCO 24-6.4 erroneous opinions due process racism church discipline racial views">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2008-18</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga38_2010__2008-15_2008-16_2008-17_2008-18_2009-01_2009-03.html">Hutchinson &amp; Bulkeley v. Western Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2008-18">Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s refusal to condemn RE Neill Payne’s views in a circulated “Africa e-mail.” The SJC did not sustain the complaint. It held that a presbytery may not condemn a church officer’s allegedly erroneous opinions without due process and that four sentences, an approving newspaper reference, and the Commission’s summary did not present Payne’s views fully enough for responsible adjudication. The SJC rejected race or intelligence as the primary determinant of a nation’s fate, while allowing the e-mail to be used as evidence in formal charges.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2008-18" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-01 Lee v. Korean Eastern" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-01: Lee v. Korean Eastern, M36GA, pp. 96–97" data-search-text="2007-01 Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery Lee challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s actions affecting his interim pastoral relationship, alleging that its October 3, 2006 meeting lacked a quorum. The SJC held the complaint moot and declared every action taken at that meeting null and void—not merely those concerning his church. The meeting opened with only two ruling elders when three were required, and the minutes did not establish when a quorum was later achieved; its presence therefore could not be presumed. complaint Partially sustained Not stated legacy 2007-1 BCO 20-6, BCO 21-9, BCO 22-6 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html">Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-01">Lee challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s actions affecting his interim pastoral relationship, alleging that its October 3, 2006 meeting lacked a quorum. The SJC held the complaint moot and declared every action taken at that meeting null and void—not merely those concerning his church. The meeting opened with only two ruling elders when three were required, and the minutes did not establish when a quorum was later achieved; its presence therefore could not be presumed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-02 Malone v. Metro NY" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-02: Malone v. Metro NY, M36GA, pp. 99–107" data-search-text="2007-02 Malone v. Metro NY Malone challenged Presbytery’s approval of a commission’s judgment and indefinite suspension imposed without process. The SJC sustained the complaint in part and vacated the judgment and censure: the commission had authority only to investigate, and Malone’s general acknowledgments neither confessed specific charges nor showed intent to waive process under BCO 38-1. Presbytery could begin anew under proper procedures. The SJC rejected Malone’s claim that suggested steps evidencing repentance improperly bound him, treating them as noncompulsory pastoral advice. complaint Partially sustained; Vacated Not stated legacy 2007-2 BCO 36-5, BCO 38-1 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-02.html">Malone v. Metro NY</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Vacated</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-02">Malone challenged Presbytery’s approval of a commission’s judgment and indefinite suspension imposed without process. The SJC sustained the complaint in part and vacated the judgment and censure: the commission had authority only to investigate, and Malone’s general acknowledgments neither confessed specific charges nor showed intent to waive process under BCO 38-1. Presbytery could begin anew under proper procedures. The SJC rejected Malone’s claim that suggested steps evidencing repentance improperly bound him, treating them as noncompulsory pastoral advice.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-04 Engel v. Evangel" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-04: Engel v. Evangel, M36GA, pp. 108–112" data-search-text="2007-04 Stephen P. Engel v. Evangel Presbytery A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to decide his guilt or innocence and its failure to return charges after his Session suspended him from the sacraments without trial or confession. The SJC sustained the complaint on the remand issue: rescission of the censure did not dispose of pending charges, so Presbytery had to rehear the complaint and require the Session either to institute proper process or dismiss them. It declined to determine guilt without a trial record and rejected the claim that the censure’s prescribed form willfully took the Lord’s name in vain. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2007-4 BCO 42-9, BCO 43-10 appeal suspension from sacraments due process trial censure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-04.html">Stephen P. Engel v. Evangel Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-04">A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to decide his guilt or innocence and its failure to return charges after his Session suspended him from the sacraments without trial or confession. The SJC sustained the complaint on the remand issue: rescission of the censure did not dispose of pending charges, so Presbytery had to rehear the complaint and require the Session either to institute proper process or dismiss them. It declined to determine guilt without a trial record and rejected the claim that the censure’s prescribed form willfully took the Lord’s name in vain.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-06 Lee v. Korean Eastern" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-06: Lee v. Korean Eastern, M36GA, pp. 92–99" data-search-text="2007-06 Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery Lee challenged irregular Presbytery meetings, classification of his interim pastorate as stated supply, expiration of his term, and appointment of a Judicial Commission. Meeting-related concerns were moot or resolved by nullification; the SJC otherwise denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. No pastoral call had been approved or installation conducted, and BCO 22-6 limited the stated-supply relationship to one year absent renewal. The ruling approved only the Commission’s appointment, not its later actions, which remained subject to pending complaints. complaint Denied; Affirmed Not stated legacy 2007-6 BCO 15-2 stated supply interim pastor pastoral relationship judicial commission">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html">Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-06">Lee challenged irregular Presbytery meetings, classification of his interim pastorate as stated supply, expiration of his term, and appointment of a Judicial Commission. Meeting-related concerns were moot or resolved by nullification; the SJC otherwise denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. No pastoral call had been approved or installation conducted, and BCO 22-6 limited the stated-supply relationship to one year absent renewal. The ruling approved only the Commission’s appointment, not its later actions, which remained subject to pending complaints.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-01_2007-06_2007-07.html">S. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-07">RE Han challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s treatment of TE Lee as stated supply rather than pastor, its clarification of its earlier action, and its appointment of a Pulpit Commission. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery: Lee lacked an approved pastoral call or installation, “interim pastor” meant stated supply under BCO 22, and his unrenewed one-year term had expired. BCO 15-2 permitted the commission’s appointment to process stated-supply requests. The ruling did not approve or disapprove the commission’s later actions.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-08 Jones v. Louisiana" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-08: Jones v. Louisiana, M36GA, pp. 113–125" data-search-text="2007-08 Jones v. Louisiana Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 2007-8 BCO 21-4, BCO 16-3.e.5, BCO 13-9.f, BCO 40-4, BCO 40-5, BCO 39-3.4, BCO 39-2, BCO 39-3, BCO 13-6, BCO 21-5, BCO 31-2, BCO 13-9, BCO 13-11, BCO 29-1, BCO 5-6, BCO 10-18 constitutional_interpretation differences_with_standards westminster_standards election perseverance apostasy visible_invisible_church baptism presbytery_procedures federal_vision judicial_review church_discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-08.html">Jones v. Louisiana</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-08">Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s decision and the Commission’s resulting actions, and directed return of expended church funds if the congregation requested. Neither the Session nor congregation had requested or consented to that authority. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-10 Lee v. Korean Eastern (2007-09 &amp; 2007-10)" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-10: Lee v. Korean Eastern (2007-09 &amp; 2007-10), M37GA, pp. 132–144" data-search-text="2007-10 Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery (2007-09 &amp; 2007-10) Lee challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s ratification and filing of a New Jersey lawsuit through a commission acting for the local church, seeking civil adjudication of who was the rightful pastor and who could act as the church’s session. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s decision in whole. PCA courts have moral and spiritual, not civil coercive, authority and cannot sue to enforce ecclesiastical decisions. The ruling does not prohibit litigation over purely civil matters and did not condemn the commission’s original appointment. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated — BCO 22-6, BCO 15-2, BCO 13-9, BCO 16-2, BCO 20-2, BCO 3-4, BCO 11-1, BCO 11-2, BCO 11-4, BCO 25-9, BCO 25-10, BCO 25-11, BCO 14-7, BCO 31-2, BCO 13-10 civil litigation by presbytery stated supply interim pastor BCO 22-6 one-year limit hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical denomination pulpit commission presbytery acting on behalf of session civil court jurisdiction over ecclesiastical matters PCA polity non-hierarchical Presbyterianism session autonomy Korean Eastern Presbytery congregational consent">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-11 Lee v. Korean Eastern" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-11: Lee v. Korean Eastern, M37GA, pp. 144–150" data-search-text="2007-11 Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern After Korean Eastern Presbytery tried, convicted, deposed, and excommunicated TE Eliot Lee, the SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the disposition and excommunication. The decisive reason was procedural: the record did not show timely service of the indictment/citations or the required 14-day trial notice, violating BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, the SJC rendered the decision it thought should have been made, finding no strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 justified formal process; it added pastoral counsel, expressly not censure. appeal Sustained; Reversed Not stated — BCO 32-3, BCO 42-9, BCO 31-2 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-11</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-11.html">Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-11">After Korean Eastern Presbytery tried, convicted, deposed, and excommunicated TE Eliot Lee, the SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the disposition and excommunication. The decisive reason was procedural: the record did not show timely service of the indictment/citations or the required 14-day trial notice, violating BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, the SJC rendered the decision it thought should have been made, finding no strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 justified formal process; it added pastoral counsel, expressly not censure.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Southwest Florida A minister complained that Presbytery placed a shepherding committee report containing findings of his alleged “sins and errors” in its minutes and directed that it be read to his congregation. Although a committee may form and record an opinion without judicial process, Presbytery&#x27;s endorsement and public dissemination effectively admonished the minister on unsubstantiated and unproven opinions without due process. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 30-2, BCO 31-2, BCO 39-3 due process admonition shepherding committee judicial procedure">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-13" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-13 Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-13: Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain, M37GA, pp. 150–163" data-search-text="2007-13 David Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery On complaint from TE David Kniseley and others, the SJC reviewed Rocky Mountain Presbytery&#x27;s refusal to forbid a mission church from giving an unordained female staff member the title &#x27;Minister of Church Life.&#x27; The SJC denied the complaint. It held the BCO uses &#x27;minister&#x27; synonymously with pastor and teaching elder, but is silent on general use for non-ordained staff; a lower court may exercise discretion subject to BCO 40-2(3)&#x27;s WESP review. The decision addressed only the constitutional issue, not the title&#x27;s wisdom or propriety; four commissioners dissented. complaint Denied Not stated — BCO 1-4, BCO 7-2, BCO 9-3, BCO 40-2, BCO 39-3 minister title non-ordained staff women constitutional interpretation presbytery judgment">

Rocky Mountain Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-13">On complaint from TE David Kniseley and others, the SJC reviewed Rocky Mountain Presbytery&#x27;s refusal to forbid a mission church from giving an unordained female staff member the title &#x27;Minister of Church Life.&#x27; The SJC denied the complaint. It held the BCO uses &#x27;minister&#x27; synonymously with pastor and teaching elder, but is silent on general use for non-ordained staff; a lower court may exercise discretion subject to BCO 40-2(3)&#x27;s WESP review. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-14" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-14 PCA v. Louisiana (Trial)" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-14: PCA v. Louisiana (Trial), M36GA, pp. 131–137" data-search-text="2007-14 PCA v. Louisiana Presbytery (Trial) In this BCO 40-5 proceeding over Louisiana Presbytery’s investigation of TE Stephen Wilkins, the SJC dismissed Specification 1 because it could not find that the cited procedures were constitutionally required or that guilt was proved. The dismissal did not erase concerns about undocumented doctrinal findings; those failures were covered by Specification 2. On Presbytery’s guilty plea to that specification, the SJC imposed a public admonition for failing to find a strong presumption of doctrinal guilt and pursue trial. Wilkins’s and his church’s withdrawal made practical amends unavailable. bco_40_5_matter Guilty; Dismissed BCO 40-5 — important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceeding — BCO 38-3, BCO 32-3, BCO 21-4, BCO 31-2, BCO 29-1, BCO 34-5, BCO 36-3, BCO 13-9, BCO 40-4, BCO 39-3, BCO 27-3, BCO 40-5, BCO 15-4, BCO 13-9.f, BCO 34-1, BCO 32-17, BCO 15-3, BCO 40-6, BCO 13-3 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-14</code> <span>· BCO 40-5 matter</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga36_2008__2007-14.html">PCA v. Louisiana Presbytery (Trial)</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Guilty; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-14">In this BCO 40-5 proceeding over Louisiana Presbytery’s investigation of TE Stephen Wilkins, the SJC dismissed Specification 1 because it could not find that the cited procedures were constitutionally required or that guilt was proved. The dismissal did not erase concerns about undocumented doctrinal findings; those failures were covered by Specification 2. On Presbytery’s guilty plea to that specification, the SJC imposed a public admonition for failing to find a strong presumption of doctrinal guilt and pursue trial. Wilkins’s and his church’s withdrawal made practical amends unavailable.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-14" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2007-16" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2007-16 Grady v. Southwest Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2007-16: Grady v. Southwest Florida, M37GA, pp. 163–176" data-search-text="2007-16 Grady v. Southwest Florida A minister appealed convictions and indefinite suspension arising from conflict over Presbytery&#x27;s direction that he resign. The SJC upheld all three convictions, finding two procedural errors nonprejudicial and rejecting the other preserved challenges. But Presbytery could not treat its authority to dissolve a pastoral relationship as authority to compel resignation on pain of discipline. The SJC therefore vacated the censure and dissolution of the call and remanded for reconsideration of censure; Grady&#x27;s separate administrative suspension remained effective. appeal Affirmed; Reversed; Vacated; Remanded Great deference unless clear error (factual findings) — BCO 13-9.c, BCO 21-5, BCO 31-10, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-13, BCO 32-20, BCO 34-9, BCO 35-3, BCO 35-5, BCO 35-10, BCO 39-3, BCO 40-5, BCO 43-2 Appeal Ministerial discipline Presbyterial jurisdiction Due process Censure and suspension Constitutional interpretation Judicial procedure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2007-16</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga37_2009__2007-16.html">Grady v. Southwest Florida</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Affirmed; Reversed; Vacated; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2007-16">A minister appealed convictions and indefinite suspension arising from conflict over Presbytery&#x27;s direction that he resign. The SJC upheld all three convictions, finding two procedural errors nonprejudicial and rejecting the other preserved challenges. But Presbytery could not treat its authority to dissolve a pastoral relationship as authority to compel resignation on pain of discipline. The SJC therefore vacated the censure and dissolution of the call and remanded for reconsideration of censure; Grady&#x27;s separate administrative suspension remained effective.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2007-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2006-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2006-06 Ehrlich v. North Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2006-06: Ehrlich v. North Georgia, M35GA, pp. 77–81" data-search-text="2006-06 Ehrlich v. North Georgia Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the instruction in force. It held that liberty of conscience does not eliminate members’ obligation to obey lawful church injunctions. Here the members had sought the Session’s advice, Presbytery had found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses, and renewed circulation would disturb the church’s peace; under those circumstances, the Session acted within its authority. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 2006-6 BCO 31-2, BCO 29-1.4, BCO 15-3, BCO 41-5, BCO 12-5, BCO 57-5, BCO 42-6, BCO 42-6.b, BCO 30-3 liberty of conscience peace and purity of the church membership vows church discipline session authority letter distribution pastoral misconduct investigation">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2006-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__2006-06.html">Ehrlich v. North Georgia</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2006-06">Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the instruction in force. It held that liberty of conscience does not eliminate members’ obligation to obey lawful church injunctions. Here the members had sought the Session’s advice, Presbytery had found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses, and renewed circulation would disturb the church’s peace; under those circumstances, the Session acted within its authority.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2006-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2006-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2006-07 Chastain v. Heritage" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2006-07: Chastain v. Heritage, M35GA, pp. 81–82" data-search-text="2006-07 Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline. appeal Out of order (type not stated) Not reached legacy 2006-7 None listed ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2006-07</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga35_2007__2006-07.html">Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Out of order (type not stated)</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2006-07">Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2006-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2005-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2005-08 Kim v. Korean Eastern" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2005-08: Kim v. Korean Eastern, M34GA, pp. 131–138" data-search-text="2005-08 Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery A minister appealed convictions for contumacy and threatening elders with civil litigation, plus deposition and excommunication. The SJC sustained contumacy as failure to remain subject to the brethren under the ordination vow, not BCO 32-6-type contumacy. It sustained deposition but found excommunication excessive given the conflict and replaced it with indefinite suspension from the sacraments. It did not sustain the threat conviction because the attorney’s letter was absent from the record. A dissent disputed the contumacy ruling. appeal Not sustained Not stated legacy 2005-8 BCO 21-5, BCO 27-3, BCO 27-4, BCO 30-3, BCO 32-6, BCO 34-4, BCO 39-3.3, BCO 42-6, BCO 46-8, BCO 33-2, BCO 32-6.type contumacy deposition excommunication suspension from sacraments pastoral dissolution ordination vow subjection to brethren censure severity due process">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2005-08</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2005-08.html">Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2005-08">A minister appealed convictions for contumacy and threatening elders with civil litigation, plus deposition and excommunication. The SJC sustained contumacy as failure to remain subject to the brethren under the ordination vow, not BCO 32-6-type contumacy. It sustained deposition but found excommunication excessive given the conflict and replaced it with indefinite suspension from the sacraments. It did not sustain the threat conviction because the attorney’s letter was absent from the record. A dissent disputed the contumacy ruling.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2005-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Eastern (Complaint), M34GA, pp. 139–148" data-search-text="2005-09 Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery (Complaint) A minister challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaints concerning a congregational petition and an Administrative Commission’s actions. The SJC sustained both issues: the petition should first have gone to the Session, and Presbytery and its Commission committed additional constitutional errors. Those errors did not excuse his refusal to obey Presbytery, however. Because he had been deposed in Case 2005-8, further action was moot; the SJC granted no remedy, vacatur, or remand. complaint Sustained; Moot Not stated legacy 2005-9 BCO 13-9, BCO 15-1, BCO 15-2, BCO 15-3, BCO 25-2, BCO 32-6, BCO 33-2, BCO 34-4, BCO 43-2 administrative commission judicial commission congregational meeting original jurisdiction contumacy complaint procedure pastoral dissolution constitutional authority due process">

<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2004-02">A member suspended from the Lord&#x27;s Table appealed after Presbytery let the Session resume her trial and failed to lift all suspensions. The SJC sustained the appeal, finding the Session&#x27;s premature censure, truncated trial, and prosecutor-judge conflict manifested prejudice and made a fair trial impossible. It set aside all judgments and censures, treated the November 13, 2003 communion letter as non-censuring advice, and did not remand.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2004-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2004-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2004-03 Harris v. Heritage" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2004-03: Harris v. Heritage, M33GA, pp. 128–129" data-search-text="2004-03 Tim J. Harris v. Heritage Presbytery A church member challenged Heritage Presbytery&#x27;s ruling that the BCO neither expressly nor implicitly requires a congregation to approve changes in a pastor&#x27;s call, and that it does not require the session to publicize budget details. The SJC held the BCO silent on both points: once the original call and terms are approved, later changes are budgetary and belong to the session under BCO 12-5b; publicizing the budget is prudent but not mandated. The complaint was not sustained; seven commissioners dissented, arguing congregational approval follows by good and necessary consequence. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 2004-3 BCO 20-6, BCO 21-6.4, BCO 23-1, BCO 12-5, BCO 12-5.b ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2004-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-03.html">Tim J. Harris v. Heritage Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2004-03">A church member challenged Heritage Presbytery&#x27;s ruling that the BCO neither expressly nor implicitly requires a congregation to approve changes in a pastor&#x27;s call, and that it does not require the session to publicize budget details. The SJC held the BCO silent on both points: once the original call and terms are approved, later changes are budgetary and belong to the session under BCO 12-5b; publicizing the budget is prudent but not mandated. The complaint was not sustained; seven commissioners dissented, arguing congregational approval follows by good and necessary consequence.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2004-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2004-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2004-05 Blevins v. Westminster" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2004-05: Blevins v. Westminster, M33GA, pp. 131–137" data-search-text="2004-05 Blevins v. Westminster SJC sustained TE Philip Blevins&#x27;s complaint against Westminster Presbytery, holding the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely despite the commission&#x27;s February 3, 2004 untimeliness ruling. The wife&#x27;s April 2003 letter was essentially a BCO 35-13 request to review new evidence, and the Session&#x27;s May 2003 denial was a new complaintable decision. The SJC did not decide the wife&#x27;s divorce grounds or the Session&#x27;s merits; it remanded for Presbytery to rehear the Session and Warhurst complaints with the Blevins/Seufert merits considered. A concurrence added that no full new trial is required. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 2004-5 BCO 35-13, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2 Procedural - Timeliness of Complaint Divorce and Biblical Grounds Censure and Church Discipline New Evidence in Judicial Cases">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2004-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-05.html">Blevins v. Westminster</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2004-05">SJC sustained TE Philip Blevins&#x27;s complaint against Westminster Presbytery, holding the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely despite the commission&#x27;s February 3, 2004 untimeliness ruling. The wife&#x27;s April 2003 letter was essentially a BCO 35-13 request to review new evidence, and the Session&#x27;s May 2003 denial was a new complaintable decision. The SJC did not decide the wife&#x27;s divorce grounds or the Session&#x27;s merits; it remanded for Presbytery to rehear the Session and Warhurst complaints with the Blevins/Seufert merits considered. A concurrence added that no full new trial is required.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2004-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

The SJC sustained the session&#x27;s complaint: BCO 25-2 permits a session to add agenda items, and BCO 24-6 does not require a member-initiated motion; the congregation&#x27;s own 503–229 vote began the process. Westminster Presbytery Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority. complaint Sustained Great deference unless clear error (discretion and judgment) legacy 2004-8 BCO 13-2, BCO 16-1, BCO 16-2, BCO 20-10, BCO 21-1, BCO 34-1, BCO 34-2, BCO 34-10, BCO 38-1, BCO 38-2, BCO 39-3 pastoral call approval presbytery discretion divestiture without censure BCO 34-10 administrative remedy congregation right to elect pastor BCO 20-10 vs 21-1 Preliminary Principle 6 minister without call">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2004-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga34_2006__2004-08.html">Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2004-08">Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2004-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2004-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2004-09 Robar v. Central Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2004-09: Robar v. Central Carolina, M33GA, pp. 144–146" data-search-text="2004-09 Scott Robar v. Central Carolina Presbytery The SJC found RE Scott Robar&#x27;s appeal from Central Carolina Presbytery judicially out of order and dismissed it because he filed his notice of appeal only with Presbytery&#x27;s stated clerk, not also with the General Assembly&#x27;s stated clerk as BCO 42-4 requires. No merits review of his conviction occurred. Four commissioners dissented, arguing that the presbytery clerk&#x27;s admittedly incorrect advice, Robar&#x27;s reliance, and Presbytery&#x27;s request to treat the appeal as timely should excuse the filing defect under the Plowman precedent and equity or estoppel principles. appeal Judicially out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 2004-9 BCO 42-4, BCO 13-9, BCO 31-2 Appeal procedure Filing requirements Jurisdictional defect Notice of appeal Equitable estoppel Procedural fairness">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2004-09</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2004-09.html">Scott Robar v. Central Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2004-09">The SJC found RE Scott Robar&#x27;s appeal from Central Carolina Presbytery judicially out of order and dismissed it because he filed his notice of appeal only with Presbytery&#x27;s stated clerk, not also with the General Assembly&#x27;s stated clerk as BCO 42-4 requires. No merits review of his conviction occurred. Four commissioners dissented, arguing that the presbytery clerk&#x27;s admittedly incorrect advice, Robar&#x27;s reliance, and Presbytery&#x27;s request to treat the appeal as timely should excuse the filing defect under the Plowman precedent and equity or estoppel principles.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2004-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<section class="judicial-year" data-judicial-year="2003"><h2>2003</h2>
<div class="judicial-year__records">
<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2003-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2003-01 Chavalas v. Northern Illinois" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2003-01: Chavalas v. Northern Illinois, M32GA, pp. 105–106" data-search-text="2003-01 Mark Chavalas v. Northern Illinois Presbytery Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. Chavalas’s later resignation did not abandon the appeal because he had appealed beforehand after a regular trial; no rebuke was issued. appeal Sustained Not stated legacy 2003-1 BCO 42-7, BCO 35-7 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2003-01</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-01.html">Mark Chavalas v. Northern Illinois Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2003-01">Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. Chavalas’s later resignation did not abandon the appeal because he had appealed beforehand after a regular trial; no rebuke was issued.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2003-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2003-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2003-02 Thornton v. Westminster" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2003-02: Thornton v. Westminster, M33GA, pp. 99–107" data-search-text="2003-02 Thornton v. Westminster Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s investigation of TE Frank Smith’s secret recording and its refusal to institute process. The SJC remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation because Presbytery had not timely obtained the other participant’s testimony or examined relevant legal and confessional questions. It rejected claims concerning alleged lying and threats, partiality, and an unbiblical recording policy. The invitation of an outside voluntary prosecutor was moot because he declined; only a separate concurrence found the invitation improper. complaint Remanded Not reached legacy 2003-2 BCO 31-2, BCO 31-6, BCO 31-9, BCO 39-2, BCO 3-3 investigation procedures secret recording of conversations witness testimony prosecutor qualifications partiality and bias discipline procedures">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2003-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-02_2003-05.html">Thornton v. Westminster</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2003-02">Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s investigation of TE Frank Smith’s secret recording and its refusal to institute process. The SJC remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation because Presbytery had not timely obtained the other participant’s testimony or examined relevant legal and confessional questions. It rejected claims concerning alleged lying and threats, partiality, and an unbiblical recording policy. The invitation of an outside voluntary prosecutor was moot because he declined; only a separate concurrence found the invitation improper.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2003-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Southwest A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2003-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2003-04 Dr. and Chin v. Covenant" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2003-04: Dr. and Chin v. Covenant, M33GA, pp. 117–118" data-search-text="2003-04 Dr. and Mrs. Frank Chin v. Covenant Presbytery The Chins complained to the SJC after Covenant Presbytery denied their complaint against Covenant Presbyterian Church Session&#x27;s refusal to examine their young children for admission to the Lord&#x27;s Supper. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. Its adopted reasoning held that BCO 57-2 leaves the time for examining young persons to the Session&#x27;s prudence and imposes no mandate to examine every child put forward; if the Session decides the time has come, careful examination is required. The dissent read BCO 57-1 as requiring examination of covenant children seeking admission. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 2003-4 BCO 57-2, BCO 57-1, BCO 15-1 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2003-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-04.html">Dr. and Mrs. Frank Chin v. Covenant Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2003-04">The Chins complained to the SJC after Covenant Presbytery denied their complaint against Covenant Presbyterian Church Session&#x27;s refusal to examine their young children for admission to the Lord&#x27;s Supper. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. Its adopted reasoning held that BCO 57-2 leaves the time for examining young persons to the Session&#x27;s prudence and imposes no mandate to examine every child put forward; if the Session decides the time has come, careful examination is required. The dissent read BCO 57-1 as requiring examination of covenant children seeking admission.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2003-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
