Westminster, M33GA, pp. 99–107" data-search-text="2003-05 Thornton v. Westminster Thornton challenged Presbytery’s investigation and refusal to institute process against Smith over secretly recording Roberts, alleged lying and threats, partiality, and its taping policy. The SJC sustained only the challenge to the secret-taping investigation: the committee failed to interview Roberts before reporting and examine the legal and confessional implications of transcription and destruction. It remanded for a new BCO 31-2 investigation. The other claims lacked sufficient proof; the voluntary-prosecutor issue was moot because Roberts declined. complaint Remanded Not reached legacy 2003-5 BCO 31-2, BCO 31-6, BCO 31-9, BCO 39-3, BCO 39-2, BCO 3-3, BCO 34-1 secret taping phone recording investigation procedure prosecutorial authority voluntary prosecutor partiality judicial process deference to lower courts">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2003-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2003-02_2003-05.html">Thornton v. Westminster</a></h3></header>

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2003-05">Thornton challenged Presbytery’s investigation and refusal to institute process against Smith over secretly recording Roberts, alleged lying and threats, partiality, and its taping policy. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2003-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2003-06 Wright v. Eastern Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2003-06: Wright v. Eastern Carolina, M32GA, pp. 106–113" data-search-text="2003-06 Wright v. Eastern Carolina The SJC found Case 2003-6 judicially out of order because the challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery action was only advice in response to a BCO 41-1 reference from White Oak Session, not a binding or complainable doctrinal decision under BCO 41-3. The underlying dispute—whether elders could hold and teach a broader atonement view—was therefore not reached. The adopted vote was 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, with 1 abstention and 4 absent. The dissent argued Presbytery&#x27;s &#x27;not allowed&#x27; language read as compulsory final disposition. complaint No final disposition in available record Not reached legacy 2003-6 BCO 41-1, BCO 41-3 Reference procedure advisory vs. binding decisions Presbytery advice on doctrinal matters complainability judicial procedure procedural order BCO 41 references">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2003-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2003-06.html">Wright v. Eastern Carolina</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> No final disposition in available record</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2003-06">The SJC found Case 2003-6 judicially out of order because the challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery action was only advice in response to a BCO 41-1 reference from White Oak Session, not a binding or complainable doctrinal decision under BCO 41-3. The underlying dispute—whether elders could hold and teach a broader atonement view—was therefore not reached. The adopted vote was 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, with 1 abstention and 4 absent. The dissent argued Presbytery&#x27;s &#x27;not allowed&#x27; language read as compulsory final disposition.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2003-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Eastern, M31GA, pp. 112–116" data-search-text="2002-01 Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery In a dispute arising from a Korean Eastern Presbytery congregational election, two ruling elders were tried, refused to plead, and were suspended from sacraments and office; KEP denied their appeal, then increased the censures to deposition and excommunication for contumacy. The SJC affirmed KEP&#x27;s denial and the guilt findings, but reversed the increased censures. An appellate court may not increase a censure under BCO 42-9; the trial court retains discretion to remove or increase an indefinite suspension, though the appellate court may recommend a lesser censure. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2002-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2002-03 Nichols and Couch v. James River" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2002-03: Nichols and Couch v. James River, M33GA, pp. 72–98" data-search-text="2002-03 Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery Ruling elders challenged James River Presbytery’s delay in honoring West End’s valid congregational vote to dissolve its pastoral relationship and a three-month salary gift to the pastor. The SJC held that Presbytery lacked a constitutional basis to delay the dissolution, but rejected the challenge to its benevolent use of its own civil funds. Complaints 16-01, 18-01, and 19-01 were judicially out of order; the others were in order. No remand or repayment was ordered. A concurrence cautioned that prompt dissolution is not automatic when objective, justifiable findings support refusal. complaint Partially sustained Not stated legacy 2002-3 BCO 13-9.f, BCO 13-9.c, BCO 14-7, BCO 16-2, BCO 20-4, BCO 23-1, BCO 25-11, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-2.2 dissolution of pastoral relationship presbytery delay complaint procedure salary gift pastoral discretion consolidated judicial cases">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2002-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga33_2005__2001-34_2002-02_2002-03.html">Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2002-03">Ruling elders challenged James River Presbytery’s delay in honoring West End’s valid congregational vote to dissolve its pastoral relationship and a three-month salary gift to the pastor. The SJC held that Presbytery lacked a constitutional basis to delay the dissolution, but rejected the challenge to its benevolent use of its own civil funds. Complaints 16-01, 18-01, and 19-01 were judicially out of order; the others were in order. No remand or repayment was ordered. A concurrence cautioned that prompt dissolution is not automatic when objective, justifiable findings support refusal.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2002-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2002-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2002-05 Plowman v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2002-05: Plowman v. Philadelphia, M32GA, pp. 59–67" data-search-text="2002-05 Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery A church session suspended a member from the Lord&#x27;s Table and found her guilty of contumacy. The chairman of Presbytery&#x27;s Judicial Business Committee advised her that her appeal was out of order; Presbytery later ruled her complaint untimely. The SJC sustained her complaint: she had submitted to regular trial, making her appeal in order under BCO 42-2, and her complaint was timely after Presbytery&#x27;s advice caused the appeal to be renamed. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the appeal. Filing the appeal suspended the Lord&#x27;s Table censure pending final adjudication; the SJC questioned the contumacy ruling. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2002-5 BCO 32-6.b, BCO 33-2, BCO 42-2, BCO 42-3, BCO 42-1, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 15-1, BCO 15-3, BCO 12-3, BCO 12-1, BCO 42-6, BCO 32-6 contumacy right of appeal submission to regular trial timely filing of complaint committee vs commission suspension from Lord&#x27;s Table due process judicial business committee authority">

Tennessee Valley, M32GA, pp. 67–71" data-search-text="2002-09 Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery The SJC denied TE Stuart H. Merriam&#x27;s appeal from Tennessee Valley Presbytery&#x27;s April 20, 2002 conviction on three ordination-vow specifications and its indefinite suspension. It rejected procedural challenges—that the earlier called meeting was improperly convened and that TVP was prejudiced by prior cases—and found no clear error, applying BCO 39-3(2)&#x27;s deference to lower-court factual findings. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2002-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2002-10 Goerig v. Pacific Northwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2002-10: Goerig v. Pacific Northwest, M31GA, pp. 116–119" data-search-text="2002-10 Carolyn Goerig v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery A church member challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery&#x27;s denial of her complaint that Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session had banned her from worship and sought to erase her membership retroactively under BCO 38-4. The SJC sustained the complaint. Because she never joined Covenant PCA, BCO 46-3 left her membership under Faith&#x27;s Session; the Session&#x27;s proposed retroactive erasure did not comply with BCO 38-4&#x27;s pastoral-oversight steps. The Presbytery therefore erred and should have remanded the matter to the Session. No separate merits relief beyond that remand directive appears. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 12-5, BCO 38-4, BCO 46-3, BCO 42-9 membership erasure BCO 38-4 BCO 46-3 transfer of membership ban from worship session spiritual powers due process in membership removal pastoral oversight">

Pacific Northwest Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2002-10">A church member challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery&#x27;s denial of her complaint that Faith Presbyterian Church (Tacoma) Session had banned her from worship and sought to erase her membership retroactively under BCO 38-4. The SJC sustained the complaint. Because she never joined Covenant PCA, BCO 46-3 left her membership under Faith&#x27;s Session; the Session&#x27;s proposed retroactive erasure did not comply with BCO 38-4&#x27;s pastoral-oversight steps. The Presbytery therefore erred and should have remanded the matter to the Session. No separate merits relief beyond that remand directive appears.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2002-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2002-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2002-11 Abshire v. Pacific Northwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2002-11: Abshire v. Pacific Northwest, M31GA, pp. 119–124" data-search-text="2002-11 Brian Abshire v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. A separate sixth issue remained before Presbytery and was not decided. complaint Partially sustained; Denied; Remanded Not stated — BCO 13-12, BCO 31-2, BCO 31-7, BCO 41-3, BCO 12-5.a, BCO 38-4 judicial commission authority complaint procedures BCO 43 exhortation as pastoral counsel suspension from office suspension from sacraments premature appointment of commission notice of called meeting BCO 31-2 investigation">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2002-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2002-11.html">Brian Abshire v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Denied; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2002-11">Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. A separate sixth issue remained before Presbytery and was not decided.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2002-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2002-14" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2002-14 Lachman v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2002-14: Lachman v. Philadelphia, M32GA, pp. 71–78" data-search-text="2002-14 Lachman v. Philadelphia Presbytery A ruling elder convicted by his Session of fifth-, sixth-, and ninth-commandment violations challenged the conviction because the prosecution presented no live witness and relied on his own letters. The SJC denied the appeal and upheld Presbytery&#x27;s affirmance, holding that the documents, Lachman&#x27;s acknowledgments of writing them, and defense witnesses supplied sufficient proof; the Session also followed Matthew 18 with patience. A concurrence urged change-of-venue procedures for small-Session bias cases, but noted Lachman never requested a reference or challenged the court before trial. appeal Denied Not stated — BCO 32-13, BCO 31-8, BCO 32-16, BCO 43-1, BCO 35-13 ruling elder suspension documentary evidence witness requirement Matthew 18 process ninth commandment fifth commandment sixth commandment change of venue references to presbytery fair and impartial trial session as court of original jurisdiction">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2002-16" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2002-16 Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2002-16: Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana, M32GA, pp. 78–103" data-search-text="2002-16 Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana Presbytery The SJC sustained a session&#x27;s timely complaint that Louisiana Presbytery barred one of its members from the Lord&#x27;s Table after assuming original jurisdiction. Under BCO 33-1, a presbytery may assume jurisdiction only when the session &#x27;refuses to act&#x27;; because the session had investigated and found no strong presumption of guilt, it acted, so LAP never acquired jurisdiction. The censure was therefore a nullity, and the member remained under his session. The SJC also held the jurisdictional assumption reviewable despite no timely complaint against it. Three commissioners dissented. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 33-1, BCO 31-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 32-5, BCO 32-4, BCO 32-3, BCO 11-3, BCO 11-4, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 13-12, BCO 34-1 assumption of original jurisdiction BCO 33-1 refuses to act session jurisdiction over members presbytery jurisdiction contumacy Southern Poverty Law Center League of the South Steve Wilkins Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church suspension from Lord&#x27;s Table graded courts timely complaint constitutionality of presbytery action">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2002-16</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga32_2004__2002-16.html">Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2002-16">The SJC sustained a session&#x27;s timely complaint that Louisiana Presbytery barred one of its members from the Lord&#x27;s Table after assuming original jurisdiction. Under BCO 33-1, a presbytery may assume jurisdiction only when the session &#x27;refuses to act&#x27;; because the session had investigated and found no strong presumption of guilt, it acted, so LAP never acquired jurisdiction. The censure was therefore a nullity, and the member remained under his session. The SJC also held the jurisdictional assumption reviewable despite no timely complaint against it. Three commissioners dissented.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2002-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-01 Kim v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-01: Kim v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 115–122" data-search-text="2001-01 Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery The SJC addressed whether a presbytery and its administrative/judicial commission could suspend a local session and assume original jurisdiction over charges against a ruling elder. It answered no: original jurisdiction belonged to the session, and a presbytery cannot &quot;act for&quot; a lower court by replacing congregationally elected elders. Preliminary Principle Six, BCO 16-2, and BCO 31-1/33-1 controlled; the commission&#x27;s interpretation of BCO 13-9 conflicted with those principles. The Presbytery&#x27;s and Commission&#x27;s actions, including the censure approved by Presbytery, were reversed. appeal Sustained; Reversed Not stated legacy 2001-1 BCO 13-9 appeal original jurisdiction Session censure church governance">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-01</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-01.html">Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-01">The SJC addressed whether a presbytery and its administrative/judicial commission could suspend a local session and assume original jurisdiction over charges against a ruling elder. It answered no: original jurisdiction belonged to the session, and a presbytery cannot &quot;act for&quot; a lower court by replacing congregationally elected elders. Preliminary Principle Six, BCO 16-2, and BCO 31-1/33-1 controlled; the commission&#x27;s interpretation of BCO 13-9 conflicted with those principles. The Presbytery&#x27;s and Commission&#x27;s actions, including the censure approved by Presbytery, were reversed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-02 Ryoo v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-02: Ryoo v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 122–124" data-search-text="2001-02 Sang Roo Ryoo v. Korean Capital Korean Capital Presbytery&#x27;s commission tried and suspended a Korean church assistant pastor for heresy and schism after he failed to answer two summonses, and Presbytery upheld the suspension. On appeal, the SJC sustained the procedural challenge because no indictment with witnesses had been served and the record lacked any minutes or hearing for the default judgment, contrary to BCO 32-3. The SJC remanded for a new trial but expressly declined to rule on the citations, default procedure, or merits. appeal Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2001-2 BCO 34-5, BCO 32-3 judicial procedure indictment requirements due process heresy and schism charges suspension from ministry">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-02</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-02.html">Sang Roo Ryoo v. Korean Capital</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-02">Korean Capital Presbytery&#x27;s commission tried and suspended a Korean church assistant pastor for heresy and schism after he failed to answer two summonses, and Presbytery upheld the suspension. On appeal, the SJC sustained the procedural challenge because no indictment with witnesses had been served and the record lacked any minutes or hearing for the default judgment, contrary to BCO 32-3. The SJC remanded for a new trial but expressly declined to rule on the citations, default procedure, or merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-03 Kim v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-03: Kim v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 124–127" data-search-text="2001-03 Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery A minister suspended for five years after a default judgment of heresy and schism appealed to the SJC. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, holding the judicial commission did not follow BCO 32 and 34: no indictment was served, and the record lacked minutes or evidence of a hearing. It remanded to Korean Capital Presbytery for a new trial. The SJC expressly did not reach the merits, the adequacy of the citations, or whether default judgment is proper. appeal Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 2001-3 BCO 32-3, BCO 32-4, BCO 34-5 appeal due process indictment trial procedure ministerial discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-03</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-03.html">Sung Keon Kim v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-03">A minister suspended for five years after a default judgment of heresy and schism appealed to the SJC. It remanded to Korean Capital Presbytery for a new trial. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-06 Kim and Kim v. Korean Eastern" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-06: Kim and Kim v. Korean Eastern, M31GA, pp. 94–101" data-search-text="2001-06 Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery The SJC sustained a complaint by two ruling elders against Korean Eastern Presbytery over a disputed congregational meeting (three commissioners dissented). The session was deadlocked and had not called a requested meeting; KEP&#x27;s administrative commission called and supervised the February 18, 2001 meeting, and KEP approved that action. The SJC reversed both lower-court actions, holding that BCO 25-2 places responsibility on the session and that the presbytery&#x27;s proper course was to adjudicate a complaint under BCO 43, not act for the session. It declined to rule on the meeting&#x27;s legal effect. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 2001-6 BCO 10-4, BCO 13-9, BCO 14-7, BCO 16-2, BCO 11-4, BCO 24-6, BCO 25-2 administrative commission authority congregational meeting session deadlock BCO 13-9 BCO 25-2 Korean church presbytery power limits complaint vs petition civil court and church dispute trustee registration">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-06.html">Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-06">The SJC sustained a complaint by two ruling elders against Korean Eastern Presbytery over a disputed congregational meeting (three commissioners dissented). The session was deadlocked and had not called a requested meeting; KEP&#x27;s administrative commission called and supervised the February 18, 2001 meeting, and KEP approved that action. The SJC reversed both lower-court actions, holding that BCO 25-2 places responsibility on the session and that the presbytery&#x27;s proper course was to adjudicate a complaint under BCO 43, not act for the session. It declined to rule on the meeting&#x27;s legal effect.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-07 Lee v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-07: Lee v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 133–134" data-search-text="2001-07 Andy Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery A complaint challenged Presbytery’s suspension of a church Session and installation of a commission to perform Session functions without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled all subsequent commission actions as the Session insofar as the commission was improperly constituted. Presbytery could not suspend elected officers and replace them without prior consent; later recognition could not cure the defect. The SJC also rejected Presbytery’s objection that a related appeal barred the complaint because the cases presented fundamentally different issues. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 2001-7 BCO 13-9, BCO 41-1 complaint original jurisdiction Session administrative commission congregational consent">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-07.html">Andy Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-07">A complaint challenged Presbytery’s suspension of a church Session and installation of a commission to perform Session functions without prior congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled all subsequent commission actions as the Session insofar as the commission was improperly constituted. Presbytery could not suspend elected officers and replace them without prior consent; later recognition could not cure the defect. The SJC also rejected Presbytery’s objection that a related appeal barred the complaint because the cases presented fundamentally different issues.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-09 Kim v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-09: Kim v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 137–139" data-search-text="2001-09 Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery On appeal from an excommunication, the SJC held that Korean Capital Presbytery and its special judicial commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction to adjudicate charges against a communicant member. Because original jurisdiction belonged to the local session, the Presbytery/commission proceedings against the member were unconstitutional and reversed. The ruling turned only on jurisdiction; it did not decide the truth of the schism and contumacy charges. The excommunication therefore could not stand on that record. appeal Sustained; Reversed Not stated legacy 2001-9 BCO 13-9 appeal original jurisdiction Session church discipline censure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-09</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-09.html">Charles Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-09">On appeal from an excommunication, the SJC held that Korean Capital Presbytery and its special judicial commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction to adjudicate charges against a communicant member. Because original jurisdiction belonged to the local session, the Presbytery/commission proceedings against the member were unconstitutional and reversed. The ruling turned only on jurisdiction; it did not decide the truth of the schism and contumacy charges. The excommunication therefore could not stand on that record.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-11" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-11 Yoo v. Korean Northwest" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-11: Yoo v. Korean Northwest, M30GA, pp. 140–141" data-search-text="2001-11 Byung Han Yoo v. Korean Northwest Presbytery A ruling elder&#x27;s complaint against Korean Northwest Presbytery was found out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-2. The action complained of was taken October 10, 2000, but the complaint was filed March 12, 2001, well outside the 30-day filing period, so the SJC reached no merits question. The case illustrates that a complaint failing BCO 43-2 timeliness is dismissed without adjudication of the underlying presbytery action. complaint Out of order (type not stated); Dismissed Not reached — BCO 43-2 procedural defect untimely filing">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-11</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-11.html">Byung Han Yoo v. Korean Northwest Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Out of order (type not stated); Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-11">A ruling elder&#x27;s complaint against Korean Northwest Presbytery was found out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-2. The action complained of was taken October 10, 2000, but the complaint was filed March 12, 2001, well outside the 30-day filing period, so the SJC reached no merits question. The case illustrates that a complaint failing BCO 43-2 timeliness is dismissed without adjudication of the underlying presbytery action.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-11" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-12" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-12 Lee v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-12: Lee v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 141–142" data-search-text="2001-12 Peter Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery The SJC sustained Deacon Peter Lee’s appeal from Korean Capital Presbytery’s censure and reversed the Presbytery and its special judicial commission for adjudicating charges that belonged to the local Session. Lee, a communicant member, had been suspended from the sacraments for five years after the commission found contumacy and a false statement; Presbytery approved. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a member’s judicial action or censure rests with the Session, not Presbytery or its commission. The reversal was jurisdictional and did not decide the underlying charges. appeal Sustained; Reversed Not stated — BCO 13-9 appeal original jurisdiction Session deacon church discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-12</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-12.html">Peter Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-12">The SJC sustained Deacon Peter Lee’s appeal from Korean Capital Presbytery’s censure and reversed the Presbytery and its special judicial commission for adjudicating charges that belonged to the local Session. Lee, a communicant member, had been suspended from the sacraments for five years after the commission found contumacy and a false statement; Presbytery approved. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a member’s judicial action or censure rests with the Session, not Presbytery or its commission. The reversal was jurisdictional and did not decide the underlying charges.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-12" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Capital Presbytery Deacon Samuel Hong appealed after Korean Capital Presbytery&#x27;s special judicial commission convicted him of contumacy and making a false statement and imposed a two-year suspension from the sacraments. The SJC sustained the appeal, holding that original jurisdiction over charges against a communicant member belongs to the local Session, not Presbytery or its commission, and reversed the Presbytery/commission actions. The SJC did not decide the underlying charges; the reversal was jurisdictional, not an acquittal. One recorded dissent gave no reasons. appeal Sustained; Reversed Not stated — None listed ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-13</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-13.html">Samuel Hong v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-13">Deacon Samuel Hong appealed after Korean Capital Presbytery&#x27;s special judicial commission convicted him of contumacy and making a false statement and imposed a two-year suspension from the sacraments. The SJC sustained the appeal, holding that original jurisdiction over charges against a communicant member belongs to the local Session, not Presbytery or its commission, and reversed the Presbytery/commission actions. The SJC did not decide the underlying charges; the reversal was jurisdictional, not an acquittal. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-14" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-14 Ham v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-14: Ham v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 144–146" data-search-text="2001-14 Moon K. Ham v. Korean Capital Presbytery Ruling Elder Moon K. Ham appealed to the SJC after Korean Capital Presbytery approved a Special Judicial Commission&#x27;s guilty findings for contumacy, church division/destruction, and a false statement, imposing indefinite suspension from the sacraments (called excommunication in the appeal). The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed Presbytery&#x27;s and the Commission&#x27;s actions. Because Ham was a church member, the Session, not Presbytery or its commission, was the proper court of original jurisdiction. The ruling did not remand, acquit, or address the merits. appeal Sustained; Reversed Not stated — BCO 13-9 appeal original jurisdiction Session excommunication church discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-14</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-14.html">Moon K. Ham v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-14">Ruling Elder Moon K. Ham appealed to the SJC after Korean Capital Presbytery approved a Special Judicial Commission&#x27;s guilty findings for contumacy, church division/destruction, and a false statement, imposing indefinite suspension from the sacraments (called excommunication in the appeal). The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed Presbytery&#x27;s and the Commission&#x27;s actions. Because Ham was a church member, the Session, not Presbytery or its commission, was the proper court of original jurisdiction. The ruling did not remand, acquit, or address the merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-14" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Because the appellant was a member of Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington, the presbytery and its commission acted contrary to constitutional standards when they adjudicated the charges and imposed excommunication. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-15</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-15.html">In Mo Chung v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-15">The SJC decided whether a presbytery and its special judicial commission could assume original jurisdiction over disciplinary charges against a church member. It sustained the appeal and reversed: the court of original jurisdiction for communicant members is the local church session. Because the appellant was a member of Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington, the presbytery and its commission acted contrary to constitutional standards when they adjudicated the charges and imposed excommunication. The ruling rested on jurisdiction, not the merits; no remand was ordered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-15" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Capital Presbytery In this SJC appeal, RE Joo Bok Suh challenged Korean Capital Presbytery&#x27;s excommunication after its special judicial commission, rather than his local session, received and adjudicated charges that he had committed contumacy and made a false statement in a civil-court filing. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery/commission action because the court of original jurisdiction over a communicant member is the local session. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-16</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-16.html">Joo Bok Suh v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-16">In this SJC appeal, RE Joo Bok Suh challenged Korean Capital Presbytery&#x27;s excommunication after its special judicial commission, rather than his local session, received and adjudicated charges that he had committed contumacy and made a false statement in a civil-court filing. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery/commission action because the court of original jurisdiction over a communicant member is the local session. The reversal was jurisdictional; the SJC did not rule on the truth of the charges, so it was not an acquittal.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-16" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Capital Presbytery Korean Capital Presbytery approved a three-year suspension from the sacraments after its special judicial commission found RE Choon Soon Lee guilty of contumacy and making a false statement on a civil-court document. On appeal, the SJC sustained and reversed. Because Lee was a communicant member, the Session—not Presbytery or its commission—was the court of original jurisdiction; the commission&#x27;s adjudication therefore violated constitutional standards. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-17</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-17.html">Choon Soon Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-17">Korean Capital Presbytery approved a three-year suspension from the sacraments after its special judicial commission found RE Choon Soon Lee guilty of contumacy and making a false statement on a civil-court document. On appeal, the SJC sustained and reversed. Because Lee was a communicant member, the Session—not Presbytery or its commission—was the court of original jurisdiction; the commission&#x27;s adjudication therefore violated constitutional standards. The SJC did not decide the underlying charges, and one commissioner dissented.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-17" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-18" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-18 Ryoo v. Korean Capital" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-18: Ryoo v. Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 151–154" data-search-text="2001-18 Sang Soo Ryoo v. Korean Capital Presbytery The SJC sustained an assistant pastor’s appeal from a three-year suspension from the sacraments after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission found him guilty of participating in the call of an allegedly unconstitutional presbytery meeting. The decisive defect was procedural: no indictment was served, no prosecutor was clearly appointed, and no trial minutes appeared in the record; service of an indictment with a witness list was critical. The case was remanded for a new trial, and the SJC expressly did not reach the merits or citation adequacy. appeal Sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 13-12, BCO 32-3 Judicial procedures Indictment requirements Due process Service of process Judicial commission procedures Proper citation">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-18</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-18.html">Sang Soo Ryoo v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-18">The SJC sustained an assistant pastor’s appeal from a three-year suspension from the sacraments after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission found him guilty of participating in the call of an allegedly unconstitutional presbytery meeting. The decisive defect was procedural: no indictment was served, no prosecutor was clearly appointed, and no trial minutes appeared in the record; service of an indictment with a witness list was critical. The case was remanded for a new trial, and the SJC expressly did not reach the merits or citation adequacy.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-18" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Capital Presbytery On appeal from a minister’s deposition in a conflicted Korean Capital Presbytery church, the SJC asked whether the commission followed BCO procedures in instituting and conducting judicial process. It sustained the appeal, holding that no indictment appears to have been served and the record lacked minutes showing a trial, contrary to BCO 32-3’s writing, indictment, and service requirements. The SJC remanded to Presbytery for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34. It expressly did not rule on the adequacy of the citations or the merits. appeal Sustained; Remanded Not stated — BCO 32-3, BCO 34-5 appeal deposition due process indictment trial procedure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-19</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-19.html">Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-19">On appeal from a minister’s deposition in a conflicted Korean Capital Presbytery church, the SJC asked whether the commission followed BCO procedures in instituting and conducting judicial process. It sustained the appeal, holding that no indictment appears to have been served and the record lacked minutes showing a trial, contrary to BCO 32-3’s writing, indictment, and service requirements. The SJC remanded to Presbytery for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34. It expressly did not rule on the adequacy of the citations or the merits.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-19" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-25" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-25 Dallison v. North Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-25: Dallison v. North Florida, M30GA, pp. 160–163" data-search-text="2001-25 Anthony Dallison v. North Florida Presbytery After TE Anthony Dallison confessed spousal abuse and received an indefinite suspension, North Florida Presbytery later found him impenitent and deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments. Dallison complained that increasing the censure required fresh charges and trial. The SJC disagreed: his BCO 38-1 confession waived trial rights as to the original charge; the offender then had to satisfy the court of repentance, and the presbytery could investigate and impose higher censure under BCO 37-3, 37-4, 37-8, and 34-4b. The complaint was not sustained. complaint Not sustained; Affirmed Not stated — BCO 37-8, BCO 43-1, BCO 34-8, BCO 36-2, BCO 38-2, BCO 27-4, BCO 38-1, BCO 37-3 ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-25</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-25.html">Anthony Dallison v. North Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-25">After TE Anthony Dallison confessed spousal abuse and received an indefinite suspension, North Florida Presbytery later found him impenitent and deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments. Dallison complained that increasing the censure required fresh charges and trial. The SJC disagreed: his BCO 38-1 confession waived trial rights as to the original charge; the offender then had to satisfy the court of repentance, and the presbytery could investigate and impose higher censure under BCO 37-3, 37-4, 37-8, and 34-4b. The complaint was not sustained.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-25" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-28" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-28 Ball v. Westminster" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-28: Ball v. Westminster, M30GA, pp. 162–172" data-search-text="2001-28 Larry Ball v. Westminster Presbytery A complaint challenged Westminster Presbytery&#x27;s denial of a challenge to its May 15, 2001 plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC answered no: the Presbytery did not err, and denied the complaint. BCO 25&#x27;s local-church withdrawal right and the BCO Preface&#x27;s grassroots principles extend to presbyteries unless expressly excluded, so a presbytery may determine its own membership and affiliation. The plan did not &#x27;act for&#x27; local churches; they retained rights to remain in the PCA or leave, and retained property and internal operations. complaint Not sustained; Affirmed Not stated — BCO 25-11, BCO 11-3, BCO 11-4, BCO 34-1, BCO 33-1, BCO 24-1 presbytery withdrawal ecclesiastical authority civil authority freedom of conscience Presbyterian governance structure grass-roots Presbyterianism property rights local church rights">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-28</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2001-28.html">Larry Ball v. Westminster Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-28">A complaint challenged Westminster Presbytery&#x27;s denial of a challenge to its May 15, 2001 plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC answered no: the Presbytery did not err, and denied the complaint. BCO 25&#x27;s local-church withdrawal right and the BCO Preface&#x27;s grassroots principles extend to presbyteries unless expressly excluded, so a presbytery may determine its own membership and affiliation. The plan did not &#x27;act for&#x27; local churches; they retained rights to remain in the PCA or leave, and retained property and internal operations.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-28" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Evangel Presbytery Third Presbyterian Church asked the SJC to review Evangel Presbytery&#x27;s denial of its complaint against a Presbytery commission&#x27;s binding arbitration award of $57,000 to Covenant Classical School. The SJC ruled the complaint not judicially in order, not denied on the merits: PCA courts may not serve as civil arbitrators, and neither Presbytery nor the SJC may review legally binding arbitration judgments. Church courts may act only as ecclesiastical arbitrators, whose decisions lack civil effect and are reviewable under BCO 43. The case is remanded to the Session, which may retry using the prior indictment or not pursue the matter. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-32" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-32 Christ Covenant Church Session v. Central Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-32: Christ Covenant Church Session v. Central Carolina, M31GA, pp. 107–111" data-search-text="2001-32 Christ Covenant Church Session v. Central Carolina Presbytery Christ Covenant Church Session complained under BCO 43 that Central Carolina Presbytery wrongly annulled the session trial commission&#x27;s judgment and found due-process error concerning H. The SJC did not reach the merits. It held the case not judicially in order because H&#x27;s complaint to the Session was untimely: it exceeded the thirty-day requirement of BCO 43-2 and came more than eighty days after the oral verdict. The ruling thus turned on a procedural gate, making no merits ruling on Presbytery&#x27;s annulment or its due-process rationale. complaint Judicially out of order Not reached — BCO 31-2, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-1 timeliness of complaint BCO 43-2 divorce due process session trial commission 30-day requirement judicially in order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-32</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-32.html">Christ Covenant Church Session v. Central Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Judicially out of order</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-32">Christ Covenant Church Session complained under BCO 43 that Central Carolina Presbytery wrongly annulled the session trial commission&#x27;s judgment and found due-process error concerning H. The SJC did not reach the merits. It held the case not judicially in order because H&#x27;s complaint to the Session was untimely: it exceeded the thirty-day requirement of BCO 43-2 and came more than eighty days after the oral verdict. The ruling thus turned on a procedural gate, making no merits ruling on Presbytery&#x27;s annulment or its due-process rationale.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-32" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-33" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-33 Jr. v. Eastern Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-33: Jr. v. Eastern Carolina, M31GA, pp. 109–111" data-search-text="2001-33 W.W. Marshall Jr. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery A minister challenged Presbytery’s decision to sustain a complaint that rescinded its earlier appellate reversal of a deacon’s conviction and censures. The SJC sustained the minister’s complaint because BCO 43-1 bars a complaint in a judicial case once an appeal has been taken, whether the appeal is past, current, or pending. It reversed Presbytery’s July judgment, restored the April judgment, and remanded to the Session, which could retry the charges using the prior indictment or decline to pursue them. complaint Sustained Not stated — BCO 43-1 complaint in judicial case appeal taken BCO 43-1 deacon discipline presbytery error rescinding judgment">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2001-33</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga31_2003__2001-33.html">W.W. Marshall Jr. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-33">A minister challenged Presbytery’s decision to sustain a complaint that rescinded its earlier appellate reversal of a deacon’s conviction and censures. The SJC sustained the minister’s complaint because BCO 43-1 bars a complaint in a judicial case once an appeal has been taken, whether the appeal is past, current, or pending. It reversed Presbytery’s July judgment, restored the April judgment, and remanded to the Session, which could retry the charges using the prior indictment or decline to pursue them.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-33" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2001-34" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2001-34 Nichols and Couch v. James River" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2001-34: Nichols and Couch v. James River, M33GA, pp. 72–98" data-search-text="2001-34 Nichols and Couch v. James River Presbytery Church members challenged Presbytery’s repeated delay in granting a properly adopted congregational request to dissolve its pastoral relationship and its gift equivalent to three months of the pastor’s compensation. The SJC found seven complaints judicially out of order, sustained the dissolution-delay challenge, and rejected the gift challenge because Presbytery controlled its own civil property. No further relief was ordered. A concurrence would permit delay based on objective, justifiable findings, but concluded that Presbytery’s stated grounds were insufficient. complaint Partially sustained Not stated — BCO 13-9.f, BCO 13-9.c, BCO 14-7, BCO 16-2, BCO 20-4, BCO 23-1, BCO 25-11, BCO 43-1, BCO 43-2, BCO 43-2.2 dissolution of pastoral relationship presbytery delay complaint procedure salary gift consolidated judicial cases">

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2001-34">Church members challenged Presbytery’s repeated delay in granting a properly adopted congregational request to dissolve its pastoral relationship and its gift equivalent to three months of the pastor’s compensation. The SJC found seven complaints judicially out of order, sustained the dissolution-delay challenge, and rejected the gift challenge because Presbytery controlled its own civil property. No further relief was ordered. A concurrence would permit delay based on objective, justifiable findings, but concluded that Presbytery’s stated grounds were insufficient.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2001-34" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-2000-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="2000-02 Adams v. Northeast" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 2000-02: Adams v. Northeast, M29GA, pp. 122–124" data-search-text="2000-02 Adams v. Northeast Presbytery A prosecutor&#x27;s complaint relating to Northeast Presbytery&#x27;s judicial case was held administratively out of order by the SJC. The SJC adopted two grounds: BCO 43-1 bars a complaint about a matter subject to an appeal in another case, and the complaint sought retrial of an accused on charges of which he had been acquitted, relief the SJC could not grant. Although the related appeal was later withdrawn and the withdrawal approved, the SJC still applied BCO 43-1. A concurrence disputed that first ground and urged BCO clarification of appellate review of acquittals. No merits ruling was made. complaint Administratively out of order Not reached legacy 2000-2 BCO 32-13, BCO 32-17, BCO 32-19, BCO 35-4, BCO 35-5, BCO 35-11, BCO 43-1 complaint during appeal appellate review acquittal retrial administratively out of order judicial procedure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2000-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__2000-02.html">Adams v. Northeast Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2000-02">A prosecutor&#x27;s complaint relating to Northeast Presbytery&#x27;s judicial case was held administratively out of order by the SJC. The SJC adopted two grounds: BCO 43-1 bars a complaint about a matter subject to an appeal in another case, and the complaint sought retrial of an accused on charges of which he had been acquitted, relief the SJC could not grant. Although the related appeal was later withdrawn and the withdrawal approved, the SJC still applied BCO 43-1. A concurrence disputed that first ground and urged BCO clarification of appellate review of acquittals. No merits ruling was made.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2000-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Korean Capital, M30GA, pp. 114–115" data-search-text="2000-09 Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery After Korean Capital Presbytery appointed a commission to suspend the functions of Korean Presbyterian Church Washington’s elected Session and replace them without prior congregational consent, TE Sung Keon Kim complained. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery violated Preliminary Principle Six and BCO 16-2, misread BCO 13-9, and impermissibly sought to act for the lower court. Relying on Chappell, it annulled the commission’s subsequent actions as the Session. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 2000-9 BCO 13-9, BCO 41-1 original jurisdiction Session administrative commission congregational consent church governance">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>2000-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga30_2002__2000-09.html">Sung Keon Kim v. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-2000-09">After Korean Capital Presbytery appointed a commission to suspend the functions of Korean Presbyterian Church Washington’s elected Session and replace them without prior congregational consent, TE Sung Keon Kim complained. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery violated Preliminary Principle Six and BCO 16-2, misread BCO 13-9, and impermissibly sought to act for the lower court. Relying on Chappell, it annulled the commission’s subsequent actions as the Session.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-2000-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1999-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1999-01 Carolina v. Tennessee Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1999-01: Carolina v. Tennessee Valley, M28GA, pp. 238–241" data-search-text="1999-01 Western Carolina v. Tennessee Valley Three presbyteries asked the General Assembly under BCO 34-1 to assume original jurisdiction over a minister alleged to have allowed women to preach from a church pulpit. The SJC held the requests administratively out of order and did not reach the allegation’s merits. Worship was the Session’s responsibility, so the minister could not be held liable for actions assigned to it; moreover, Tennessee Valley Presbytery had acted on the allegations, defeating BCO 34-1’s refusal-to-act prerequisite. No further proceedings were ordered. original_jurisdiction_request Administratively out of order Not reached legacy 1999-1 BCO 34-1, BCO 31-2, BCO 12-5.e Women in ministry Pulpit authority Session jurisdiction Presbytery jurisdiction Worship standards">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1999-01</code> <span>· Original-jurisdiction request</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-01.html">Western Carolina v. Tennessee Valley</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1999-01">Three presbyteries asked the General Assembly under BCO 34-1 to assume original jurisdiction over a minister alleged to have allowed women to preach from a church pulpit. The SJC held the requests administratively out of order and did not reach the allegation’s merits. Worship was the Session’s responsibility, so the minister could not be held liable for actions assigned to it; moreover, Tennessee Valley Presbytery had acted on the allegations, defeating BCO 34-1’s refusal-to-act prerequisite. No further proceedings were ordered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1999-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

</div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1999-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1999-02 Tan v. South Texas" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1999-02: Tan v. South Texas, M28GA, p. 241" data-search-text="1999-02 Tan v. South Texas Presbytery Tan&#x27;s complaint challenged South Texas Presbytery&#x27;s action at its July 30–31, 1999 meeting. The SJC declared the complaint administratively out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-3: although dated and faxed August 28, it was not mailed until September 4 and was received September 7—beyond 30 days. SJC Manual 19.10 requires receipt in the Stated Clerk&#x27;s office and disallows fax filing. The merits were not reached. Twenty-two members concurred; one was recused and one absent. complaint Administratively out of order; Dismissed Not reached legacy 1999-2 BCO 43-3 complaint administrative order timeliness filing deadline 30-day period facsimile filing">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1999-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga28_2000__1999-02.html">Tan v. South Texas Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Administratively out of order; Dismissed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1999-02">Tan&#x27;s complaint challenged South Texas Presbytery&#x27;s action at its July 30–31, 1999 meeting. The SJC declared the complaint administratively out of order because it was untimely under BCO 43-3: although dated and faxed August 28, it was not mailed until September 4 and was received September 7—beyond 30 days. SJC Manual 19.10 requires receipt in the Stated Clerk&#x27;s office and disallows fax filing. The merits were not reached. Twenty-two members concurred; one was recused and one absent.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1999-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1999-03">A minister appealed an unidentified Presbytery judgment, then requested withdrawal. The full SJC approved the request, ending Case 99-3 without a merits decision. The source also records that Adams’s related complaint was considered out of order under BCO 43-1, but that complaint was distinct from the withdrawn appeal.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1999-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1999-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1999-05 Rountree v. Covenant" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1999-05: Rountree v. Covenant, M29GA, pp. 82–85" data-search-text="1999-05 Rountree v. Covenant After a minister remained on his presbytery&#x27;s rolls without call and outside its bounds for more than seven years, the presbytery completed involuntary divestiture without censure. He appealed. The SJC denied the appeal and sustained the divestiture, reasoning that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 allowed the presbytery to follow that procedure once the constitutional three-year limit had long passed and no call to a particular ministry was available. The action therefore left the divestiture without censure in force. appeal Partially sustained; Denied Not stated legacy 1999-5 BCO 13-2, BCO 34-10 Ministerial status Divestiture Book of Church Order compliance Presbytery jurisdiction Ministers without call">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1999-05</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-05.html">Rountree v. Covenant</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1999-05">After a minister remained on his presbytery&#x27;s rolls without call and outside its bounds for more than seven years, the presbytery completed involuntary divestiture without censure. He appealed. The SJC denied the appeal and sustained the divestiture, reasoning that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 allowed the presbytery to follow that procedure once the constitutional three-year limit had long passed and no call to a particular ministry was available. The action therefore left the divestiture without censure in force.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1999-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Central Carolina Presbytery A member challenged Presbytery’s affirmance of his excommunication, contending that SJC Case 97-9 had reversed his four guilty verdicts and precluded increased censure. The SJC did not sustain either issue. Case 97-9 had reversed only the original censure, leaving guilt intact. Because the offender bore the burden of showing repentance, and Session’s contrary factual determination received great deference absent clear error, the later excommunication remained in effect. appeal Not sustained Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 1999-6 BCO 14-7, BCO 30-3, BCO 30-4, BCO 31-7, BCO 32-17, BCO 32-19, BCO 33-3, BCO 36-5, BCO 37-3, BCO 39-3, BCO 42-9, BCO 57-5 interpretation of judicial decisions excommunication indefinite suspension repentance factual findings discretion and judgment">

<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1999-06">A member challenged Presbytery’s affirmance of his excommunication, contending that SJC Case 97-9 had reversed his four guilty verdicts and precluded increased censure. The SJC did not sustain either issue. Case 97-9 had reversed only the original censure, leaving guilt intact. Because the offender bore the burden of showing repentance, and Session’s contrary factual determination received great deference absent clear error, the later excommunication remained in effect.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1999-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1999-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1999-07 Black v. Eastern Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1999-07: Black v. Eastern Carolina, M29GA, pp. 89–110" data-search-text="1999-07 Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand because Presbytery had effectively adjudicated the complaint; the separate objection to proceeding without Black was not first filed below and was administratively out of order. It upheld Presbytery’s ruling that not every non-Calendar-Day view constitutes an exception. Because the record did not identify the licentiate’s precise view, the decision did not determine its acceptability or whether it could be taught. complaint Not sustained Great deference unless clear error (factual findings; discretion and judgment) legacy 1999-7 BCO 39-3 creation days Westminster Standards exception transfer examination exceptions to Westminster Standards">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1999-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga29_2001__1999-07.html">Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1999-07">Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand because Presbytery had effectively adjudicated the complaint; the separate objection to proceeding without Black was not first filed below and was administratively out of order. It upheld Presbytery’s ruling that not every non-Calendar-Day view constitutes an exception. Because the record did not identify the licentiate’s precise view, the decision did not determine its acceptability or whether it could be taught.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1999-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1998-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1998-01 Snapp v. James River" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1998-01: Snapp v. James River, M27GA, pp. 70–73" data-search-text="1998-01 Snapp v. James River Presbytery The complaint challenged James River Presbytery&#x27;s approval of an ordination examination in which the candidate called the Genesis creation days God&#x27;s anthropomorphic work days, not necessarily twenty-four-hour days. The complainant argued that view conflicted with WCF I.9. The SJC denied the complaint and answered &#x27;No&#x27; to whether the Presbytery erred; the examination stood. It held the Presbytery had authority and discretion, no General Assembly had declared anthropomorphic days contrary to the Standards, and an advisory-committee study left the SJC unwilling to decide creation-day length. A six-member dissent sought an exception and study-committee referral. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 1998-1 None listed creation days days of creation ordination examination Genesis 1 anthropomorphic days Westminster Confession of Faith WCF 1.9 presbytery discretion confessional standards exceptions">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1998-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga27_1999__1998-01.html">Snapp v. James River Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Denied</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1998-01">The complaint challenged James River Presbytery&#x27;s approval of an ordination examination in which the candidate called the Genesis creation days God&#x27;s anthropomorphic work days, not necessarily twenty-four-hour days. The complainant argued that view conflicted with WCF I.9. The SJC denied the complaint and answered &#x27;No&#x27; to whether the Presbytery erred; the examination stood. It held the Presbytery had authority and discretion, no General Assembly had declared anthropomorphic days contrary to the Standards, and an advisory-committee study left the SJC unwilling to decide creation-day length. A six-member dissent sought an exception and study-committee referral.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1998-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
