<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1990-08" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1990-08 Bowen v. Eastern Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1990-08: Bowen v. Eastern Carolina, M19GA, pp. 539–566" data-search-text="1990-08 Bowen v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. But it affirmed that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals admitting no officer exception. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1990-8 BCO 24-1, BCO 24-5.2, BCO 21-5.2, BCO 24-6, BCO 24-7, BCO 24-8, BCO 24-9, BCO 43-8, BCO 43-9, BCO 43-10, BCO 33-1, BCO 13-9, BCO 31-1, BCO 32-2, BCO 11-4, BCO 29-1, BCO 21-5, BCO 24-5, BCO 41-1, BCO 34-5 infant baptism limited atonement fundamentals of the system of doctrine officer ordination annulment of ordination rescinding prior actions subscription to confessional standards ruling elder qualification deacon qualification covenant theology TULIP five points of Calvinism original jurisdiction suspension from office without due process Robert&#x27;s Rules rescind motion">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1990-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-08.html">Bowen v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1990-08">Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. But it affirmed that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals admitting no officer exception. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1990-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1990-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1990-09 Hathaway v. Grace" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1990-09: Hathaway v. Grace, M19GA, pp. 567–579" data-search-text="1990-09 Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church failed to institute discipline against seven members who had not attended worship for over a year. The judicial panel denied the complaint on the grounds that the Session retained discretion to determine the timing of discipline proceedings, and procedural errors did not result in material prejudice. complaint Denied Not stated legacy 1990-9 BCO 43-6, BCO 43-2, BCO 46-5, BCO 32-20, BCO 27-5, BCO 27-3, BCO 51-5 church discipline non-attending members member roll deletion session authority pastoral duty circularization of court record of case session discretion absent members neglect of church attendance deletion from roll complaint procedure circularization of commission">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1990-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1990-10 Hathaway v. Grace" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1990-10: Hathaway v. Grace, M19GA, pp. 580–584" data-search-text="1990-10 Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery A pastor complained that Presbytery upheld his Session’s refusal to give him financial reports prepared for Session members, while also alleging record-transmission, circularization, factual, and constitutional errors. The SJC denied Specifications 1–5 but sustained Specification 6: because the pastor was a Session member, the Session’s authorization made the reports available to him regardless of whether other elders collected copies. His pastoral relationship had ended, however, so the access claim was moot and conferred no present right to the reports. Reasons for Specifications 1–2 were adopted from Case 90-9. complaint Partially sustained; Moot Not stated — BCO 43-6, BCO 43-2, BCO 12-1, BCO 12-2, BCO 12-5 financial reports session membership pastor rights dissolution of pastoral relation mootness session records access">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1990-10</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga19_1991__1990-10.html">Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Moot</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1990-10">A pastor complained that Presbytery upheld his Session’s refusal to give him financial reports prepared for Session members, while also alleging record-transmission, circularization, factual, and constitutional errors. The SJC denied Specifications 1–5 but sustained Specification 6: because the pastor was a Session member, the Session’s authorization made the reports available to him regardless of whether other elders collected copies. His pastoral relationship had ended, however, so the access claim was moot and conferred no present right to the reports. Reasons for Specifications 1–2 were adopted from Case 90-9.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1990-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
<div class="judicial-case__topics" aria-label="Topic tags"><span class="judicial-case__topics-label">Topics</span><span class="judicial-pill">financial reports</span><span class="judicial-pill">session membership</span><span class="judicial-pill">pastor rights</span><span class="judicial-case__topics-extra" id="judicial-topics-1990-10" hidden><span class="judicial-pill">dissolution of pastoral relation</span><span class="judicial-pill">mootness</span><span class="judicial-pill">session records access</span></span><button type="button" class="judicial-topics__toggle" aria-controls="judicial-topics-1990-10" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Show 3 more topics" data-topic-count="3">+3 topics</button></div>

<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-02">Fox challenged a Session’s acceptance of his resignation while censured, refusal to restore him, denial of relevant records, and allegedly uneven discipline in his marital dispute. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-1988-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1988-03 Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1988-03: Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia, M16GA, p. 387" data-search-text="1988-03 David C. Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery Complainant elders challenged Philadelphia Presbytery&#x27;s tie-vote refusal to sustain its judicial commission&#x27;s judgment that the Calvary Session wrongly treated physical cruelty as biblical grounds for divorce. The General Assembly adopted the commission&#x27;s judgment sustaining all three specifications: the Session&#x27;s action contravened Matthew 5 and 19, WCF 24:6, and the church&#x27;s disciplinary role. It annulled Presbytery&#x27;s refusal and instructed Presbytery to advise the Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce. The explanatory opinion urged pastoral alternatives, such as separation and rehabilitation, before any divorce determination. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 1988-3; Case #3; Minutes 3 None listed complaint referral to commission Philadelphia Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case2.html">David C. Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-03">Complainant elders challenged Philadelphia Presbytery&#x27;s tie-vote refusal to sustain its judicial commission&#x27;s judgment that the Calvary Session wrongly treated physical cruelty as biblical grounds for divorce. The General Assembly adopted the commission&#x27;s judgment sustaining all three specifications: the Session&#x27;s action contravened Matthew 5 and 19, WCF 24:6, and the church&#x27;s disciplinary role. It annulled Presbytery&#x27;s refusal and instructed Presbytery to advise the Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce. The explanatory opinion urged pastoral alternatives, such as separation and rehabilitation, before any divorce determination.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Philadelphia Presbytery Philadelphia Presbytery ordered Christ Church, Oreland’s Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial cases were on appeal. The General Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission’s judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification for insufficient documentation but sustaining the constitutional challenge: BCO 12-5 and the separation of church-court powers reserve membership control to the Session, which correctly withheld transfer during pending judicial process. The judgment annulled Presbytery’s instruction and imposed three-year constitutional-inquiry safeguards, plus Digest purchase and officer review. complaint Partially sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 1988-4 BCO 12-5 complaint transfer of membership separation of church-court powers constitutional inquiry safeguards">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case2.html">TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-04">Philadelphia Presbytery ordered Christ Church, Oreland’s Session to transfer three ruling elders while their judicial cases were on appeal. The General Assembly adopted its special Judicial Commission’s judgment rejecting the improper-debate specification for insufficient documentation but sustaining the constitutional challenge: BCO 12-5 and the separation of church-court powers reserve membership control to the Session, which correctly withheld transfer during pending judicial process. The judgment annulled Presbytery’s instruction and imposed three-year constitutional-inquiry safeguards, plus Digest purchase and officer review.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1988-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1988-05 Rayburn et al. v. Missouri" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1988-05: Rayburn et al. v. Missouri, M16GA, p. 387" data-search-text="1988-05 Robert G. Rayburn et al. v. Missouri Presbytery Missouri Presbytery instructed its Candidates and Credentials Committee to examine candidates without treating a qualified minority view on prophecy and tongues as disqualifying. Complainants argued this conflicted with the 1986 Gentry decision. The Judicial Commission, adopted by the 16th General Assembly, did not sustain the complaint and confirmed the lower court 7-4. Although earlier similar cases had annulled lower-court actions, it cited the absence of a specific candidate, safeguards, inconclusive debate, and a preference for grass-roots resolution, encouraging Overture 25. The dissent called the view fundamentally out of accord. complaint Not sustained; Affirmed Not stated legacy 1988-5; Case #5; Minutes 5 None listed complaint referral to commission Missouri Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case3.html">Robert G. Rayburn et al. v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-05">Missouri Presbytery instructed its Candidates and Credentials Committee to examine candidates without treating a qualified minority view on prophecy and tongues as disqualifying. Complainants argued this conflicted with the 1986 Gentry decision. The Judicial Commission, adopted by the 16th General Assembly, did not sustain the complaint and confirmed the lower court 7-4. Although earlier similar cases had annulled lower-court actions, it cited the absence of a specific candidate, safeguards, inconclusive debate, and a preference for grass-roots resolution, encouraging Overture 25. The dissent called the view fundamentally out of accord.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1988-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1988-06 DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1988-06: DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia, M17GA, pp. 209–227" data-search-text="1988-06 TE John T. DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation. complaint Sustained; Annulled; Guilty; Not guilty Not stated legacy 1988-6 None listed complaint trials de novo plea bargaining necessary witnesses church discipline">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case3.html">TE John T. DeBardeleben v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled; Guilty; Not guilty</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-06">A complaint challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of proceedings that cleared teaching and ruling elders without properly trying serious public accusations arising from Christ Church’s division. All three specifications were sustained because plea bargaining, dropped charges, and failure to hear necessary witnesses left the accusations unresolved. Presbytery’s action was annulled and de novo trials produced mixed convictions and acquittals. Harold Burkhart received six months’ suspension, Douglas McCready an admonition, and six former ruling elders three-month suspensions. The decision stressed taking such conflicts to Presbytery or judicial process rather than the congregation.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1988-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1988-07 Jamison v. Western Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1988-07: Jamison v. Western Carolina, M16GA, p. 387" data-search-text="1988-07 Robert Jamison v. Western Carolina Presbytery A ruling elder complained that Western Carolina Presbytery wrongly left a confessing bisexual Teaching Elder under indefinite suspension rather than deposing him, excluding him from the sacraments, and cutting him off from fellowship. The General Assembly&#x27;s adjudicating commission did not sustain the specification of error and confirmed Presbytery&#x27;s action, holding it complied with BCO 30-3, 4 and 34-7. Review was limited to the constitutionality of the disciplinary process; the commission cited Presbytery&#x27;s restorative purpose and evidence of repentance. The Assembly was advised Presbytery later deposed the Teaching Elder. complaint Not sustained; Affirmed Not stated legacy 1988-7; Case #7; Minutes 7 BCO 30-3 complaint referral to commission homosexuality Western Carolina Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case4.html">Robert Jamison v. Western Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-07">A ruling elder complained that Western Carolina Presbytery wrongly left a confessing bisexual Teaching Elder under indefinite suspension rather than deposing him, excluding him from the sacraments, and cutting him off from fellowship. The General Assembly&#x27;s adjudicating commission did not sustain the specification of error and confirmed Presbytery&#x27;s action, holding it complied with BCO 30-3, 4 and 34-7. Review was limited to the constitutionality of the disciplinary process; the commission cited Presbytery&#x27;s restorative purpose and evidence of repentance. The Assembly was advised Presbytery later deposed the Teaching Elder.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1988-09" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1988-09 Morrison et al. v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1988-09: Morrison et al. v. Philadelphia, M17GA, pp. 228–231" data-search-text="1988-09 Morrison et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery Philadelphia Presbytery treated a letter as a complaint although it had not first been filed with the Session, judged the Session without proper process, and asked its clerk to facilitate membership transfers despite the Session&#x27;s authority over dismissal letters. Those and a constitutional-limits specification were sustained; claims that Presbytery neglected underlying questions and acted for the Session were not. The March 12 actions were annulled, specified language expunged, and Presbytery directed to adopt safeguards for constitutional inquiries and review relevant church-law materials. complaint Partially sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 1988-9 None listed complaint referral to commission Christ Reformed Presbyterian Church Oreland PA Philadelphia Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-09</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga17_1989__case4.html">Morrison et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-09">Philadelphia Presbytery treated a letter as a complaint although it had not first been filed with the Session, judged the Session without proper process, and asked its clerk to facilitate membership transfers despite the Session&#x27;s authority over dismissal letters. Those and a constitutional-limits specification were sustained; claims that Presbytery neglected underlying questions and acted for the Session were not. The March 12 actions were annulled, specified language expunged, and Presbytery directed to adopt safeguards for constitutional inquiries and review relevant church-law materials.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-09" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1988-10" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1988-10 Serio et al. v. Palmetto" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1988-10: Serio et al. v. Palmetto, M16GA, p. 388" data-search-text="1988-10 James Serio et al. v. Palmetto Presbytery The 16th General Assembly approved the adjudicating Commission’s judgment sustaining a complaint against Palmetto Presbytery. The Commission found that Presbytery erred by sustaining John Tomlinson’s theology examination and licensing him despite his belief in continuing noncanonical revelation through prophecy, tongues, dreams, visions, and direct speech, contrary to WCF I.1 and I.6 and BCO 7-1. It directed Presbytery to annul the theology examination, suspend its licensing action, counsel and re-examine Tomlinson, exercise greater care, and report to the next Assembly. complaint Sustained Not stated Case #10; Minutes 10 BCO 7-1 complaint referral to commission charismatic gifts candidate examination Palmetto Presbytery">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1988-10</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga16_1988__case6.html">James Serio et al. v. Palmetto Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1988-10">The 16th General Assembly approved the adjudicating Commission’s judgment sustaining a complaint against Palmetto Presbytery. The Commission found that Presbytery erred by sustaining John Tomlinson’s theology examination and licensing him despite his belief in continuing noncanonical revelation through prophecy, tongues, dreams, visions, and direct speech, contrary to WCF I.1 and I.6 and BCO 7-1. It directed Presbytery to annul the theology examination, suspend its licensing action, counsel and re-examine Tomlinson, exercise greater care, and report to the next Assembly.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1988-10" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<section class="judicial-year" data-judicial-year="1987"><h2>1987</h2>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1987-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1987-01 Harris v. Philadelphia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1987-01: Harris v. Philadelphia, M15GA, p. 323" data-search-text="1987-01 Erwin Morrison, TE Donald Stone, TE David Brewer, TE Steve Christian, RE John Harley, RE David Lachman, RE George Harris v. Philadelphia Presbytery Philadelphia Presbytery ordained Lester Porter as a Ruling Elder of Presbytery to serve a cross-cultural mission church with no particular-church members. The Assembly, adopting the Judicial Commission&#x27;s adjudication, sustained all three specifications and upheld the complaint: the ordination lacked BCO compliance and the Presbytery mishandled the complaint. It refused to annul Porter&#x27;s ordination—reasoning Presbytery may ordain Ruling Elders in organizing churches—but directed Presbytery to find a BCO-conforming temporary government for Church Without Walls, stop ordaining Ruling Elders not duly elected by a particular church, and bring Porter&#x27;s ordination into conformity. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1987-1; Minutes 15-73 None listed complaint presbytery action commission appointed complaint found in order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1987-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga15_1987__case1.html">Erwin Morrison, TE Donald Stone, TE David Brewer, TE Steve Christian, RE John Harley, RE David Lachman, RE George Harris v. Philadelphia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1987-01">Philadelphia Presbytery ordained Lester Porter as a Ruling Elder of Presbytery to serve a cross-cultural mission church with no particular-church members. The Assembly, adopting the Judicial Commission&#x27;s adjudication, sustained all three specifications and upheld the complaint: the ordination lacked BCO compliance and the Presbytery mishandled the complaint. It refused to annul Porter&#x27;s ordination—reasoning Presbytery may ordain Ruling Elders in organizing churches—but directed Presbytery to find a BCO-conforming temporary government for Church Without Walls, stop ordaining Ruling Elders not duly elected by a particular church, and bring Porter&#x27;s ordination into conformity.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1987-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1986-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1986-01 Jr. et al. v. Calvary" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1986-01: Jr. et al. v. Calvary, M14GA, p. 329" data-search-text="1986-01 Kenneth L. Gentry, Jr. et al. v. Calvary Presbytery Ministers challenged Calvary Presbytery&#x27;s approval of William Hyer&#x27;s examination and reception despite his belief that noncanonical, nonbinding revelation could continue. The Assembly sustained the complaint because PCA standards foreclose continuing revelation beyond illumination and providence. It annulled only the examination portion concerning revelation, suspending his reception, and instructed Presbytery to counsel and re-examine him, then report to the next Assembly. The majority deemed the record sufficient despite a dissent emphasizing Hyer&#x27;s affirmation of Scripture&#x27;s finality and the absence of an examination transcript. complaint Sustained; Annulled; Remanded Not stated legacy 1986-1; Case #1; Minutes 1 None listed complaint commission appointed complaint found in order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1986-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case1.html">Kenneth L. Gentry, Jr. et al. v. Calvary Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1986-01">Ministers challenged Calvary Presbytery&#x27;s approval of William Hyer&#x27;s examination and reception despite his belief that noncanonical, nonbinding revelation could continue. The Assembly sustained the complaint because PCA standards foreclose continuing revelation beyond illumination and providence. It annulled only the examination portion concerning revelation, suspending his reception, and instructed Presbytery to counsel and re-examine him, then report to the next Assembly. The majority deemed the record sufficient despite a dissent emphasizing Hyer&#x27;s affirmation of Scripture&#x27;s finality and the absence of an examination transcript.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1986-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

</div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1986-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1986-02 Jr. et al. v. Grace" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1986-02: Jr. et al. v. Grace, M14GA, p. 329" data-search-text="1986-02 Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr. et al. v. Grace Presbytery A complaint challenged Grace Presbytery&#x27;s approval and installation of a candidate who had been divorced for his own infidelity and had remarried; the complainants argued Scripture, the Westminster Confession, BCO 16-3, and the Seventh General Assembly&#x27;s divorce report barred ordination. The Judicial Commission did not sustain any of the four specifications and upheld Presbytery&#x27;s action. Its adopted reason was that the PCA&#x27;s constitutional statements do not explicitly address divorce and remarriage for church officers; noting wide interpretive disagreement, it called for study. The ordination and installation remained undisturbed. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 1986-2; Case #2; Minutes 2 BCO 16-3 complaint commission appointed complaint found in order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1986-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case2.html">Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr. et al. v. Grace Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1986-02">A complaint challenged Grace Presbytery&#x27;s approval and installation of a candidate who had been divorced for his own infidelity and had remarried; the complainants argued Scripture, the Westminster Confession, BCO 16-3, and the Seventh General Assembly&#x27;s divorce report barred ordination. The Judicial Commission did not sustain any of the four specifications and upheld Presbytery&#x27;s action. Its adopted reason was that the PCA&#x27;s constitutional statements do not explicitly address divorce and remarriage for church officers; noting wide interpretive disagreement, it called for study. The ordination and installation remained undisturbed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1986-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1986-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1986-03 Jr. v. Palmetto" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1986-03: Jr. v. Palmetto, M14GA, p. 329" data-search-text="1986-03 Henry D. Knight, Jr. v. Palmetto Presbytery A ruling elder challenged Palmetto Presbytery’s publication, as an appendix to meeting minutes, of a letter never discussed at that meeting, and its handling of his complaint. The Judicial Commission sustained specifications 1 and 3: Presbytery had not clearly declared the publication erroneous, and it risked harming Covenant’s Session. Specifications 2 and 4 failed because Presbytery timely referred the complaint, though its record was inaccurate, and acted in good faith. Despite Presbytery’s later deletion of the letter, the Commission remanded for a new hearing on specifications 1 and 3. complaint Partially sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 1986-3; Case #3; Minutes 3 None listed complaint commission appointed complaint found in order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1986-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case3.html">Henry D. Knight, Jr. v. Palmetto Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1986-03">A ruling elder challenged Palmetto Presbytery’s publication, as an appendix to meeting minutes, of a letter never discussed at that meeting, and its handling of his complaint. The Judicial Commission sustained specifications 1 and 3: Presbytery had not clearly declared the publication erroneous, and it risked harming Covenant’s Session. Specifications 2 and 4 failed because Presbytery timely referred the complaint, though its record was inaccurate, and acted in good faith. Despite Presbytery’s later deletion of the letter, the Commission remanded for a new hearing on specifications 1 and 3.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1986-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Because no one appeared to represent the appeal, the Committee on Judicial Business judged it abandoned, leaving the merits and requested relief undecided. appeal Abandoned Not reached legacy 1986-4; Case #4; Minutes 4 BCO 30-1, BCO 30-5, BCO 34-10, BCO 42-6 appeal commission appointed appeal found in order suspension of judgment divestiture from office">

<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1986-04">An appeal challenged Great Lakes Presbytery&#x27;s decision to divest TE Edward A. Steele III without censure and without judicial process, which he alleged followed an accusation that he was not engaged in his official duties. Steele alleged constitutional and discriminatory error and sought investigation, rescission, or erasure of his name. Because no one appeared to represent the appeal, the Committee on Judicial Business judged it abandoned, leaving the merits and requested relief undecided.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1986-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1986-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1986-05 Abee et al. v. James River" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1986-05: Abee et al. v. James River, M14GA, p. 329" data-search-text="1986-05 D. Keith Abee et al. v. James River Presbytery Five appellants challenged censures imposed after a Presbytery commission treated a Session&#x27;s request for assistance as authority to initiate judicial process. The Assembly sustained all six specifications, holding that the commission lacked authority to proceed before charges were approved and that original jurisdiction remained with the Session. It reversed the censures, ordered their public removal, and remanded for the Session to address any properly specified charges. The ruling expressly did not determine the appellants&#x27; guilt or innocence. appeal Sustained; Reversed; Remanded Not stated legacy 1986-5; Case #5; Minutes 5 None listed appeal commission appointed appeal found in order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1986-05</code> <span>· Appeal</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case5.html">D. Keith Abee et al. v. James River Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Reversed; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1986-05">Five appellants challenged censures imposed after a Presbytery commission treated a Session&#x27;s request for assistance as authority to initiate judicial process. The Assembly sustained all six specifications, holding that the commission lacked authority to proceed before charges were approved and that original jurisdiction remained with the Session. It reversed the censures, ordered their public removal, and remanded for the Session to address any properly specified charges. The ruling expressly did not determine the appellants&#x27; guilt or innocence.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1986-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1986-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1986-06 Bogue et al. v. of the Ascension" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1986-06: Bogue et al. v. of the Ascension, M14GA, p. 335" data-search-text="1986-06 Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension Presbytery’s response claiming that Lutjens had changed his sacramental views was challenged as factually false and as a retroactive rewriting of minutes Presbytery had previously refused to interpret. All five specifications were sustained, including illegitimate interpretation of BCO 58-4. Because the earlier examination transcript was unavailable through mechanical failure, Presbytery was ordered to reexamine Lutjens, provide a complete transcript, and report by November 10, 1986. Discipline remained conditional on continued nonconformity after pastoral counsel. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1986-6; Case #6; Minutes 6 BCO 43-1, BCO 14-25, BCO 58-4 complaint complaint not in order appeal vs complaint procedural bar">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1986-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga14_1986__case6.html">Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1986-06">Presbytery’s response claiming that Lutjens had changed his sacramental views was challenged as factually false and as a retroactive rewriting of minutes Presbytery had previously refused to interpret. All five specifications were sustained, including illegitimate interpretation of BCO 58-4. Because the earlier examination transcript was unavailable through mechanical failure, Presbytery was ordered to reexamine Lutjens, provide a complete transcript, and report by November 10, 1986. Discipline remained conditional on continued nonconformity after pastoral counsel.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1986-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1985-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1985-05 Jr., et al. v. Missouri" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1985-05: Jr., et al. v. Missouri, M13GA, pp. 104–132" data-search-text="1985-05 S. Michael Preg, Jr., et al. v. Missouri Presbytery Can a presbytery require an annual committee visit to every session and congregation absent a request or evident problem? The judicial commission sustained the complaint against Missouri Presbytery 16-0, holding BCO 11-4 limits higher-court jurisdiction to express constitutional provisions and BCO 13-9 contains no clear authorization for such required visits. It instructed presbytery to conform its Standing Rules and visitation procedures to the BCO, while encouraging voluntary pastoral oversight; several commissioners recorded negative votes without stated reasons. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1985-5; Case #5; Minutes 5 BCO 11-4, BCO 13-9 presbytery authority constitutional jurisdiction church visitation limits on higher court powers pastoral oversight">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1985-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga13_1985__case1.html">S. Michael Preg, Jr., et al. v. Missouri Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1985-05">Can a presbytery require an annual committee visit to every session and congregation absent a request or evident problem? The judicial commission sustained the complaint against Missouri Presbytery 16-0, holding BCO 11-4 limits higher-court jurisdiction to express constitutional provisions and BCO 13-9 contains no clear authorization for such required visits. It instructed presbytery to conform its Standing Rules and visitation procedures to the BCO, while encouraging voluntary pastoral oversight; several commissioners recorded negative votes without stated reasons.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1985-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

</div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1984-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1984-01 Wuckovich v. Central Carolina" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1984-01: Wuckovich v. Central Carolina, M12GA, p. 288" data-search-text="1984-01 Elder Roy J. Wuckovich v. Central Carolina Presbytery A ruling elder complained that Central Carolina Presbytery violated the BCO in examining and approving Rick Downs for ordination, citing five specifications about the call, Downs’s Sabbath exception, the revote after an initial disapproval, lack of Scriptural search, and ordination questions. The judicial commission held points 1, 2, 4, and 5 not sustained 11–0 and point 3 not sustained 10–1; the general complaint was not sustained 11–0, and the lower court decision was confirmed. Its explanatory opinion said the commission disagreed on the Sabbath/subscription question and acted largely because the specifications did not substantiate the complaint. complaint Not sustained; Affirmed Not stated legacy 1984-1; Minutes 12-80 None listed complaint presbytery action judicial commission appointed">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1984-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case1.html">Elder Roy J. Wuckovich v. Central Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained; Affirmed</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1984-01">A ruling elder complained that Central Carolina Presbytery violated the BCO in examining and approving Rick Downs for ordination, citing five specifications about the call, Downs’s Sabbath exception, the revote after an initial disapproval, lack of Scriptural search, and ordination questions. The judicial commission held points 1, 2, 4, and 5 not sustained 11–0 and point 3 not sustained 10–1; the general complaint was not sustained 11–0, and the lower court decision was confirmed. Its explanatory opinion said the commission disagreed on the Sabbath/subscription question and acted largely because the specifications did not substantiate the complaint.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1984-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1984-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1984-02 Toms and Thompson v. Central Florida" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1984-02: Toms and Thompson v. Central Florida, M12GA, p. 288" data-search-text="1984-02 Russell D. Toms and TE William L. Thompson v. Central Florida Presbytery Central Florida Presbytery received a minister while he had a pending call to labor in another presbytery. A Judicial Commission sustained the specification of error, holding that BCO 13-2,5 barred receiving him under those circumstances; the vote was 9–4. It also voted 13–0 to remand the entire matter for proper procedures regarding his admission to the PCA. The Commission commended the presbytery&#x27;s aim of receiving him but ruled the process erroneous, leaving the admission to be handled through proper procedures. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 1984-2; Case #2; Minutes 12-81 BCO 13-2 complaint presbytery action judicial commission appointed">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1984-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case2.html">Russell D. Toms and TE William L. Thompson v. Central Florida Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1984-02">Central Florida Presbytery received a minister while he had a pending call to labor in another presbytery. A Judicial Commission sustained the specification of error, holding that BCO 13-2,5 barred receiving him under those circumstances; the vote was 9–4. It also voted 13–0 to remand the entire matter for proper procedures regarding his admission to the PCA. The Commission commended the presbytery&#x27;s aim of receiving him but ruled the process erroneous, leaving the admission to be handled through proper procedures.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1984-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1984-05" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1984-05 Peterson, et al. v. of Ascension" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1984-05: Peterson, et al. v. of Ascension, M12GA, p. 298" data-search-text="1984-05 Robert C. Peterson, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension Complaint challenged Ascension Presbytery&#x27;s March 10, 1984 refusal to obey the Eleventh General Assembly&#x27;s directive to correct constitutional defects in Kurt Lutjens&#x27;s ordination trial, and its purported BCO 41 reference of the matter to the Twelfth General Assembly for retrial. The CJB sustained specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation and adopted recommendations for remedial action. The complaint&#x27;s asserted distinction—that BCO 41 cannot return a prior General Assembly decision for retrial—marks the case&#x27;s practical limit. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1984-5; Minutes 12-83 None listed complaint presbytery action judicial commission">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1984-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case6.html">Robert C. Peterson, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1984-05">Complaint challenged Ascension Presbytery&#x27;s March 10, 1984 refusal to obey the Eleventh General Assembly&#x27;s directive to correct constitutional defects in Kurt Lutjens&#x27;s ordination trial, and its purported BCO 41 reference of the matter to the Twelfth General Assembly for retrial. The CJB sustained specifications of continued non-compliance and constitutional violation and adopted recommendations for remedial action. The complaint&#x27;s asserted distinction—that BCO 41 cannot return a prior General Assembly decision for retrial—marks the case&#x27;s practical limit.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1984-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1984-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1984-06 Gardner, et al. v. of North Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1984-06: Gardner, et al. v. of North Georgia, M12GA, p. 298" data-search-text="1984-06 Warren Gardner, et al. v. Presbytery of North Georgia A complaint challenged North Georgia Presbytery&#x27;s transfer of Trinity Mission, Elberton, Georgia, to Central Georgia Presbytery, alleging insufficient debate and failure to examine discipline issues. The Judicial Commission unanimously did not sustain the specification of error. Its adopted explanation found that two years of contact and discussions had done as much as possible to clear misunderstanding. It nevertheless noted the presbytery&#x27;s inadequate explanation and the complainants&#x27; failure to secure adequate information; no relief was granted, and the listed questions about congregational choice and transfer power were not answered. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 1984-6; Case #6; Minutes 12-82 None listed complaint presbytery action judicial commission">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1984-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case3.html">Warren Gardner, et al. v. Presbytery of North Georgia</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1984-06">A complaint challenged North Georgia Presbytery&#x27;s transfer of Trinity Mission, Elberton, Georgia, to Central Georgia Presbytery, alleging insufficient debate and failure to examine discipline issues. The Judicial Commission unanimously did not sustain the specification of error. Its adopted explanation found that two years of contact and discussions had done as much as possible to clear misunderstanding. It nevertheless noted the presbytery&#x27;s inadequate explanation and the complainants&#x27; failure to secure adequate information; no relief was granted, and the listed questions about congregational choice and transfer power were not answered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1984-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1984-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1984-07 Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio, et al. v. of Ascension" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1984-07: Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio, et al. v. of Ascension, M12GA, p. 298" data-search-text="1984-07 Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension A Session and other complainants challenged Presbytery’s May 1984 resolution as continued noncompliance with directions from an earlier ordination case. The continued-noncompliance specification was sustained, but allegations of constitutional violation and contumacy were not sustained. Remedial recommendations were adopted, although the supplied excerpt provides neither their terms nor the deciding body’s reasons. <header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1984-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga12_1984__case4.html">Session of Faith Presbyterian Church, Akron, Ohio, et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1984-07">A Session and other complainants challenged Presbytery’s May 1984 resolution as continued noncompliance with directions from an earlier ordination case. The continued-noncompliance specification was sustained, but allegations of constitutional violation and contumacy were not sustained. Remedial recommendations were adopted, although the supplied excerpt provides neither their terms nor the deciding body’s reasons. The mixed ruling therefore distinguishes noncompliance from the complainants’ more serious characterizations of Presbytery’s conduct.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1984-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Illiana, M11GA, pp. 138–139" data-search-text="1983-01 Robert L. Reymond et al. v. Illiana Presbytery A teaching elder confessed adultery, but Presbytery charged him only with ninth-commandment violations, admonished him, and required him to reconsider his call. The complaint alleged Presbytery failed to take BCO 34-7 action and improperly reduced the charges. The Commission sustained both items and remanded for a new trial, reasoning that the confessed sins were not considered and the censure was not commensurate with the offenses charged; it did not itself convict or sentence him. It adopted a recommendation directing Presbytery to follow BCO disciplinary procedures. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 1983-1; Case #1; Minutes 1 BCO 34-7 ministerial discipline adultery censure new trial judicial procedure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1983-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case1.html">Robert L. Reymond et al. v. Illiana Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1983-01">A teaching elder confessed adultery, but Presbytery charged him only with ninth-commandment violations, admonished him, and required him to reconsider his call. The complaint alleged Presbytery failed to take BCO 34-7 action and improperly reduced the charges. The Commission sustained both items and remanded for a new trial, reasoning that the confessed sins were not considered and the censure was not commensurate with the offenses charged; it did not itself convict or sentence him. It adopted a recommendation directing Presbytery to follow BCO disciplinary procedures.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1983-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1983-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1983-02 Barleman et al. v. of Ascension" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1983-02: Barleman et al. v. of Ascension, M11GA, p. 69" data-search-text="1983-02 Val H. Barleman et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension The General Assembly sustained a complaint against Ascension Presbytery for sustaining a candidate&#x27;s ordination trials despite exceptions to PCA constitutional standards. The Commission upheld specifications that his Lord&#x27;s Supper and baptism views denied required visible-church membership and that his women-deacons view conflicted with the BCO; it rejected specifications on Sabbath recreation and immersion. The Assembly annulled the Presbytery&#x27;s sustaining action, but not the ordination itself, so the candidate remained on the roll. It directed correction of the trial and pastoral instruction, with possible discipline if his views persisted. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 1983-2; Case #2; Minutes 2 BCO 21-5, BCO 56-6, BCO 58-4, BCO 7-2, BCO 9-3 ordination doctrinal subscription Lord&#x27;s Supper baptism Sabbath women deacons">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1983-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case2.html">Val H. Barleman et al. v. Presbytery of Ascension</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1983-02">The General Assembly sustained a complaint against Ascension Presbytery for sustaining a candidate&#x27;s ordination trials despite exceptions to PCA constitutional standards. The Commission upheld specifications that his Lord&#x27;s Supper and baptism views denied required visible-church membership and that his women-deacons view conflicted with the BCO; it rejected specifications on Sabbath recreation and immersion. The Assembly annulled the Presbytery&#x27;s sustaining action, but not the ordination itself, so the candidate remained on the roll. It directed correction of the trial and pastoral instruction, with possible discipline if his views persisted.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1983-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1983-07" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1983-07 Wilbor et al. v. North Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1983-07: Wilbor et al. v. North Georgia, M11GA, p. 70" data-search-text="1983-07 Stark Wilbor et al. v. North Georgia Presbytery Complainants challenged North Georgia Presbytery’s approval of John Parrish’s transfer examination after he denied that the first day of the week is the Christian Sabbath. The General Assembly sustained the specification of error and annulled Presbytery’s action, characterizing the teaching as a fundamental element of doctrine. Presbytery was directed to instruct Parrish and, only if his view conformed to Scripture, the doctrinal standards, and the BCO, re-examine him in that area. complaint Sustained; Annulled Not stated legacy 1983-7; Case #7; Minutes 7 None listed licensure transfer of license Christian Sabbath Westminster Confession doctrinal examination">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1983-07</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case3.html">Stark Wilbor et al. v. North Georgia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Annulled</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1983-07">Complainants challenged North Georgia Presbytery’s approval of John Parrish’s transfer examination after he denied that the first day of the week is the Christian Sabbath. The General Assembly sustained the specification of error and annulled Presbytery’s action, characterizing the teaching as a fundamental element of doctrine. Presbytery was directed to instruct Parrish and, only if his view conformed to Scripture, the doctrinal standards, and the BCO, re-examine him in that area.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1983-07" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1983-08</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case5.html">Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1983-08">Complainants challenged Presbytery’s called meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adopted adjudication sustained the objection to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote because Robert’s Rules required a two-thirds vote, and sustained without stated grounds the objection to ordering the dissolved commission to reassemble and revote. It rejected the challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its consideration of David Alexander’s complaint; the membership claim failed because church membership is not itself a court. No express remedy was ordered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1983-08" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1983-13" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1983-13 Codling et al. v. of Eastern Canada" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1983-13: Codling et al. v. of Eastern Canada, M11GA, p. 71" data-search-text="1983-13 Donald A. Codling et al. v. Presbytery of Eastern Canada Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained regarding the improperly adopted supermajority rule and the insufficiency of objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace; claims that pertinent data was excluded and requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. Citing the fragmented examination and sharply differing views, the Assembly urged a complete reexamination at one meeting. It did not order Harris licensed or formally remand the matter. complaint Partially sustained Not stated Case #13; Minutes 13 None listed licensure standing rules notice ministerial examination preaching pastoral qualification">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1983-13</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga11_1983__case10.html">Donald A. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1983-13">Presbytery members challenged Eastern Canada Presbytery’s denial of Ron Harris’s licensure. The complaint was sustained regarding the improperly adopted supermajority rule and the insufficiency of objections concerning counseling, evangelistic preaching, and sovereign grace; claims that pertinent data was excluded and requests to hear Harris preach were blocked were not sustained. Citing the fragmented examination and sharply differing views, the Assembly urged a complete reexamination at one meeting. <article class="judicial-case" id="case-1982-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1982-01 Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1982-01: Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast, M10GA, pp. 213–219" data-search-text="1982-01 Stephen M. Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast Presbytery A Session challenged Gulf Coast Presbytery’s refusal to sustain Raymond Bradford Fell’s ordination examination, contending that his theonomic view was improperly treated as disqualifying and that prejudicial materials affected the process. The General Assembly sustained specifications 1, 2, and 5, but not 3 and 4. It ordered re-examination after direct guidance on specific biblical and confessional deficiencies, while expressly refusing to dictate the result. It also urged that no view of the judicial law’s present application should itself define orthodoxy or heresy. complaint Partially sustained Not stated legacy 1982-1; Case #1; Minutes 1 None listed theonomy theological examination application of God&#x27;s law complaint Gulf Coast Presbytery ordination examination deposition censure restoration to office status under censure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1982-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case1.html">Stephen M. Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1982-01">A Session challenged Gulf Coast Presbytery’s refusal to sustain Raymond Bradford Fell’s ordination examination, contending that his theonomic view was improperly treated as disqualifying and that prejudicial materials affected the process. The General Assembly sustained specifications 1, 2, and 5, but not 3 and 4. It ordered re-examination after direct guidance on specific biblical and confessional deficiencies, while expressly refusing to dictate the result. It also urged that no view of the judicial law’s present application should itself define orthodoxy or heresy.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1982-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Davis, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia A teaching elder complained that Central Georgia Presbytery wrongly refused to sustain his complaint against a session that closed a disciplinary matter involving unbiblical separation, divorce, and remarriage before any judicial action. The General Assembly&#x27;s Judicial Commission sustained the complaint, treating the session&#x27;s &quot;closing of the matter&quot; as the central issue. It did not grant the requested reproof, suspension, or excommunication; it requested the presbytery to aid the session in corrections and heed WCF 24:6 and SC 87 on divorce and repentance. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1982-2; Case #2; Minutes 2 BCO 27-4, BCO 27-5, BCO 32-3, BCO 32-9, BCO 32-20, BCO 34-8, BCO 37-7, BCO 39-2, BCO 42-7, BCO 43-1, BCO 56-1 church discipline marital divorce unscriptural grounds biblical repentance Presbyterian judicial procedure session discipline">

Davis, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia</a></h3></header>

<div class="judicial-case__layout">

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1982-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1982-03 Bryson, et al. v. of Central Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1982-03: Bryson, et al. v. of Central Georgia, M10GA, pp. 58–111" data-search-text="1982-03 David H. Bryson, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia Teaching elders challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s refusal to sustain a complaint against Liberty Presbyterian Church’s Session for closing a disciplinary matter before taking judicial action. The General Assembly sustained the complaint, adopting findings that counseling, Session discussion, and instruction on discipline were underway before the Session closed the matter and refused to reopen it. It requested Presbytery to assist the Session with appropriate corrections or further action and said both courts should heed confessional teaching on marriage and repentance. The complainants’ requested affirmations were not expressly ordered. complaint Sustained Not stated legacy 1982-3; Case #3; Minutes 3 BCO 27-4, BCO 27-5, BCO 42-7, BCO 43-1, BCO 39-2 church discipline divorce remarriage repentance marital dissolution session authority presbytery oversight">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1982-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case3.html">David H. Bryson, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1982-03">Teaching elders challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s refusal to sustain a complaint against Liberty Presbyterian Church’s Session for closing a disciplinary matter before taking judicial action. The General Assembly sustained the complaint, adopting findings that counseling, Session discussion, and instruction on discipline were underway before the Session closed the matter and refused to reopen it. It requested Presbytery to assist the Session with appropriate corrections or further action and said both courts should heed confessional teaching on marriage and repentance. The complainants’ requested affirmations were not expressly ordered.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1982-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Grace Presbytery Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery&#x27;s refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against a minister in Western Carolinas Presbytery. Hathaway, Jr., et al. v. Grace Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1982-04">Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery&#x27;s refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against a minister in Western Carolinas Presbytery. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because Western Carolinas had not refused jurisdiction. It nevertheless directed that presbytery to proceed at its next stated meeting and held the one-year limitation inapplicable because its commission had unduly delayed formal process. The ruling was conditional, not an unqualified endorsement of the handling below.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1982-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1982-05</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case5.html">James K. <p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1982-05">The Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to rescind its resolution calling voluntary total abstinence from alcohol the proper Christian lifestyle. The General Assembly unanimously sustained the complaint, adopting the commission’s conclusion that the resolution in practice bound consciences and exceeded Scripture’s requirements contrary to the Westminster Confession. The judgment did not expressly rescind the resolution, and it distinguished improper conscience-binding from permissible teaching and counseling against alcohol abuse and intemperance.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1982-05" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1982-06" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1982-06 Session of First Presbyterian Church, Stanley, North Carolina v. Central Carolina, M10GA, p. 72" data-search-text="1982-06 Session of First Presbyterian Church, Stanley, North Carolina v. Central Carolina Presbytery The Session challenged Presbytery’s refusal to receive complaints and associated voting, executive-session, elder-emeritus, interpretive, and disciplinary actions. The General Assembly sustained items 1, 2, and 5, but not 3, 4, and 6. Receiving a complaint under BCO 43-1 was not subject to a vote; when heard, complainants and respondents could not participate. Executive session was permissible, an elder emeritus retained full privileges, and item 6 was improper in this court. No reason was given for item 5. Presbytery was instructed to receive and hear the complaints properly. complaint Partially sustained Not stated legacy 1982-6; Case #6; Minutes 6 BCO 43-1, BCO 39-2, BCO 11-3, BCO 27-5 complaint procedure judicial commission appointment presbytery actions executive session improper voting">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1982-06</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga10_1982__case6.html">Session of First Presbyterian Church, Stanley, North Carolina v. Central Carolina Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1982-06">The Session challenged Presbytery’s refusal to receive complaints and associated voting, executive-session, elder-emeritus, interpretive, and disciplinary actions. The General Assembly sustained items 1, 2, and 5, but not 3, 4, and 6. Receiving a complaint under BCO 43-1 was not subject to a vote; when heard, complainants and respondents could not participate. Executive session was permissible, an elder emeritus retained full privileges, and item 6 was improper in this court. No reason was given for item 5. Presbytery was instructed to receive and hear the complaints properly.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1982-06" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1981-03">A complaint challenged Presbytery&#x27;s one-year delay before accepting a petition to organize a mission congregation. Calvary, M8GA, p. 77" data-search-text="1980-03 Teaching Elders Byron Snapp and James M. Hope v. Calvary Presbytery Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The Assembly sustained the complaint’s single specification because Presbytery had not demonstrated either extraordinary circumstances or the man’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. Rather than answer the broader question about proper use of the clause, it ordered a report to the Ninth General Assembly. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 1980-3; Case #3; Minutes 3 BCO 22-4 ordination extraordinary clause ministerial examination Hebrew requirement">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1980-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case1.html">Teaching Elders Byron Snapp and James M. Hope v. Calvary Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1980-03">Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The Assembly sustained the complaint’s single specification because Presbytery had not demonstrated either extraordinary circumstances or the man’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. Rather than answer the broader question about proper use of the clause, it ordered a report to the Ninth General Assembly.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1980-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>
