<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1980-04" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1980-04 Bogue et al. v. of the Ascension" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1980-04: Bogue et al. v. of the Ascension, M8GA, pp. 52–96" data-search-text="1980-04 Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension Complainants challenged Presbytery&#x27;s sustaining of ordination trials for a candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate&#x27;s views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards&#x27; teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call&#x27;s omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate. complaint Sustained; Remanded Not stated legacy 1980-4; Case #5; Minutes 5 BCO 44-4, BCO 43-4, BCO 21-1, BCO 21-4, BCO 7-1, BCO 36-11, BCO 33-19, BCO 21-1.compliant doctrinal standards continuation of spiritual gifts revelation canon of Scripture Westminster Confession of Faith ordination trials campus ministry call ecclesiastical judicial procedure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1980-04</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga08_1980__case3.html">Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Sustained; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1980-04">Complainants challenged Presbytery&#x27;s sustaining of ordination trials for a candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate&#x27;s views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards&#x27; teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call&#x27;s omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1980-04" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Mid-Atlantic, M6GA, pp. 47–77" data-search-text="1978-01 James H. Campbell v. Mid-Atlantic Presbytery Ruling Elder James H. Campbell complained that Mid-Atlantic Presbytery approved a commission report finding charges against Rev. Robert Schoof inadmissible rather than proceeding on them. The General Assembly adopted the Committee on Judicial Business recommendation ordering Presbytery to hold a new hearing on the original charges under BCO 44-5, to conform to the BCO, and to keep the principals informed; it also appointed a judicial commission for any further complaint or appeal. The adopted report gives no further reasoning and does not expressly rule on the late-filing request. complaint Remanded Not reached legacy 1978-1 BCO 44-5 judicial process charges new hearing ministerial discipline notice and record">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1978-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga06_1978__case1.html">James H. <div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1978-01">Ruling Elder James H. Campbell complained that Mid-Atlantic Presbytery approved a commission report finding charges against Rev. Robert Schoof inadmissible rather than proceeding on them. The General Assembly adopted the Committee on Judicial Business recommendation ordering Presbytery to hold a new hearing on the original charges under BCO 44-5, to conform to the BCO, and to keep the principals informed; it also appointed a judicial commission for any further complaint or appeal. The adopted report gives no further reasoning and does not expressly rule on the late-filing request.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1978-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1978-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1978-02 Jr. et al. v. Tennessee Valley" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1978-02: Jr. et al. v. Tennessee Valley, M6GA, pp. 49–108" data-search-text="1978-02 Luther L. Allin Jr. et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery Session members challenged Presbytery’s order to hold a congregational meeting on officer rotation and its handling of the complaint hearing. The Judicial Commission held that ten days ran from the notice’s postmark and that Bristow and Pastor Vitullo could not participate as members of the reviewing court. It nevertheless upheld Presbytery’s authority to require the meeting: a sufficient petition left the Session no option to refuse, while the congregation retained authority to decide rotation. The complaint was sustained in part and remanded for a properly noticed hearing. complaint Partially sustained; Denied; Remanded Not stated legacy 1978-2 BCO 44-5, BCO 43-8, BCO 14-9, BCO 16-3, BCO 26-2, BCO 28-5, BCO 32-8, BCO 60-1, BCO 60-6, BCO 25-1 Session authority Congregational meetings Officer rotation Notice requirements Judicial procedures Conflicts of interest Parliamentary procedure">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1978-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga06_1978__case2.html">Luther L. Allin Jr. et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Partially sustained; Denied; Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1978-02">Session members challenged Presbytery’s order to hold a congregational meeting on officer rotation and its handling of the complaint hearing. The Judicial Commission held that ten days ran from the notice’s postmark and that Bristow and Pastor Vitullo could not participate as members of the reviewing court. It nevertheless upheld Presbytery’s authority to require the meeting: a sufficient petition left the Session no option to refuse, while the congregation retained authority to decide rotation. The complaint was sustained in part and remanded for a properly noticed hearing.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1978-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<section class="judicial-year" data-judicial-year="1977"><h2>1977</h2>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1977-01" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1977-01 Karlberg and Luce v. Central Georgia" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1977-01: Karlberg and Luce v. Central Georgia, M5GA, pp. 53–55" data-search-text="1977-01 Rev. Paul L. Karlberg and Ruling Elder James G. Luce v. Central Georgia Presbytery Complainants Karlberg and Luce challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s commission as biased—it heard the Faith Church minority but not the majority—and challenged its judicial designation and recommendations. After Presbytery rescinded recommendations 2–6, complainants dropped those reasons, leaving only the bias claim. A General Assembly judicial commission heard both sides and unanimously declined to sustain. It reasoned both parties acted in good faith, mistakes were inadvertent, and remand would not further Christ’s cause. The rescinded recommendations and designation were not adjudicated. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 1977-1; Minutes 5-13, 5-87 None listed ">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1977-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case1.html">Rev. Paul L. Karlberg and Ruling Elder James G. Luce v. Central Georgia Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1977-01">Complainants Karlberg and Luce challenged Central Georgia Presbytery’s commission as biased—it heard the Faith Church minority but not the majority—and challenged its judicial designation and recommendations. After Presbytery rescinded recommendations 2–6, complainants dropped those reasons, leaving only the bias claim. A General Assembly judicial commission heard both sides and unanimously declined to sustain. It reasoned both parties acted in good faith, mistakes were inadvertent, and remand would not further Christ’s cause. The rescinded recommendations and designation were not adjudicated.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1977-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1977-03" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1977-03 Barnes et al. v. Evangel" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1977-03: Barnes et al. v. Evangel, M5GA, pp. 59–89" data-search-text="1977-03 Rev. Thomas Barnes et al. v. Evangel Presbytery The Fifth General Assembly approved its Judicial Commission’s refusal to sustain a complaint challenging Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without a call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. No reason for rejecting the complaint was stated. The ruling nevertheless required Presbytery to have—and itself issue—a written call before implementing the ordination decision, and requested referral of the broader question defining a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 1977-3; Minutes 5-15, 5-83 BCO 2-2, BCO 8-7, BCO 18-1, BCO 22-3 call to ministry ordination evangelist parachurch ministry labor out of bounds">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1977-03</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga05_1977__case3.html">Rev. Thomas Barnes et al. v. Evangel Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1977-03">The Fifth General Assembly approved its Judicial Commission’s refusal to sustain a complaint challenging Presbytery’s approval of Mercer for ordination as an evangelist without a call and for parachurch work outside its bounds. No reason for rejecting the complaint was stated. The ruling nevertheless required Presbytery to have—and itself issue—a written call before implementing the ordination decision, and requested referral of the broader question defining a valid ministerial call to the Permanent Committee on Judicial Business.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1977-03" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Covenant, M4GA, pp. 53–72" data-search-text="1976-01 Session of Eastland Presbyterian Church, Memphis, Tennessee v. Covenant Presbytery A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving the summer employment of a divorced and remarried man in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid, holding that McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. It expressly did not decide whether such employment would violate the Constitution. The General Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment, leaving the presbytery&#x27;s action undisturbed. complaint Not sustained Not stated legacy 1976-1; Minutes 4-13 None listed ministerial employment jurisdiction complaint validity">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1976-01</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga04_1976__case2.html">Session of Eastland Presbyterian Church, Memphis, Tennessee v. Covenant Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Not sustained</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1976-01">A session complained that Covenant Presbytery violated PCA standards by approving the summer employment of a divorced and remarried man in a ministerial capacity. The Judicial Commission found the complaint invalid, holding that McKeown was not employed in a ministerial capacity. It expressly did not decide whether such employment would violate the Constitution. The General Assembly adopted the report as its action and judgment, leaving the presbytery&#x27;s action undisturbed.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1976-01" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

<article class="judicial-case" id="case-1976-02" data-judicial-record data-judicial-short-citation="1976-02 Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace" data-judicial-full-citation="Case 1976-02: Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace, M4GA, pp. 52–72" data-search-text="1976-02 Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace Presbytery Trinity Church complained that Grace Presbytery&#x27;s July 9, 1976 substitute motion, delaying Adrian Pater&#x27;s ordination until he was called to PCA work, was an out-of-order reconsideration. The Judicial Commission did not reach the merits: because the BCO 43-5 record was not complied with and minutes were inadequate, it returned the whole matter to the lower court for a new hearing. The Assembly accepted that judgment and separately adopted, 238–131, a recommendation that the BCO does not envisage ordination expressly for pastoral service in another denomination. complaint Remanded Not reached legacy 1976-2; Minutes 4-12 BCO 18-3, BCO 21-1, BCO 22-4, BCO 43-5 ordination ministerial examination call to ministry out of bounds labor procedural order">
<header class="judicial-case__header"><p class="judicial-case__docket"><code>1976-02</code> <span>· Complaint</span><span class="judicial-saved-state" data-judicial-saved hidden> · Saved</span></p><h3><a href="/pca-ga/cases/ga04_1976__case1.html">Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace Presbytery</a></h3></header>
<p class="judicial-case__outcome"><span>Outcome</span> Remanded</p>
<div class="judicial-case__layout">
<div class="judicial-case__content">
<div class="judicial-case__summary-wrap"><p class="judicial-case__summary" id="judicial-summary-1976-02">Trinity Church complained that Grace Presbytery&#x27;s July 9, 1976 substitute motion, delaying Adrian Pater&#x27;s ordination until he was called to PCA work, was an out-of-order reconsideration. The Judicial Commission did not reach the merits: because the BCO 43-5 record was not complied with and minutes were inadequate, it returned the whole matter to the lower court for a new hearing. The Assembly accepted that judgment and separately adopted, 238–131, a recommendation that the BCO does not envisage ordination expressly for pastoral service in another denomination.</p><button type="button" class="judicial-case__summary-toggle" aria-controls="judicial-summary-1976-02" aria-expanded="false" hidden>Show full synopsis</button></div>

Pacific, M3GA, pp. 50–88" data-search-text="1975-01 Rev. Harold L. Webb &amp; Rev. Thomas Miller v. Pacific Presbytery Ministers complained that Pacific Presbytery conducted nonroutine business without the constitutionally required quorum of three teaching and three ruling elders. The Assembly agreed that the August 4, 1975 actions were irregular, but dismissed the complaint because Presbytery later met with a quorum and ratified those actions. The dismissal therefore reflected correction of the defect, not approval of proceeding without a quorum. complaint Dismissed Not reached legacy 1975-1; Minutes 3-12 BCO 14-4 quorum requirement presbytery competence constitutional violation judicial complaint ratification of actions">
